v4.slots: SLOTS (added 2026-07-26, owner request). Any layer whose code counterpart is React.ReactNode should be a slot, so a designer can drop in an Avatar / StatusDot / icon button without detaching. Recipe: key = master.addComponentProperty("<bem-name>", "SLOT", "") then node.componentPropertyReferences = {...existingRefs, slotContentId: key}. THE REFERENCE KEY IS `slotContentId` — it is in none of the official skill docs, which list only characters/visible/mainComponent. Wiring it CONVERTS the frame into a real SLOT node in place: same node id, default content kept, other bindings (e.g. visible) kept, layout sizing kept — but the node is RENAMED to the property name, so name the property with the BEM class to keep layer names mapped to CSS. There is no figma.createSlot(); wiring the reference is the only programmatic path. clone() preserves slots.
v4.slotPolicy: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-26: forward-only plus high-value backfill. Every NEW page slots any layer whose code counterpart is React.ReactNode. Backfill was scoped to the compound families that designers actually compose with — Item, Field, InputGroup, Attachment — of which only InputGroup was already shipped, so the backfill was that one page. Item, Field and Attachment are still in the Phase 3 queue and get slots natively. The simpler shipped atoms keep their baked content deliberately; do NOT sweep them.

Append means the end. NOTE THE DELIBERATE MISMATCH WITH STORYBOOK: parameters.ui.changelog is NEWEST first (CLAUDE.md), because that page renders a list a developer scans from the top. Do not "fix" either one to match the other.

lessons: Instances cannot receive appendChild — masters must pre-provision max children; hide extras per-instance (visible=false).
createAutoLayout defaults clipsContent=true — unclip rows/cells or focus rings get cut.
Focus/* drop shadows need showShadowBehindNode=false or they darken translucent fills (matches CSS box-shadow clipping).
REST get_screenshot serves stale renders for MODIFIED nodes but is fine for freshly created nodes; node.exportAsync is always live but base64 results >20kb get truncated in tool output.
On horizontal auto-layout, counterAxisSizingMode=FIXED freezes HEIGHT (text clips on wrap) — use primaryAxisSizingMode=FIXED + counterAxisSizingMode=AUTO for fixed-width/hug-height rows.
A COMPONENT_SET can be appendChild-ed into an auto-layout frame (Overview nests the Button set).
Component sets must bind brand fills to the THEME collection vars, NOT Mode brand/main/* — otherwise theme modes don't flip them. Ghost text stays color/secondary-foreground (neutral carve-out).
figma.root.name is read-only — file rename must be manual.
Code Connect blocked: needs Dev/Full seat on Org/Enterprise plan.
Load Inter Regular/Medium/Semi Bold/Bold + JetBrains Mono before any text op.
use_figma scripts are ATOMIC — one thrown error rolls back everything the script did, including work on unrelated pages. Build one component page per script so a typo costs one page, not four.

Setting any property a text style owns (letterSpacing, fontSize, lineHeight) DETACHES textStyleId and trips the lint. If the design needs a value no style carries, create the style — 'xs/leading-none/Mono' (12), 'sm/leading-none/Mono' (14) and 'xs/leading-normal/Medium Wide' (--tracking-wide) were added this way.

A gradient overlay used to fake an un-bindable effect (Skeleton's shimmer) must be full-bleed with STRETCH constraints. A narrower band leaves its own rect edge visible wherever the parent clips to a radius.
Component-SET wrappers need their padding and corner radius bound too — Figma gives new sets a default radius of 5, which the lint flags. Bind to spacing/* and radius/lg.
_Doc/ChangelogRow's master had unbound 8px top/bottom padding (now bound to spacing/2). When the lint flags a _Doc instance, fix the MASTER — it clears every page at once, past and future.
Re-applying a text style RESETS the properties it owns — setTextStyleIdAsync is the fix for an accidental detach, not just the initial assignment.

Cloning a variant (component.clone()) preserves EVERY binding — variable-bound fills/strokes/radii, effect styles, and boolean-bound child visibility. Button/Icon-only was built by cloning all 120 labelled variants and editing three things, which is far safer than rebuilding and is the right move whenever a new set is a systematic transform of an existing one. Read the per-variant colour binding off the node you are about to delete (the label) and re-apply it to its replacement.

Figma TRIMS whitespace at the edge of a TEXT node when it hugs, so a line of code split into per-token spans renders as 'exportfunctionSidebar'. Use non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) for every space inside multi-span text — same width in a mono face, never trimmed. Applies to any run of coloured spans laid out in a horizontal auto-layout.

Figma will NOT let you override vector geometry inside an instance ('This property cannot be overridden in an instance'). Any component with a swappable glyph therefore needs the icon to be an INSTANCE of an icon component plus an INSTANCE_SWAP property — a drawn glyph locks every instance to it. Colour and stroke weight ARE overridable; geometry is not.

Set layoutSizing AFTER parenting. Sizing modes assigned before appendChild get reset by the new parent's auto-layout — a card built with primaryAxisSizingMode='AUTO' then appended arrived stuck at its placeholder 10px height and its children spilled over the following siblings.

NEVER pipe bulk asset data through the conversation. 1,746 lucide icons are ~353 KB of markup; batching it through use_figma scripts would have cost six figures of tokens. Instead: generate ONE SVG locally with each icon wrapped in <g id='{name}'>, call upload_assets for a submitUrl, POST it with curl, then convert the imported tree in-place. Figma keeps the group ids as layer names, which is the whole mapping. Imported SVG groups hug their glyph bounds, so wrap each in a 24x24 frame and offset the group by (groupXY - cellXY) to restore a uniform box.

Third-party icon sets imported from Figma community files are a trap for THIS project: the library's first hard rule is that lucide-react is the only runtime dependency, so a Hugeicons/Phosphor/Tabler glyph in Figma is unbuildable. It is also a licensing hazard — MIT and Apache-2.0 both require the copyright notice to be retained, and paid tiers (Hugeicons Pro) and template vendors (shadcncraft) carry their own notices. Generate from node_modules instead; provenance and buildability come free.

Icon stroke weight does NOT scale when you resize an instance in Figma, but it DOES scale in the browser, because SVG stroke-width is in viewBox units. A 24px master at stroke 2 placed at 12px must be set to 1.0 by hand. Measure the real value in the browser (computedStrokeWidth x renderedSize / viewBoxSize) rather than assuming.

instance.swapComponent() DISCARDS overrides whose layer names don't match the new component. Give every member of a swappable family identical inner layer names, or every swap silently resets colour and stroke.

An INSTANCE_SWAP property swap DISCARDS nested overrides — uniform layer names do NOT save you (that only helps manual swapComponent in limited cases). Anything that must survive a swap has to come from a VARIABLE MODE set on an ancestor, because modes cascade and are not overrides. Verify on a real placed-and-swapped instance, never on the master: the master can look perfectly correct while every real usage is wrong.

Typing a raw value over a variable-bound property in the Figma UI silently DETACHES the binding. After any hand-edit to a variable-driven system, re-check bindings before assuming the system still holds — count bound vs unbound, don't eyeball.

Before inventing a Figma variable, check whether the number already exists as a token. icon/stroke-weight's 24/16/12 modes turned out to equal icon-border-width/lg, /default and /sm exactly, so they alias the Primitives rather than duplicating the values. Aliasing keeps one source of truth; duplicating creates two that drift.

Two ways to change a nested icon behave differently: the INSTANCE_SWAP property keeps the child's variable bindings, while selecting the nested instance and swapping it directly drops them. Test both paths — designers will use whichever the right-hand panel makes easiest.

Do not infer a mechanism's behaviour from nodes you have already mutated by another route. I concluded 'INSTANCE_SWAP discards overrides' from instances my own swapComponent() pass had broken, and reported a non-existent limitation. Reproduce on a FRESH instance created from the current master before naming a root cause.

A per-layer override only reaches layers present on the component's DEFAULT swap target. If a swappable family has varying inner layer counts, anything set as an override will be applied partially — the visible symptom is an icon rendering half in one colour and half in another. Normalise the family to a single, uniformly-named layer instead.

Merge vector geometry at the NODE level (concatenate vectorPaths entries), never by string-joining path `d` data. String-joining silently breaks any sub-path that begins with a relative moveto — it resolves against the previous path's endpoint instead of the origin. That corrupted 551 of 1,746 icons on an earlier attempt.

Figma caps a variable collection at 10 modes. Anything needing more distinct cascading values (13 icon colours here) cannot use the mode mechanism at all — check the count before designing around modes.

figma.flatten() merges vectors correctly (it respects each node's local transform); concatenating vectorPaths by hand does NOT — path data is in each node's own coordinate space, so merging discards every other node's offset and collapses the geometry. That corrupted all 1,746 icons and required a full rebuild from the source SVG. If a bulk geometry operation exists as a Figma built-in, use it.

Verify a destructive bulk operation on ONE duplicated node and screenshot it BEFORE running it across a library. Counts and property reads looked perfect after the bad merge ('1 path, stroke kept, 24x24') while every glyph was visually destroyed. Numbers are not verification for geometry — pixels are.

When a component's shape comes from a CHILD layer's radius, a stroke or ring applied to the ROOT will follow the root's (square) geometry instead. Mirror the radius onto every layer the CSS sets it on — Avatar's CSS applies it to both the root and the inner clip layer, and modelling only the inner produced square rings around circular avatars.

A pinned CSS stroke-width on an SVG icon is in VIEWBOX units, not rendered pixels — pinning '1.33px' on a 12px icon renders 0.665px. If a token's value is meant as a rendered width, it only matches at the size where viewBox and box coincide. Usually the right move is to NOT pin it and let lucide's own 2 units scale.

Check hit targets, not just visuals: measure getBoundingClientRect against WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24. A control can look right and be untappable. Where the drawn box must stay small, expand the target with a transparent ::after rather than resizing.

node.targetAspectRatio is READ-ONLY to plugins — an aspect-ratio constraint can only be set in the Figma UI. When a component's whole point is a constraint the API cannot express, size the frames correctly and flag the manual toggle on the page rather than leaving a silent gap.

When a prop is CONTINUOUS (a number) rather than a union, a Figma variant axis cannot be faithful. Model representative values and say plainly in the set description that they are a shortcut, not the API — otherwise a designer reads six options as the whole surface.

Use neutral, invented placeholder copy in design-system demos — not real people's quotations or names. A component library's demo content gets copied into product mockups, and a real attribution reads as endorsement. Blockquote's first draft used a real person's aphorism; replaced with invented copy and a fictional reviewer.

Hiding a native scrollbar transfers all of its accessibility to you. ScrollArea set scrollbar-width:none and drew its own thumb, which meant the missing tabIndex had no fallback at all — and its hover-reveal could never trigger for keyboard users because :focus-within had nothing to match. If a component takes over a native affordance, audit what the browser was doing for free before shipping it.

An audit note is only as good as its list. CLAUDE.md claimed component SCSS was fully tokenized and enumerated what had been checked (durations, easings, border-widths, focus-rings). Opacity was not on that list and five raw literals were sitting in four components with --o-* already defined. Enumerate token CATEGORIES from tokens.scss and grep for a raw literal of each, rather than trusting a prose summary.

When two components share an interaction shape and differ only in emphasis (Chip vs Toggle: both aria-pressed, one brand one neutral), the doc page's job is the DECISION RULE, not the pixel diff. 'Does the on-state change what data is shown, or how a tool behaves?' is what a designer actually needs; a side-by-side of the two fills is not.

RESOLVED 2026-07-26 — the repo was importing 13 DEPRECATED lucide aliases, which the Figma icon set (built from canonical names only) does not contain, so a designer searching the swap list for 'align-left' found nothing. Detection is mechanical, not guesswork: in lucide-react/dist/esm/icons an ALIAS module is a bare `export { default } from './canonical.mjs'` re-export, while a canonical module calls createLucideIcon. Migrated all 13: AlignLeft->TextAlignStart, AlignCenter->TextAlignCenter, AlignRight->TextAlignEnd, AlertCircle->CircleAlert, AlertTriangle->TriangleAlert, XCircle->CircleX, CheckCircle2->CircleCheck, MoreHorizontal->Ellipsis, FileVideo->FilePlay, FileWarning->FileExclamationPoint, FileJson->FileBraces, BarChart3->ChartColumn, Home->House. Two were in SHIPPED source (Breadcrumb.tsx, Pagination.tsx), the rest in stories/prototypes. Re-run the alias check after any lucide upgrade — today's canonical name is tomorrow's alias.

figma appendChild() returns VOID, not the appended child. `parent.appendChild(x).layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL'` throws 'cannot set property of null' and — because scripts are atomic — rolls the whole page back. Use an add(parent,node,fill) helper that appends, optionally sets sizing, and returns the node.
layoutWrap='WRAP' can only be set AFTER layoutMode='HORIZONTAL'. Setting it on a frame that is still VERTICAL throws.

The overflow check must be RECURSIVE. Comparing only the top-level frames' direct children passed clean while both example bars sat collapsed at 100px with their contents spilling — the bug was one level deeper. Walk every auto-layout frame against its own children (skipping layoutPositioning==='ABSOLUTE').

Figma paints later siblings on top, exactly like the DOM — so a CSS z-index lift CANNOT be shown by applying a focus effect to a middle child. The neighbour that follows it covers the ring and the canvas silently documents the BUG rather than the fix. Draw the ring as an absolutely-positioned rect appended last instead.

When a code example puts several parts inside ONE container, model it in Figma as ONE run with corners assigned by GLOBAL position. Composing it from sub-groups restarts the first/last logic and produces rounded corners in the middle of a control: ButtonGroup's toolbar shipped with Copy rounded on its right and Paste rounded on both sides, and the 'Sort by' cell as a free-floating pill, because each sub-group thought it had its own first and last child. The CSS runs :not(:first-child)/:not(:last-child) across ALL the group's children — text cells and separators included. Read the real borderRadius per child out of the browser and match it literally. Where a run must break (a full-width separator), nest the collapsed run inside a spacing-0 outer row rather than restarting the corner logic.

A frame with clipsContent:true HIDES its own overflow from absoluteBoundingBox — the box comes back clipped, so a bounding-box overflow check reports clean while content is visibly cut off (Card's 150px footer clipped its Cancel button). Add a CONTENT check alongside the box check: sum the children's widths/heights plus gaps and padding and compare against the frame, skipping layoutWrap==='WRAP' frames.

primaryAxisAlignItems='SPACE_BETWEEN' makes Figma IGNORE itemSpacing, so a FILL child absorbs the gap. CSS does not work that way — `justify-content: space-between` and `gap` both apply. Card's header gave its title 16px more width than the browser until the align was changed to MIN (the FILL child already grows, so MIN reproduces the CSS exactly). Whenever a frame has both a FILL child and SPACE_BETWEEN, check the numbers against the browser.

Figma SLOTS are reachable from the plugin API even though nothing documents them: addComponentProperty(name,'SLOT','') then node.componentPropertyReferences={slotContentId:key}. The key `slotContentId` is undocumented — the official component-creation reference lists only characters/visible/mainComponent, and every guess (slot, slotContent, content, children) is rejected as an unrecognized key. I only found it by having the owner convert ONE layer in the UI and reading back its componentPropertyReferences. Lesson: when an API looks unavailable, have the user perform the action once in the UI and inspect the result, rather than concluding it cannot be done.

Slot vs TEXT vs INSTANCE_SWAP: a slot is right when the code prop is React.ReactNode AND the content is genuinely open (an avatar, a status dot, an icon button). A short string is still better as a TEXT property — InputGroup/Button keeps Label on its 8 labelled variants and slots only the 8 icon-only ones. Slots and text properties coexist: a slot preserves its default content, so a TEXT-bound node living inside a slot keeps working (Card's Body does exactly this).

preferredValues AND description are both writable on a SLOT property via editComponentProperty(key,{preferredValues,description}) — accepting {type:'COMPONENT_SET'|'COMPONENT', key}. They are suggestions surfaced at the top of the picker, not a whitelist, so listing a handful costs nothing and guides the designer.

A Figma slot can quietly outrun the code. Exposing a WHOLE region as one free slot lets a designer compose things the component has no prop for — Card's header has no leading position at all, so a featured icon was undrawable in code while being trivial in Figma. Prefer NAMED slots that map 1:1 to real props; if the design need is real, add the prop to the code first and mirror it, which is what CardHeader's `media` was.

Converting a frame to a SLOT STRIPS componentPropertyReferences from its children and hides them. Item's header/footer labels lost their `characters` binding and went invisible, leaving two orphan TEXT properties. Slot default content is treated as placeholder, so do NOT expect a text property to survive inside a newly-converted slot — bind text BEFORE deciding, or (better) accept that a ReactNode region should not have a text prop at all.

A freshly-converted SLOT holds a stale explicit height (100px) and REPORTS layoutSizingVertical:'HUG' while ignoring it. Setting HUG alone does nothing; call resize(w, contentHeight) first to clear the explicit size, then set HUG and it sticks. Symptom is a 100px empty band where a 16px line should be.

The overflow check must skip hidden children. A node hidden by a boolean keeps a STALE absoluteBoundingBox, which reported 18 phantom overflows on Item. Filter c.visible !== false alongside the ABSOLUTE-positioning filter.

A SLOT's sublayers CANNOT hold componentPropertyReferences — Figma throws 'Cannot set component property references on slot sublayer'. So a region is either a slot OR has text properties inside it, never both. Attachment's content stayed a plain frame for exactly this reason, keeping Title/Description as text props. Oddly, a binding that existed BEFORE conversion can survive (Card's Body does, verified) while Item's labels were stripped — treat survival as unreliable and re-check after every conversion.

findAll() does NOT traverse into component-set variants, but findAllWithCriteria() DOES. A health check written with findAll reported 'wired 0' for slots that were in fact wired across all 6 variants. Use findAllWithCriteria for anything inside a set.

The auto-layout sizing axes FLIP with layoutMode, and it bites twice: on HORIZONTAL, primary=width and counter=height; on VERTICAL it is the reverse. Applying the same FIXED/AUTO pair to both orientations gave Attachment's vertical variants a frozen 100px height and a hugging width — the exact inverse of the intent. Set the axes per orientation.

layoutAlign='MAX' silently does not stick on an auto-layout child (stays INHERIT); the parent's counterAxisAlignItems wins. To reproduce CSS align-self:flex-end, make the child FILL the width and set its own primaryAxisAlignItems='MAX'.

CloseButton hard-codes an <X> — it is a close button, not an icon-button primitive, and its two variants differ only in hover background. Splitting them would yield two close buttons. When a component looks like it should be shared but its icon is fixed, the reusable thing is the SHELL underneath, not the component: `.ui-icon-button` in src/styles/icon-button.scss now carries the box, hover tint, focus ring, disabled state and hit-target expansion for CloseButton, AttachmentAction and the Chat composer tools.

Instance sublayers cannot be removed — figma throws 'Node with id I…;… not found' on remove(). To change what is inside an instance you need a slot, a boolean-bound visibility, or an INSTANCE_SWAP; there is no deleting.

Do NOT read a transitioned property immediately after toggling a class — getComputedStyle returns the pre-transition value and it looks like a specificity bug. Chat's recording colour read as muted right after the class change and settled to --error 300ms later. Wait out the transition before measuring.

A grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr disclosure needs THREE layers, and the third is not optional: grid / clip / body. Collapsible shipped with two, so the consumer's className landed on the clip context and 16px of padding left a 32px phantom gap when closed. The tell that it was real rather than theoretical: both internal consumers had already added their own third div to work around it. When two consumers independently work around the same thing, the component is missing it.

A HORIZONTAL wrap frame (examples bar) with counterAxisSizingMode='FIXED' freezes its HEIGHT, so cells taller than the frozen height overflow vertically — the inverse of the width case. For a wrap row that must grow to its tallest cell, counterAxisSizingMode must be 'AUTO' (hug height). Also: a fixed-width TEXT node inside a padded root overflows when the root is resized narrower than textWidth + padding — cap the text below the narrowest root you will use.

First reuse of the aiden dark-overlay pattern outside Button. A gradient fill (GRADIENT_LINEAR) is NOT caught by the unbound-solid-fill lint — only SOLID fills without a bound variable are. So the aiden light gradient (literal stops, un-bindable) passes clean, but a literal-hex SOLID indicator does NOT — the success example bar used #047857 and got flagged until bound to --success. Draw semantic bars with the bound variable; only the aiden gradient gets literal stops.

The 'clear stale slot heights with layoutSizingVertical=HUG' trick is safe ONLY when the slot holds an instance (which carries its own size). When a slot holds DRAWN content with a deliberate aspect (Empty's 48x48 icon tile), HUG collapses one axis to the content and distorts it. Empty's tile rendered 48x32 until the height was re-fixed. Check what a slot contains before hugging it.

After extracting a shared primitive (FeaturedIcon), sweep for slots it should fill: add it to the preferredValues of any leading-visual slot where it fits (Empty media, Card header-media) and update the 'Uses inside' pills + slot descriptions. NOT every media slot — Item/Attachment media are the compact list-tile pattern and deliberately do NOT suggest FeaturedIcon. Record future homes (Dialog/AlertDialog/ChatGreeting) so the wiring happens when they're built.

Compound components (Breadcrumb) must be modelled as instanceable ATOMS, not one fixed hand-drawn composition. First cut built Breadcrumb as a single component locked to one trail with no text props/slots — so every example had to be hand-rebuilt from raw frames and drifted from the master. The owner caught it: 'why aren't you using the actual component in the examples?' Fix: expose the reusable parts as components (Crumb with Type variant + Label text prop, Separator with Glyph variant, Ellipsis) and COMPOSE every trail — overview, spec, examples — from real instances. Rule: if a doc page's examples are hand-drawn rather than instances, the component is under-modelled. Applies to every compound family (Breadcrumb/Chat/etc.).

A component that WRAPS another control (Field) is modelled with a Figma SLOT for the control (default content = a real control instance), so examples compose real instances. Two gotchas: (1) if the wrapped control has its OWN label (Input's 'Show label' defaults true), turn it off or it doubles the wrapper's label. (2) Filling a slot on an INSTANCE is append-not-replace: slot.appendChild(newControl) leaves the master's default content visible, so hide slot.children[0] first. Also: resize() on an auto-layout frame freezes BOTH axes to FIXED — re-assert the hug axis AFTER any resize().

A rotated node's .x/.y is NOT its visual top-left — Figma's rotation origin shifts it, so positioning a rotated shape (a tooltip/popover arrow) by x/y math lands it wrong (the tooltip top arrow ended ~4px inside the bubble and was invisible). Position it in two passes: set an approximate x/y, read the node's absoluteBoundingBox to get its TRUE rendered center, then add (targetCenter - currentCenter) to x/y. Use a plain square (cornerRadius 0) for the arrow — a same-colour diamond centered on the bubble edge reads as a clean triangle; a rounded corner makes it a pentagon. Applies to every Overlay arrow ahead (Popover / HoverCard / DropdownMenu / Select / Combobox).

resize() on an auto-layout frame freezes BOTH sizing axes to FIXED — this has now bitten on Field, Dialog panels AND the Dialog scrim stage. Standing rule: after ANY resize() on an auto-layout node, re-assert the axis that should hug (primaryAxisSizingMode/counterAxisSizingMode='AUTO'); better, avoid resize entirely — append the frame to its parent, then set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' (or a width via the parent) and the hug axis to AUTO. A frozen axis shows as a 10px-tall strip with content spilling.

A Figma SLOT whose default content is MULTIPLE loose nodes is unswappable: hiding one default child re-renders the slot and invalidates the OTHER defaults' node refs, so the next .visible read throws 'node not found' — even iterating slot.children with .find throws on the stale node. Two rules: (1) give a swappable slot a SINGLE wrapper frame as its default content, not loose siblings; (2) hide that wrapper BEFORE appending the replacement (a ref grabbed before an append goes stale after it). Dialog/Field slots worked only because each had exactly one default child.

Command page: setProperties on a standalone COMPONENT (not just a set) still needs the FULL property key with the #id suffix (e.g. 'Label#588:24'), not the bare name — the bare name throws 'Could not find a component property'. Variant props use the bare axis name ('State'); TEXT/BOOL props always use name#id.

Toast page: composing real component INSTANCES inside a new atom is the cleanest path for cards that wrap other components (Button/CloseButton/Progress). Instances are skipped by lint. To customize a nested composed component (e.g. a Button's label, or swap an icon), reach into the OUTER instance with findOne by the layer name you set at build time and setProperties/swapComponent on it — the wrapping atom need not re-expose every inner prop. After swapComponent on an icon, re-bind its stroke to the desired color var (the swap discards the binding).

Atom master components must live NESTED inside a page frame (the convention: an 'Overview > … > parts' frame), NOT as loose top-level canvas components. Building a master with figma.createComponent()/combineAsVariants() places it at the page root; if you then only instance it in the frames, the master itself is left stranded on the canvas (looks like stray orphan components far below). Fix: append the master(s) into a labeled 'parts' frame inside the Overview. Instances elsewhere stay valid — an instance references its master by id regardless of where the master lives. (Hit on Command + Toast; caught by visual review of the page canvas, not by lint.)

Provider/hook components with no visual atom (Direction; later maybe others) get a CONCEPT page, not a component-set page: keep the 3-frame shape but swap the middle 'Spec' for a mechanism/behaviour demo, and DROP the 'component master' section (there's nothing to nest). Figma has NO live RTL auto-layout — to illustrate dir='rtl' you hand-arrange token-bound primitives (reverse child order, text-align right, swap directional icons); caption it as 'the rendered DOM' so it's clearly an illustration, not a live mirror.

Don't hand-draw a sub-part that has its own code component (e.g. the sidebar search = SidebarInput, a distinct export from Input). Make it an instanceable atom and compose it. For 'flexibility via slots' on an assembled template, the lightest idiomatic Figma path is show/hide BOOLEAN props on regions (wire a child's `visible` to the prop) + relying on the atom instances for real composition — full INSTANCE_SWAP region slots are heavier and usually unnecessary for variable-length content like a menu list.

Figma has NO arbitrary-children slot: you cannot add/remove layers inside a locked COMPONENT instance (instance-swap only swaps one nested instance for one component). So an assembled 'template' whose list must be extendable (a sidebar menu, a nav, a form) should be a plain FRAME, not a component. Build it by detachInstance()-ing an instance of an assembled component — the outer becomes an editable frame while nested atom INSTANCES stay linked, giving an open auto-layout you copy and extend. detachInstance() preserves variable bindings (lint stays clean). Keep the ATOMS as the linked components; the assembly is a copyable template.

When restructuring a frame from HORIZONTAL to VERTICAL (or vice-versa), CLEAR stale layoutGrow / layoutSizing on its children — a child that was FILL on the old main axis keeps layoutGrow=1, which now grows/collapses it on the NEW main axis (a label collapsed to 1px tall). Also: a container built FIXED-height + clipsContent will clip newly-added children; set primaryAxisSizingMode='AUTO' to hug. Caught only by eyeballing the render, not by lint.

Figma plugin: findOne(cb) walks ALL descendants incl. freshly-created icon-instance internals, and a broken nested proxy node's .name getter can CRASH the callback ('Node with id ... not found'). When editing inside variant components, navigate by DIRECT children (comp.children.find(...)) instead of findOne to avoid descending into instances.

Figma: a nested component instance can be EXPOSED (instance.isExposedInstance===true) so its properties show on the parent in the UI, but those props are NOT merged into the parent's setProperties map — they stay keyed to the nested instance. To set them via API, find the nested instance and setProperties on IT (or drill in via the UI).

Page PROSE drifts silently and nothing catches it. The design-check lint validates bindings, names and styles — not whether a sentence is still true. HoverCard sat for two days documenting role="tooltip" and "non-interactive" after the code moved to role="dialog" and made the card keyboard-enterable, which would have led anyone building from the page to reproduce an invalid pattern. Diff prose against source whenever a role, aria relationship, prop or keyboard behaviour changes.

Before deleting a page, resolve every instance in the file to its main component — do NOT infer safety from a scan of the page you are deleting. A first pass here "proved" the legacy masters were unused by scanning a page that had no components on it, which proves nothing. The real check walked 8,533 instances on the other 73 pages and confirmed none resolved to the 23 doomed components.

Size vocabulary standardised in CODE on 2026-07-30 to xs/sm/default/lg — both the prop and the emitted class (ui-button--sz-sm). FIGMA IS DELIBERATELY BEHIND: the Button (120 variants), Button/Icon-only (120) and Chip (6) sets still carry title-case spelled-out Size options (XSmall|Small|Default|Large). Renaming them is a named follow-up — use the variant-property rename API, never delete-and-recreate, and rehearse on Chip first: done wrong it detaches every instance variant selection file-wide. Nothing programmatic breaks meanwhile; Code Connect is blocked on a paid seat so the coupling is prose only.

Figma: resize() on an instance does NOT scale cornerRadius or children — a 28.8px radius on a 24px square renders a circle with the glyph clipped. Use node.rescale(factor) for proportional scaling, and set child constraints to SCALE so manual handle-drags behave the same.

Figma: setting textAutoResize="HEIGHT" BEFORE resize(w, h) pins the height at h — every wrapping paragraph silently collapsed to 10px and overflowed its box. Order is: set width, THEN set textAutoResize="HEIGHT" so it recomputes. Re-applying NONE→HEIGHT repairs an already-collapsed node.

Figma: node.screenshot() defaults to contentsOnly:true, so shooting a backing frame that merely SITS BEHIND a sibling returns an empty rectangle. Either pass contentsOnly:false or put the background on the node itself.

Figma: copying one variant layer stack across a set to unify effects also carries its GLYPH. Five marks silently ended up with the same icon, and the variant names truncated at the same time. After any cross-variant paste, re-check both the icon content and the variant property values.

Figma: addComponentProperty(name, "INSTANCE_SWAP", value) rejects a component KEY and accepts the component NODE ID, despite the docs implying key. Probe with a throwaway component before committing to either.

Figma: a set-level INSTANCE_SWAP property has a single default across all variants, so binding a per-variant nested instance to it overwrites every variant with that one default. If each variant needs its own nested component, leave it an unbound nested instance — still swappable by selecting it — and skip the property.

Figma: page children paint back-to-front, so inserting a backing panel at a later index than existing nodes hides them. Same trap as the bloom-over-glyph z-order; appendChild the content after the panel.

Colour: white (#ffffff) clears WCAG AA 4.5:1 at L* <= 49.89, for EVERY hue at ANY chroma. Contrast measures luminance, so hue and saturation are nearly free and the lightness is the whole constraint. A flat L* 50 measures 4.48 and FAILS — the ceiling is 49.9, not 50. Chroma cannot buy the difference back: pushing db to the gamut edge gained 1.2 L*, the largest gain available anywhere on the wheel.

Colour: sRGB hue determines how far a brand's mark middle stop has to fall to carry a white label. Measured against #ffffff the seven POC brands read db 4.71 (already passing), ec/rm 3.95, ph 3.66, aiden 3.64, nb 3.25, dc 3.15 — so blue needs no move and the bright greens/teals need ~9-10 L*. This is why a single global --primary-foreground cannot serve a hue-spread brand set.

Figma: setBoundVariableForPaint binds the RAW variable value, so binding a derived colour (a 40% border tint, a 6% surface tint) to the base variable silently paints the base at full strength. Bind only the properties that are literally the variable; leave derived tints static and say so on the canvas, or the reader assumes the whole card is live.

Figma: the POC page carries '07 · White-label study' (node 851:426) — the Storybook MinimalOption A/B rebuilt for colour tweaking. Column A's Primary + Live chips are bound to the 'White study' collection (VariableCollectionId:851:418, one try/{brand} colour each); column B is the static white-safe target. Printed contrast ratios are labels, NOT live readouts.

Figma: the POC page carries '08 · Marks — white-safe primary' (node 855:418) — a COPY, masters untouched. Top row is live instances of the mark set; bottom row is detached copies with ONLY gradientStops[1] replaced, so highlight and deep are provably identical and any visible difference is the middle stop alone.

Colour: measured against PURE WHITE (#ffffff, which every theme scope sets as --{code}-primary-foreground — NOT the #f8fafc base), the marks as drawn read db 4.57 (passes untouched), rm 4.03, ec 4.00, ph 3.66, aiden 3.64, nb 3.25, dc 3.15. Smallest hue- and chroma-preserving drop to clear 4.5: nb -9.3 L*, dc -10.4, aiden -6.0, ph -5.8, ec -3.2, rm -3.1, db 0.

Colour: solve a contrast target against the ROUNDED 8-bit hex, not the float. Stepping L* down until the float passes yielded #00867a (4.48) and #dc01b0 (4.49) — both fail once written as hex. Round inside the search loop.

Design: a three-stop mark HIDES a middle-stop change — the highlight and deep dilute it, so even a 10 L* drop reads as a slightly deeper icon. A solid button is the whole middle stop, so the same change is obvious there. Always show both when proposing a mark colour change, or the reviewer sees no difference and assumes nothing happened.

Colour: the shipped POC anchors now come from '08 · Marks — white-safe primary' bottom row, NOT the mark masters on the same page. Light middles are a contrast solve against pure #ffffff; deeps were re-cut by hand by the owner to keep the marks' depth. The masters still hold the pre-solve values — the repo is ahead of Figma.

Design: a per-brand --primary-foreground (some brands white, some ink) measures fine and is a worse system — the CTA's label flips colour depending on which sub-app you are in, for a reason no consumer can see. Move the FILL to fit one label rather than the label to fit each fill.

Colour: deep re-cuts are cheap to the surface system. Because deep only reaches surfaces through a 60%-slate stock applied at single digits, hand-editing all six deeps moved every tinted surface by 0.0-0.6 dE00 and muted-text contrast by at most 0.05. Deep is safe to treat as a design judgement; the middle is not.

Colour: db's deep was re-cut violet -> navy (#2e0db0 -> #002e7c, -44 chroma, -14 hue). It FIXED the long-standing db/aiden collision (deeps 7.8 -> 18.0 dE00, surfaces 2.3 -> 6.0) and CREATED a db/ec one (deeps 18.7 -> 10.3, surfaces 4.6 -> 0.9 — indistinguishable). Moving a deep to resolve one adjacency can silently create another; check every pair, not just the one you were fixing. Nothing in the surface recipe warns about it.

Colour: mixing a WARM brand into a COOL neutral passes THROUGH grey. ph's border (orange primary into slate-300 #cbd5e1) reads chroma 6 at 20%, 0.7 at 10%, 2.0 at 8% — non-monotonic, because the mix crosses the neutral axis around 10-11%. So 'half the brand in the border' silently means 'no brand at all' for the warm brands. Check chroma per brand, not just the percentage.

Design: --ring is not chrome and should not be greyed with the borders. It is the focus indicator; WCAG 1.4.11 wants it to stand out from its surroundings, and dulling it toward slate makes it agree with the border it sits beside.

Technique: to desaturate a shadow WITHOUT lightening it, pre-mix the source into a slate of almost the same lightness rather than lowering the alpha. Deep 35% into slate-700 dropped chroma 25-107 to 11-55 while the composited weight over a white card stayed 1.44-1.50 (raw deep was 1.40-1.55 — same depth, more consistent).

Colour: a border mixed toward slate-300 (#cbd5e1) converges on chroma 7.1, NOT zero — the neutral token is itself a cool blue-grey. At 5% brand the seven POC brands land on 3.9-10.7, within about 3 of the plain token either side. That is the floor of the mix-toward-neutral technique; going lower does not get greyer, it just crosses the axis.

Design: two applications that EMBED in each other should share a surface, not differ. db and aiden now share the deep exactly (#1d43a9), so their tinted surfaces are byte-identical — the owner's reasoning being that a surface which shifts as you cross a boundary users cross constantly is noise, not information. Do not 'fix' a zero surface distance by measurement; which pairs may look alike is a product question about adjacency.

Colour: a gradient can have zero LIGHTNESS travel and still not look flat. aiden's mark runs middle L*33 -> deep L*32, but chroma runs 112 -> 64, so it reads as a saturation fade; the glass overlay supplies the light-falloff separately. Measure depth as L* delta, but look at the render before calling it a defect.

Design: a mark colour and a UI accent are allowed to be different colours, and that is NOT the same smell as a derived --primary sitting a few percent off its anchor. The test: can you SEE the difference and say why in one sentence? aiden's mark stays violet #4d14de (the AI identity) while --primary is indigo #2543d2 (a violet that saturated is too much on every button, chip and progress bar). 9.2 dE00 apart, deliberately.

Figma/CSS: when --primary is allowed to diverge from a mark's middle stop, every ARTWORK rule must switch to the mark token. The first cut of the aiden split left var(--primary) in --poc-mark/--poc-hero/--poc-bubble, so the mark silently turned indigo — undoing the entire point — while every contrast measurement still passed. Contrast tests cannot see 'the right colour in the wrong place'.

Design: splitting --primary off a mark's middle stop FREES the mark. aiden's middle had been stuck dark (L*32.6, half a point above its own deep, the only mark in the set with no light-falloff) purely because it had to carry a white label. Once the label moved to a separate --primary, the middle lifted to L*41.7 and the mark got 9.6 L* of depth back. A contrast constraint on a display colour distorts the artwork; take it off and the artwork fixes itself.

Figma: figma.createAutoLayout() returns a frame with a DEFAULT WHITE FILL. On a light panel that is invisible; drop the same rows on a dark panel and every one paints a white strip that hides the light-coloured labels on it. Clear fills = [] on every layout container you create, or check the render on the darkest surface you intend to use.

State 2026-08: the POC page carries '09 · Anchors — light and dark' (node 873:500). LIGHT rows are detached, recoloured copies because the mark masters are stale for light; DARK rows are live instances because the Mode=Dark masters are still accurate. Dark has received NONE of the white-label solve, the deep re-cuts, the db/aiden shared deep or the aiden split — five of seven deeps now sit >8 degrees of hue from their light counterpart (ec 14, aiden 16, nb 13, rm 12, db 10).

Colour: aiden's two modes are no longer the same brand. Light mark middle is a violet at hue 309 chroma 100; dark is a blue at hue 289 chroma 62. Whenever one mode is reworked and the other is not, check hue delta per stop across modes — contrast tests run per-mode and will never see it.

CSS: the POC recipe selects on [data-theme-poc][data-brand='x'][data-mode='y'] — a COMPOUND selector, all three on ONE element. A nested <div data-brand='db'> inside a poc scope matches nothing and silently renders stock slate. The suite page's first run had correct layout and no brand anywhere for exactly this reason. Stamp all three attributes or none.

Design: the parent brand is not a colour, it is the SET. The suite page is the only surface allowed to use every brand at once (a spectrum ramp across the headline, a six-corner bubble field) — inside a sub-app that would contradict the point, which is that one brand is in charge. Scope full-set styling to its own class prefix so it cannot leak.

Colour: a mark's glyph should track --primary-foreground, not be pinned white. Dark middles are LIGHT by construction, so ink on them reads 5.11-6.42 — the same fact that lets dark-mode buttons carry ink. Pinning the glyph white makes the mark disagree with every button beside it in dark.

Figma->CSS: a gradient's ANGLE is not in the file — Figma stores a gradientTransform. For the mark's ramp, [[0.62,0.62,-0.12],[-0.62,0.62,0.5]] solves to an axis from (0.5,-0.31) to (1.31,0.5) in unit space = CSS 135deg, and projecting Figma's 0/0.52/1 stops onto the CSS gradient line of a square box puts them at 9.7/51.6/90.3%. Copying the stop positions straight across compresses the ramp and loses the deep corner.

Figma->CSS: a layer's opacity multiplies its fill's per-stop alpha, and CSS has no layer opacity on a background-image. Fold the product into each stop (mark sheen: layer 0.7 x fill 0.7 x stop 0.5 = 0.245) or the whole layer comes out roughly twice as strong.

CSS: a grid child with no z-index paints BELOW a ::before on the same element — pseudo-elements come after normal-flow children in the same stacking context. The mark's icon needed position:relative;z-index:1 or the sheen washed over it.

State 2026-08: .poc-mark is now the full six-layer stack from the Figma component (ramp, radial highlight, bloom, sheen on ::before, sparkle on ::after, icon) plus 1 drop + 3 inner shadows. THREE drop shadows and one magenta radial fill exist in the component and are switched OFF — deliberately not reproduced. Everything is percent-based except the sparkle blur and the shadow offsets, which read --poc-mark-px set inline.

CSS: :nth-child counts ALL siblings, not matching ones. Adding a bloom element ahead of three .poc-mark__glint spans shifted every glint by one and left the third matching nothing — width 0, no animation, silently absent, and it still passed every structural check. Select repeated siblings by a data index that travels with the element, not by position.

Motion: stagger by PRIME-ish durations that share no common factor (11s / 7.3s / 4.1s / 5.3s / 6.7s). The composite cycle then runs minutes and never visibly repeats — the magic is not any one animation, it is that the next one is unpredictable. A single shimmer on a loop is found by the eye in about two passes.

Motion: do NOT speed ambient loops up on hover — changing animation-duration mid-cycle snaps the element to a new position. Add a one-shot animation and transition-based changes instead, and leave the loops running underneath.

Design: a four-point star (clip-path polygon) reads as a catch of light; a blurred circle reads as bokeh. The star also survives the blur that makes it glow, so it is the better primitive for a sparkle.

Design: sparkles must never land on the glyph. A mark's icon sits centred at 46%, so it owns 27-73% on BOTH axes — any twinkle inside that box competes with the thing the mark exists to show. Pin them to the rim.

Design: a lift with an unchanged drop shadow reads as a sticker, not a lift. Grow the blur AND swing the offset toward where the light now falls, and give the icon its own drop-shadow moving the OTHER way from the tile's tilt — the parallax is what sells the depth, not the scale.

Figma->CSS: a radial gradientTransform with a rotation component is an ELLIPSE, not a glow. The owner's motion frame added a white radial at 20% rotated 62 degrees, centred at -6.5%/22.8% of the tile; solving it revealed a raking light STREAK, which became the primary ambient motion. Always solve the transform before deciding what a fill is.

Design: the mark's sparkle stays STATIC. Two passes animated it — a pulse, then three four-point stars — and both times it stopped being a highlight and became the thing you looked at. A mark exists to show its glyph; a detail on the glass should not out-compete it. Same verdict on a raking light streak: faithful to the source, genuinely pretty, and one more moving thing on a 26px tile. Ambient motion is now bloom (11s) and sheen (7.3s) only, both slow, plus hover.

CSS bug class: never TRANSLATE or ROTATE a highlight band that is pinned to an edge. The mark's sheen sits at the top of the tile and its brightest point is its top edge (alpha 0.243); translating it down 2% and rotating 1.5deg lifted that edge off y=0 and exposed it as a bright line running the full width, sliding every 7s. Scale from transform-origin 50% 0% instead, so the band only grows into its own falloff and the pinned edge cannot move.

CSS: a PERCENTAGE border-radius on a child resolves against the CHILD's box, not the parent's. `border-radius: inherit` on the mark's 52%-tall sheen gave it its own elliptical corners (37.8px x 19.8px) that read as curved highlights. Overhang the sides and let the parent's overflow:hidden do the trimming.

Debugging: clearing #storybook-root wipes the story-injected <style>. A diagnostic that rebuilt a rig with root.innerHTML='' silently deleted the entire POC stylesheet, so every subsequent 'no rules match' reading was an artifact of the tooling. Append a rig, never replace the root.

CSS: an animation ALWAYS beats a transition on the same property, so you cannot add a hover transform to an element whose loop already animates transform — it is silently ignored. Swap the animation-name on hover instead and use animation-fill-mode: forwards to hold the state while the pointer is there.

Design: two highlight layers on the same object should run on the SAME clock. The mark's sheen and sparkle now share 7.3s in phase — they are one light on one piece of glass, and separate durations make the tile look like it has two light sources. The bloom deliberately does NOT share a factor with them, because it is atmosphere rather than a highlight.

TRAP, again, new guise: a BACKTICK inside POC_CSS terminates the template literal. Prose in a CSS comment saying `transform` broke the file at build time. The header warns about comment delimiters; add backticks to that list. tsc catches this one immediately, unlike the comment-delimiter version which fails silently.

CSS: `translate`, `rotate` and `scale` are INDIVIDUAL properties in modern CSS, not one composited transform. That lets an animation own one and a transition own another on the same element — the mark's sparkle loop owns translate+opacity while hover owns scale. It is the clean way out of 'an animation always beats a transition on the same property'.

CSS: a keyframe property declared only at the frames where it CHANGES is interpolated across every gap between them. Declaring the sparkle's translate at just the two jump frames made it cruise from corner to corner instead of teleporting — straight through the glyph, 12% overlap, measured. Repeat the value at the start AND end of every dwell to hold a position.

Motion: put the EXIT transition on the base rule and the ENTRY on :hover. One transition for both directions means either a dull entry or a snapped exit, and a spring easing on the way out overshoots back toward rest, which reads as a flinch. The mark uses 460ms ease-out leaving, 200ms ease-spring arriving.

Tooling: npm run test:poc-css guards the recipe's template literal — stray backticks (loud), prose outside a comment (silent), unbalanced braces (silent), and any line that is not valid CSS. Added after backticks broke the build twice in one session.

Design: a highlight is ONE fixed light on ONE fixed surface, so it does not tour the object. Moving the mark's sparkle between three corners read as three different sparkles rather than one piece of glass catching the light. It holds its corner and wanders ~4% of the tile instead — a lens flare, not a firefly. Bias the drift AWAY from the glyph so no keyframe can approach it.

Technique: the tvOS parallax is three CSS custom properties. A pointer handler writes --mx/--my (-1..1 from centre) and --on (0/1); every visual rule is a calc off those. React never re-renders, nothing is written per frame but the variables, and it degrades to nothing if the handler never runs.

Perf: cache getBoundingClientRect on pointerENTER, not per pointermove — it forces layout, so calling it every move is a forced reflow per frame. And batch the writes in one rAF carrying only the newest position: pointer events fire faster than frames on a high-rate trackpad.

Design: in a depth parallax, WHICH WAY each layer moves is the whole effect. Background layers move WITH the tilt and least; foreground moves AGAINST it; the specular moves against it hardest, because a highlight does not sit still on a turning surface; the shadow swings opposite because the light did not move, only the object did.

CSS: a pointer-driven translate and an animation-driven translate cannot share an element. The mark's flare is two nested elements — the loop owns the inner translate, the pointer owns the wrapper's. Same 'one property, one owner' rule as animation-vs-transition.

CSS bug class, SECOND occurrence: a layer pinned to an edge must never be allowed to move AWAY from that edge. The sheen's top edge is its brightest point; the pointer tilt reintroduced a downward translate and the bright line came straight back. Bias the term so it can only ever be negative — calc((var(--my) - 1) * n) is 0 at one extreme and -2n at the other — rather than trusting the range to stay small.

Measurement: getComputedStyle().translate returns the AUTHORED unit, '%' or 'px', not a resolved pixel value — and a percentage there resolves against the element's OWN box. Treating '7%' as 7px made a correct layout measure as 12 points out of position and nearly triggered a fix for a bug that did not exist. Convert per-token, using each element's own dimensions.

Geometry: do not measure a child's position against a parent that carries a 3D transform. getBoundingClientRect on a rotated parent returns the axis-aligned bounding box of the projected quad, which is larger than the face, so every child reads as further inside than it is. Measure in the untransformed layout space instead.

DECISION (final, 2026-08): Aiden is a SURFACE, not a seventh brand. A theme says which room you are in; Aiden is the assistant that walks into whichever room you are already in. It takes the MAIN BRAND'S NEUTRALS — a panel that repainted its host's surfaces would tear a hole in the page, and Aiden's own product is a chat, where a surface tint is a liability rather than an asset (Claude and ChatGPT are near-neutral for the same reason). The gradient carries the identity instead.

RULE: gradient fill = Aiden, flat fill = a sub-app. The gradient is a CATEGORICAL difference where a surface tint is only ever a matter of degree — a gradient FAB in a db page reads as not part of the page. Every mark in the system is a three-stop gradient, so the pull toward giving the six brands gradient buttons is real; the second gradient in the system is the one that kills the first.

Design: Aiden's fill is the MARK'S OWN RAMP — same anchors, same 135deg axis, same 9.7/51.6/90.3 stops — so a button and the icon beside it are visibly the same object rather than two things that happen to share colours.

TRAP: a token can go stale while every consumer looks right. --poc-mark still held the pre-solve 140deg/0/52/100 ramp while .poc-mark had been rebuilt inline at 135deg/9.7/51.6/90.3, and NOTHING consumed the variable — so it read as correct until --aiden-fill was compared against it. One definition, consumed by everything; a gradient defined twice under one name will drift.

Design: a mark and a button should NOT share a gradient. A mark is ~48px of artwork with nothing on it, so a third stop reads as depth; a button is a wide flat shape with a label across it, and the third stop only ever appears as a band the eye has to cross. Aiden ships a 3-stop mark and a 2-stop fill.

Colour (Aiden fill, POC, current): light #0060ba -> #8244ff on white, worst 5.00; hover DEEPENS 5 L* to #0054a4 -> #7236f0 (6.03). Dark #47a6ff -> #aa75ff on ink, worst 5.69; hover LIGHTENS 5 L* to #70b3ff -> #b786ff (6.69). Opposite hover directions because light carries white and dark carries ink. The violet end holds across modes (308/308); the BLUE end does not — 282 light vs 271 dark, an 11 degree split taken deliberately because dark needs the lightness to carry ink and the hue moved with it. If they ever have to match, rotate LIGHT toward 276, not dark toward 282 — dark has no lightness to spare. The mark keeps its own 3-stop ramp and is NOT this gradient.

Colour: a 2-stop gradient must clear its label at BOTH ends, so the constraint is the LIGHTER stop. White needs L* <= 49.9, which killed #48a3ff (L*71, 2.64) and #008ace (L*54.7, 3.80) before #007cba (L*49.4, 4.51) worked. A mark's stops are almost never reusable as a button fill for exactly this reason.

STATE 2026-08 (open problem): db moved to the shipped indigo #6063f1 and its deep to #01529e, which broke two earlier decisions silently. (1) db and aiden no longer share a surface — deeps 6.2 dE00 apart, where they were byte-identical by decision; it costs nothing only because aiden takes the MAIN neutrals and never derives a surface from its deep. (2) aiden's FLAT accent #5a56d3 is now 5.9 dE00 from db's #6063f1, the tightest pair in the set, between the two apps that overlap most — it was 20.7 before the move. The gradient does not fix this: the flat accent is what paints aiden's text, borders, chips and its own app's buttons.

CORRECTION to the previous entry: db and aiden no longer sharing a deep is MOOT, not broken. That rule existed so their surfaces would match; aiden takes the main brand's neutrals now, so it never derives a surface from its deep at all and the two match by construction whatever the deeps do. Aiden's deep is mark artwork only. The one real open issue is the FLAT ACCENT: #5a56d3 vs db's #6063f1, 5.9 dE00.

CSS: a scope wrapper dropped into a grid or flex parent TAKES A CELL. The Aiden FAB's data-surface wrapper collapsed six dashboard layouts before it got display:contents, which removes the box while leaving custom-property inheritance intact — the same trick DirectionProvider uses for its dir wrapper.

DECISION: an app MARK does not invert with the mode. It is brand artwork, not a themed component — an iOS icon is the same object whatever the system theme is doing. The POC's marks now read --mark-a/b/c, which carry the LIGHT anchors in both modes; --primary-* stays mode-aware because it paints UI.

Why the mode-aware mark failed: dark anchors are lighter by construction (middles L* 57-64 vs light's 45-50), so in dark the marks came out 8-14 points BRIGHTER than in light on a page 87 points darker. They read as lamps, not objects — and because the glyph tracked --primary-foreground it went ink, making them look like light-mode stickers on a dark page. Every glass layer (sheen, inner highlights, bloom) assumes a mid-dark tile and does nothing on a pale one.

OPEN: with constant marks, the tile sits 3.17-3.25 against the dark page — above the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 wants for a UI boundary — EXCEPT aiden at 2.70, whose ramp is the darkest in the set. An Aiden FAB on a dark page needs a ring or shadow to hold its edge; the fill alone does not.

THE SOURCE FRAME WAS BOUND TO A FOREIGN VARIABLE LIBRARY, and it rendered correctly, which is why nobody caught it. Three fills on the owner-supplied TabBar frame (1275:2003) pointed at variable ids carrying remote library keys — d2604e6b.../3243:105 and friends — not this file collections. Figma reported their names as --muted-foreground and colors/slate/500, so they LOOKED like our tokens; the resolved values were another system entirely (that library --muted-foreground is #f1f5f9; ours is #475569). A foreign binding is invisible until the other library moves or unpublishes. CHECK WHAT A FILL IS BOUND TO, NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: a local id is VariableID:N:N, a foreign one is VariableID:<40-hex>/N:N.

The component index grid (1220:62) is an auto-layout HORIZONTAL frame with layoutWrap=WRAP, so cell ORDER is child order — writing x/y on its children is a silent no-op that auto-layout immediately overrides. Insert a new component with grid.insertChild(indexOfNextName, cell); everything after re-flows for free. The first attempt re-computed a 6-column grid by hand and assigned coordinates, which appeared to work in the return value because the positions were read back before layout settled.

Index page counts live in a _Doc/PageHeader INSTANCE, so they are component-property-driven text: setProperties on the instance, never .characters (which silently no-ops). Both the description prose and a _Doc/Meta pill carry the number independently — updating one and not the other is the drift the playbook already records. Verify by reading the rendered characters back, not by trusting the write.

Renaming instance labels invalidates PROSE that described them. Switching the TabBar page to generic Tab 1..N labels silently falsified two section descriptions that explained why the third tab truncated — with short labels nothing truncates. Figma has no typechecker for this: the prose still reads fluently and is simply wrong. After any content rename, re-read the surrounding prose, and sweep for product names in component DESCRIPTIONS too, not just TEXT nodes.

THE FIGMA VARIABLE NAMES IN THIS PLAYBOOK WERE STALE. The colour variables are NOT named color/* — they are surface/* and text/* (surface/background 2:3, text/foreground 2:4, surface/secondary 2:5, text/muted-foreground 2:8, surface/accent 2:9, surface/card 2:11, surface/border 2:15). The IDs recorded were correct; the names were not, and a name lookup for "color/background" returns nothing. Resolve by ID, or list the collection first.

INSTANCE_SWAP properties in this file take a NODE ID, not a component key. Passing comp.key throws "Property value is incompatible with component property type". Read the property's current value first — it is a node id like "312:20158" (Icon/plus) — and pass the same shape. Cost: an actions cell shipped a plus glyph instead of an ellipsis, silently, because the swap was wrapped in a try/catch that swallowed the error. NEVER swallow a setProperties error; report it.

An effect-style focus ring will not render on a node whose fills are []. Focus/* styles are drop shadows, and a drop shadow needs an opaque shape to cast from. Three focus demos rendered as nothing at all while every property read back correctly. Put the ring on a FILLED wrapper sized to the control.

node.clone() inside a try/catch that then throws leaves the clone ORPHANED on the page. A diagnostic probe that cloned an instance, called setProperties (which threw), and only removed the clone afterwards left a stray node at page level — the script itself succeeded, so nothing flagged it. Found only by listing page.children during the final lint. Put the remove() in a finally, or check page children before declaring done.

The claim that the API cannot reach instances nested inside component-set variants is NARROWER than recorded. setProperties and findOne reached the nested Button/Checkbox/Badge instances in all 18 variants of two sets. The original finding was about reading VECTOR geometry; do not assume the whole class of access is blocked.

A proposal page needs its honesty markers designed in, not appended. The Overview chip that normally carries src/components/{Name} is the one a designer scans for, so that is the chip that must be replaced with the warning — adding a note lower down leaves the scannable line still implying the component ships.

A component-SET whose layoutMode is VERTICAL cannot take layoutWrap = WRAP — Figma throws. The recorded gotcha says WRAP must be set AFTER layoutMode = HORIZONTAL; the same rule bites from the other side when the node is vertical and you just want more columns. Check layoutMode before reaching for WRAP, and remember the script is atomic, so the throw rolls back everything else it did.

An INSTANCE keeps the fixed width of its source variant even after you hide children inside it. Hiding two of four triggers to make a compact theming cell left every instance at the variant's 440px, so seven cells wrapped to two per row. Resize the instance to its inner hugged content (read the child frame's width and resize to it) — hiding children is not a layout operation on the instance.

Two adjacent 1px borders read as one 2px rule and are invisible in a screenshot. A browser-style tab strip drew a hairline on the tablist AND a border-top on the panel, flush against each other with a zero gap. Only a measured read (list.bottom vs content.top, plus both border widths) showed it. Whenever two elements meet with gap 0, check whether BOTH are drawing an edge.

A component set can ship with ZERO non-variant properties and still look finished. Tabs had Orientation and Variant and nothing else — its triggers were plain FRAMEs whose componentPropertyReferences was an empty object — so every label was uneditable without detaching, and nothing in the lint or a screenshot showed it. When auditing a set, read componentPropertyDefinitions and check whether any entry is NOT type VARIANT.

Accessing findAllWithCriteria on a TEXT node THROWS on the property GET — `typeof node.findAllWithCriteria !== "function"` does not guard it, because reading the property is itself the error. Guard by node type against a container whitelist (FRAME/GROUP/COMPONENT/COMPONENT_SET/INSTANCE/SECTION) before calling it.

Replacing hand-drawn frames with component instances DESTROYS any override that targeted those frames. Fourteen theming cells had hidden two trigger frames directly; after the rebuild those nodes were gone and all four tabs returned inside a box sized for two. Before swapping frames for instances, list what currently overrides them and plan the equivalent property — the repair is only cheap if the new component actually exposes one.

ComponentNode.instances can return instances whose ancestor chain never reaches a PAGE, on any page you load. Treat "unreachable" as a real bucket in any instance audit and report it rather than assuming zero — it can mean an unloaded page, or someone editing the file at the same time.

A STALE-BUT-BOUND VARIABLE PASSES EVERY LINT. When a component moves from one token to another, hand-drawn examples elsewhere on the page keep their old binding — surface/muted here — and the design-check lint sees a properly bound fill and says nothing. The page then states two different truths at once: the set and the TOKENS list said --accent while 14 drawn tablists said --muted. After ANY token change, sweep the whole page for the OLD variable id specifically; passing the lint is not evidence.

Examples built as hand-drawn frames drift; examples built as instances cannot. The Tabs page had four hand-drawn example tablists that silently fell behind the component twice — once on the token change, once when two variants were added and the examples still showed only the default. Replacing them with configured instances (reading the old labels, active index and panel copy off the frames first) makes the next component change propagate for free. Prefer an instance for any example the component can actually express.

Adding a variant axis to a component silently makes every existing EXAMPLE incomplete, not just wrong. Nothing errors, nothing lints, and the examples still render — they just quietly document one third of the component. Treat "what does this page now fail to show?" as part of shipping a new axis, alongside the prose sweep.

Appending a _Doc/ChangelogRow with insertChild(0, row) puts it ABOVE the section header. The history frame contains the _Doc/Section title as its own child at index 0, so index 0 is the header slot, not the first row. Two rows rendered above the "Version history" heading before anyone noticed. Find the section index first and insert after it — or append to the end, which is what the convention wants anyway.

Figma changelog rows are OLDEST first; the Storybook changelog is NEWEST first. Both are correct and the mismatch is deliberate — the Figma section literally instructs "Append a row per edit", and ToggleGroup, Button and Toggle all read 1.0 -> 1.1 -> 1.2. Check an existing multi-row page before choosing an order rather than carrying the Storybook convention across.

Moving several children into a new order with insertChild(i, node) throws "Cannot insert node at index greater than the number of existing siblings" — moving a node within its own parent shortens the list mid-loop and the later indices go stale. Replay the whole desired order with appendChild instead, which moves each child to the end in sequence.

A network error from use_figma (net::ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR) does NOT mean the script did not run. Atomicity covers SCRIPT errors, not transport failures — a 120-variant clone completed in full and only the response was lost. Always re-read state before retrying, and write the guard that makes a retry idempotent BEFORE running anything expensive.

A Figma BOOLEAN property can only drive `visible`. Anything that changes a STYLE — opacity, fill, size — has to be a VARIANT axis. That is why "disabled" on Button could not be the boolean it looks like it should be, and why it doubled the set to 240.

Before claiming a component follows "the file convention", COUNT. The ledger said states live in the Spec table rather than as variants, "set by Button" — but 20 of 33 audited sets carry a state axis and only 13 do not. The note described one component and had been generalised into a rule. componentPropertyDefinitions across the ledger's setIds is a cheap census; run it before arguing from convention.

Doubling a component set silently breaks the page that nests it. Button's Overview frame was a FIXED height and overflowed by 556px the moment the set grew — nothing errors, the variants just run past the frame. After any change to a set's variant count, re-check the containing frame's sizing mode.

Do not run a name-derivation rule across the whole file. A sweep intended for ~24 structural layers on four component pages matched 169 nodes once the page filter came off, including imported chart geometry on the brand-palette pages — which got fake-semantic names like "cluster — jan". A generic name on imported artwork is HONEST; an invented semantic one is a lie about what the node is. Scope the page list explicitly.

A revert regex is as dangerous as the rename it undoes. Reverting everything matching /^cluster/ back to "group" also hit pre-existing legitimate layers named "cluster" on Chip, Toggle, Table and Start Here — 13 nodes, including two the same session had created. Before a bulk revert, diff against the list of ids the original operation actually returned rather than pattern-matching the result.

Name a layer from its own content, not from a template. Button's spec rows carry a _Doc/Annotation holding the style name, so "row — default" falls straight out of the node and matches the Style variant option 1:1. Every one of the 60 validated against the real axis options with zero unmatched, which is what proved the derivation correct rather than plausible.

Renaming a layer does NOT disturb its componentPropertyReferences — a TEXT bound to a Label#... property keeps the binding through a rename. The exception is a SLOT: converting a frame to a slot RENAMES the node to the property name, so there the name and the property are coupled. Rename freely elsewhere; never assume it is safe on a slot.

When a bulk edit has already gone wrong once, drop the heuristic and inspect every node first, then drive the change from an explicit id->name map with a guard on the current value. Nineteen nodes across five pages renamed with zero skips and zero collateral, against a derivation sweep that had hit 169 nodes when it was meant to hit 24.

A component whose internals are FIXED width silently refuses to fill. Setting an INSTANCE to layoutSizingHorizontal=FILL grows the instance, but a fixed-width child inside it does not follow — Accordion/Item grew to 440 while its wrap, trigger and divider stayed at the master's 320, leaving the chevron floating mid-row and the hairline stopping three-quarters across. Set FILL down the WHOLE chain in the master, not just on the placed instance. This stays hidden as long as every example is hand-authored at its final width, which is exactly why hand-drawn examples hide component bugs.

To add a divider to an auto-layout item WITHOUT changing its height, make it an absolutely-positioned child with constraints STRETCH/MAX. A normal child adds its own height to the stack (52 -> 53 everywhere), and a stroke cannot be driven by a BOOLEAN property because booleans only drive `visible`. Absolute children are excluded from auto-layout sizing, so the height is untouched and the boolean still works.

A TEXT property value SURVIVES a variant switch even when the referencing node does not exist in the target variant. Content was set on State=open, switched to closed (which has no content region at all) and back — the value was intact. Properties live on the SET, so there is no need to add hidden nodes to the other variants just to hold a value. Verify on a placed instance, never the master.

Hand-drawn examples on a doc page are the SYMPTOM, not the disease. Accordion's seven examples were geometry because the component had no dividers and no text properties and literally could not render them. Do not rebuild the examples first — fix the component, and the examples become instances almost for free. The ledger already records the test ("if a doc page's examples are hand-drawn, the component is under-modelled"); this is what acting on it looks like.

Audit a Figma component by naming the obvious task and trying it, not by reading its Spec frame. Accordion's Spec documented all three states correctly and told you nothing about the fact that a designer could not type a question or get a hairline between two rows. "Could someone build an FAQ with this?" found in one question what a state-by-state review would have missed entirely.

Only COMPONENTS and COMPONENT SETS appear in the Figma Assets panel — a FRAME never does, whatever it is named. The "editable template frame" pattern therefore costs ALL Assets discoverability, which is invisible when you are building via the plugin API and obvious the moment a designer opens the panel and searches. Say so out loud when proposing it.

The template-frame precedent does not transfer to every list. Sidebar, Chat, TabBar and Table are UNBOUNDED and HETEROGENEOUS. An accordion is a homogeneous stack of one atom at a realistic 3-8 rows, so a locked set with a Rows variant of exposed instances is strictly better — discoverable AND editable per row. Check both properties (unbounded? heterogeneous?) before reaching for a frame.

A count variant of EXPOSED nested instances gives a locked component per-row editability without detaching. Accordion ships Rows 3-8 with 33 exposed Accordion/Item instances; a placed instance let every row be opened, retitled and given its own divider setting, and resizing the whole accordion carried through to row, wrap and divider. This is the ToggleGroup model and it generalises to any fixed-length homogeneous list.

YOU CANNOT FILL A SLOT WITH setProperties — Figma throws "Slot component property values cannot be edited" for both a component key and a node id. Fill it by calling appendChild directly on the SLOT node inside the placed instance. That is the one instance sublayer you are allowed to add to, and it is the whole point of a slot. The ledger documented creating slots but never filling one.

A slot inherits the geometry of the frame it was converted from, including a FIXED size. If the CSS counterpart hugs its content (inline-flex + min-width), set the slot to auto-layout with primary/counterAxisSizingMode AUTO and minWidth/minHeight equal to the old fixed size. Avatar's badge was a fixed 16px box, so a Badge dropped in would have clipped; hugging makes it grow 16 -> 24 and extend from its bottom-right anchor exactly as the CSS does.

Check the page PROSE before assuming the component is right. Avatar's example caption already read "badge slot — usually a StatusDot" while the component modelled a boolean over an empty frame — the writing was ahead of the build. Prose that describes a capability the component lacks is the same signal as a hand-drawn example.

A VARIANT switch on a parent PRESERVES the property values of its exposed nested instances. Switching an assembled Breadcrumb from Glyph=chevron to Glyph=slash changed all three separators at once and left all four crumb labels intact. Do NOT generalise the recorded "an INSTANCE_SWAP property swap DISCARDS nested overrides" lesson to variant switching — they behave differently, and the difference decides whether a count/style axis on an assembly is safe. Verified on a placed instance.

Put the shared style axis on the ASSEMBLY, not only on the exposed children. Breadcrumb separators are individually exposed, but a designer changing a four-level trail from chevrons to slashes would make three separate edits and any missed one leaves a mismatched trail. A Glyph axis on the parent makes it one action and makes the inconsistent state unreachable. Cost: it doubles the variant count, which is trivial next to the correctness win.

Watch for the fix that overshoots. Breadcrumb went locked-single-trail (rejected: examples had to be hand-drawn) -> atoms only (correct, but nothing in Assets to drag) -> atoms PLUS an assembled set. Each step fixed the previous complaint and created the next. When correcting a modelling decision, check whether the opposite failure is now available.

Adding instances of an atom whose geometry is UNBOUND multiplies the lint finding. A new TabBar set added 40 unbound-geometry hits purely because TabBar/Tab carried raw 12px padding that every instance inherits. Fix the ATOM, not the instances: binding the master cleared all 40 and 72 pre-existing on the same page, 226 -> 76. Before adding a set built from existing atoms, lint the atoms first — otherwise you inherit and multiply their debt and it looks like you caused it.

An exposed-instance count variant cannot enforce a single-selection invariant. An assembled TabBar with Tabs=4 lets a designer set two tabs to State=Open, which is invalid. Figma has no cross-instance constraint, so the only honest options are to state it in the set description or to make selection a variant axis on the parent (which multiplies the set). Stated it. Same class applies to any assembly with one-of-N state.

A component can carry a state-like axis and still be missing the interaction states. Chip had Active (a VALUE — pressed or not) and no Disabled at all, while its Spec table documented enabled / hover / focus-visible / disabled. When auditing, separate value axes from interaction-state axes: Active, Checked and State=Complete are the former, Disabled/Hover/Focus the latter, and having one says nothing about the other.

The Assets panel shows PRIVATE components to the file they live in. An underscore prefix (_Doc/Meta pill) excludes a component when the library publishes to other files, but it still appears locally — so a designer working in the source file legitimately sees two things called "chip". Explain the split rather than renaming; the _Doc/* family has 505 instances and the confusion does not exist downstream.
