A _Doc/* master whose leaf name matches a real component makes the Assets panel ambiguous. Searching "chip" returned Chip and _Doc/Chip; "separator" returned nine real Separators plus the doc one. The underscore prefix does NOT keep a component out of the Assets panel of the file it lives in, so the collision is live for anyone working in the source file. Name doc furniture so its leaf can never match a component: Meta pill, Rule, Panel.

Renaming a component master costs NOTHING. Instances track by node id, not by name — 505, 541 and 222 instances all survived their master being renamed, counts identical before and after. Do not talk yourself out of a rename on the grounds that it would "touch" the instances; it does not touch them at all.

Figma breaks words mid-way when a text node is narrower than a single word; CSS does not. A card at 180px left its title 56px and rendered "Engine/ering" — .ui-card__title has no word-break, so a browser would wrap the word whole or overflow. A real instance can therefore still show a rendering the code cannot produce. When an example looks cramped, check whether the break is one CSS would make.

A --background stage does NOT separate a --card object in light mode — both resolve to #ffffff. Card regions sitting on a card panel were invisible at their edges, and a fill swap would have changed nothing; the hairline is what draws the boundary. Check the two surfaces actually differ in BOTH modes before reaching for a fill to create separation.

A component added late can end up loose on the canvas and invisible to every check. Card/Media sat outside every frame for eighteen days with zero instances and no mention in any prose — the page lint passed, no overflow check touched it, and the assembled Card already had the matching slot so nothing looked wrong. Listing page.children is the check that finds this; run it after adding any master.

Grep the page TEXT and you will over-report by 5x. Sixteen components appeared to document a disabled state they could not produce; checking actual Spec state COLUMNS (_Doc/Annotation labels reading enabled / hover / focus-visible / disabled) cut it to three. Prose mentions disabled constantly — "disabled triggers are skipped", "the root disabled overrides" — and none of that is a claim about a placeable state. Match the structure, not the word.

A component can look like it has no disabled support because the rule lives in a SHARED stylesheet. CloseButton.scss contains no :disabled rule at all — it inherits one from .ui-icon-button. Check the shared shells (icon-button.scss, the Button/Input class reuse) before concluding a component does not support a state.

A disabled state is not always just opacity. Fab also hides its pulse rings, because a disabled control that keeps animating is worse than one that does not. Read the whole :disabled block before mirroring it as opacity 0.5 — and if the Figma set does not model the animated part at all, say so in the description so the gap is visible rather than silently correct-looking.

A component master sitting LOOSE on the page canvas is not a cosmetic filing problem — it is invisible to the doc page that is supposed to teach it. Chat had 14 of 20 loose, so the Overview documented six atoms for a family of twenty. Check page.children for COMPONENT/COMPONENT_SET before declaring a page done; the fix is usually one appendChild loop, and if the parts frame is already HORIZONTAL + layoutWrap=WRAP it costs no layout work at all.

Before converting hand-built rows into instances of an existing atom, diff the PROPERTIES, not the look. Chat/ComposerMenu's three rows look exactly like Command/Item and reuse its CSS classes in code — but Command/Item has no icon-swap property, so converting would have flattened three meaningful glyphs (file-text / at-sign / sparkles) into one and erased the slash-vs-mention distinction. Reusing the classes in code does not mean reusing the component in Figma.

textAutoResize=WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT inside a fixed-width auto-layout parent silently clips MID-WORD — the node grows sideways past its container instead of wrapping, and Figma shows no overflow warning. Two Chat demos were unreadable this way. Fix is textAutoResize=HEIGHT then layoutSizingHorizontal=FILL, IN THAT ORDER: setting FILL first is undone by the resize-mode change.

A repeated instance showing IDENTICAL content reads as a rendering bug, not as a demo. Chat/Sources shipped three cards all saying "1 · Q3 Financial Report". Where a component contains N of the same child, give each one distinct content — it costs one setProperties call and is the difference between "the list works" and "the list is broken".

When a Figma master is the PLURAL of a code component, name it that way. Chat/MessageAction contained four buttons; ChatMessageAction in code is ONE button and ChatMessageActions is the row. A singular name on a plural master sends a designer looking for a container that does not exist.

Zero unmapped values in a geometry-binding pass is itself the finding: it proves the numbers were always right and only the BINDINGS were missing. 83 of 83 Chat values matched an existing spacing/radius token. If a binding pass instead turns up literals with no token, that is a design-system gap and must be recorded, never rounded to the nearest rung.

Before calling a component family "nothing to drag from Assets", check its componentPropertyDefinitions for a SLOT. Four of the six families in the Tier-2 audit already had a wired Body slot on their Content component and needed no work at all; the claim was made from the atom list alone.

figma.createSlot does not exist — ACCESSING it throws, it does not return undefined. Slots in this file were authored in the UI. A plugin building a new assembly cannot create one, so a bounded count variant plus exposed nested instances is the mechanism available.

isExposedInstance can only be set on an instance that is ALREADY inside a component or set. When building an assembly from a cloned frame, call createComponentFromNode FIRST and expose afterwards — the other order throws.

Figma refuses to expose an instance that has nothing to configure: "Can only expose instances that have exposed nested instances or children with component property references." A propertyless atom (Command/Separator) cannot be exposed, so filter by whether the main component has any property definitions rather than exposing every nested instance blindly.

combineAsVariants does NOT lay the variants out — they keep their source coordinates and can land stacked at 0,0, which renders as overlapping garbage that looks like a corrupted component. Every set in this file is a VERTICAL auto-layout with 16px padding and spacing (Breadcrumb and TabBar are the reference); set layoutMode, padding, itemSpacing and HUG explicitly after combining, and screenshot it.

A newly created COMPONENT_SET wrapper defaults to corner radius 5 — Figma's own container chrome, which matches no design token and will show up as an unbound-geometry finding with nothing to bind it to. The file's convention is 8 bound to radius/lg; copy it from a sibling set rather than reaching for the nearest token.

Hand-ASSEMBLED is not hand-DRAWN, and only the second is a finding. The "examples are hand-drawn therefore the component is under-modelled" test (from Accordion) applies to frames faking geometry. Command's example palettes are frames of REAL Command/Item and Command/Empty instances showing shapes the fixed assembly cannot express — converting them would have made the page worse.

A loose master with ZERO instances and ZERO properties is two findings wearing one coat: it is invisible to its doc page (Tier 3) and unconfigurable if you do find it (Tier 5). All seven of Sidebar's were exactly this. Count both when triaging, because adopting them without adding properties only fixes half of it.

Corner radius 5 unbound on a COMPONENT_SET is Figma's own container chrome, not a design value — no token will match it and a binding sweep will report it as unmappable. This file's convention is 8 on radius/lg. It turned up on a set built by a plugin (Pagination) AND on one built long before (RadioGroup/Item), so treat four unbindable radius findings on a set as this, and copy the value from a sibling set rather than reaching for the nearest token.

INSTANCE_SWAP is the right property for an icon that carries the meaning of a row. Sidebar/Rail got Icon 1-4 rather than visibility booleans, because a rail IS its icons — hiding rows would have been the cheaper edit and the less useful one. Ask what the component is FOR before choosing between a swap, a boolean and an exposure.

Measure a lint category file-wide before trusting an audit that sampled component pages. Tier 4 was recorded as ~900 findings; the real number was 6,444, and 80 percent of it sat on palette and specimen pages nobody had counted.

Split geometry findings into DOC PAGES (where geometry is the design-system spec and must be bound) and SPECIMEN pages (swatch grids, imported prototypes) before sweeping. Binding 1,712 values on a brand-palette page adds volume, not truth — a swatch exists to show a colour and its corner radius is incidental.

Fractional geometry is the signature of proportional ARTWORK and must be left alone. Mark's 368 remaining values are all 0.225 times a tile size (5.4/24, 7.2/32, 10.8/48, 14.4/64, 18.9/84). Tokenising one ratio scaled across five sizes is impossible and would break the artwork; "all remaining findings are fractional" is a clean end state, not an incomplete one.

There is a real difference between rounding to the nearest token (wrong) and matching a measured house convention (right). Mark's anatomy cards were pad 18 / radius 14; rather than pick 16 or 20 arbitrarily, a histogram of comparable doc cards across seven pages showed pad 20-or-24 on radius 12, which made the target defensible. For a COMPONENT's own geometry neither move is allowed — that would misstate the spec.

Figma's default COMPONENT_SET radius of 5 was file-wide, not incidental: 14 sets carried it, spanning components built months apart. When the same unbindable value appears on a third page, stop fixing it locally and sweep the whole file for it.

A propertyless component is not automatically a gap. Census by what it COULD configure — own text nodes, nested instances carrying properties, icons — and three categories fall out as correct: separators with zero children, artwork masters that are the targets of an INSTANCE_SWAP elsewhere (Mark glyphs MUST stay bare or the swap has nothing to point at), and assemblies whose configuration lives entirely in exposed instances.

Naming a text layer after its own content is a trap that springs later. Three Chart components had layers literally called "Sessions by channel" and "Weekly active users"; the name is accurate exactly until a designer uses the component. Name by ROLE — title, subtitle, axis-N, series-N — which is also what makes the property list readable.

A side-by-side light/dark specimen pair binds BOTH frames to the same mode-aware variable and pins one with setExplicitVariableModeForCollection(modeCollection, darkModeId). Hardcoding the two hexes is what makes them drift: the Charts page dark band was #0f1729 against a real token value of #0f172a, off by one and invisible to the eye.
Exclude the Icons page before running any file-wide component census. It holds ~1,700 single-child glyph masters with no properties, and they will bury the 13 findings that matter.

Scan for hand-drawn depictions by finding ui-* frames that sit OUTSIDE any COMPONENT or INSTANCE, then CLASSIFY before fixing: a container holding real instances (ui-radio-group, ui-item-group) is correct composition, and a frame explicitly labelled a mock is a recorded decision. Only pure geometry where a master already exists is a finding. Of 164 matches, 40 were not findings.

The clearest signal a doc page is not using its own component is the instance count on the master. FeaturedIcon had a 36-variant set with TWO instances while the page drew the tile 44 times. Compare master instance count against how often the page depicts the thing before reading any geometry.

A track that FILLs its cell while its indicator stays FIXED will silently paint 100% forever, because the oversized indicator just clips. Progress's spec table showed 10%, 50% and 100% as three identical full bars. Any progress / meter / slider built as clip-a-wide-child needs BOTH sides pinned, and the check is a screenshot — the raw numbers read as a harmless layout quirk.

When a state exists in the Spec table but not on the axis, extend the axis only where the file's convention says that state is placeable. Tabs/Trigger gained hover and disabled (tab and menu items carry hover here) but NOT focus, which stays painted — so 16 of the 20 spec triggers became instances and 4 deliberately did not. A mixed table is the correct outcome, not an unfinished one.

Variable SCOPES gate the human colour picker only — the plugin API binds regardless. A file can therefore be full of bindings a designer cannot recreate or modify by hand, and it looks fine until someone tries. Audit scopes against actual usage: any token bound to icon strokes needs STROKE_COLOR, to vector fills SHAPE_FILL. text/muted-foreground had 166 stroke bindings and a TEXT_FILL-only scope.

Scope foreground-family tokens TEXT_FILL + STROKE_COLOR + SHAPE_FILL, never FRAME_FILL — icons are stroked vectors so text colours must reach strokes (the currentColor convention), but a text token offered as a frame fill invites painting surfaces with it.

Button.isLoadingProp: isLoading#183:0 — BOOLEAN on the set; each of the 120 variants holds a Spinner instance named 'spinner' at child index 0, visible bound to the prop, Size tracking the button size (XSmall=12, Small/Default=16, Large=20) and stroke bound to the same variable as that variant's label.
Button.setNote: TWO sets: 76:300 'Button' (120 = Variant 6 × Style 5 × Size 4, + Label TEXT + isLoading BOOLEAN) and 260:1600 'Button/Icon-only' (the same 120 with the label suppressed). Separate sets, not a 4th axis: in code `iconOnly` makes the label unrenderable ({!iconOnly && label}), so they are mutually exclusive — same reasoning as Badge vs Badge/Category. Icon-only variants were CLONED from their labelled counterparts, so all fills/strokes/focus effects/theme bindings and the aiden flag/is-dark overlay carry over verbatim; only the label removal, squared padding (--p-1 xsmall, --p-2 else; icon 12/14/20/24px) and aiden's --rounded-full differ. The icon-only set carries an INSTANCE_SWAP property `Icon` pointing at the _Icon/* components on _Template (Plus, Copy, Check, Pencil, Trash, More, Send, Download). That slot is REQUIRED, not decoration: Figma forbids overriding vector geometry inside an instance, so a drawn glyph would have locked every instance to the placeholder. Examples frame now shows icon-only in three contexts (card header actions, toolbar, aiden send) in light and dark.
resolved: The Figma Button set modelled no iconOnly / icon slot, so components composing an icon-only Button (CodeBlock copy, ChatComposerSend) had nothing faithful to instance. Closed 2026-07-25 with the Button/Icon-only set. Also bound the Button set wrapper's padding/radius (previously raw 32px / 5px default) and fixed a 17px overflow — the page is now all-zeros on lint.

Button/Icon-only initially shipped with a drawn placeholder glyph, which made it nearly useless — instances could not change the icon. Reworked 2026-07-25: each variant's icon is now an instance of an _Icon/* component bound to an INSTANCE_SWAP property.

The 8 hand-drawn _Icon/* placeholders were replaced 2026-07-25 by the real lucide library: all 120 variants' icon instances swapped, the INSTANCE_SWAP default repointed to Icon/plus, 18 example instances remapped to their canonical equivalents (Trash->trash-2, More->ellipsis, Send->arrow-up), and the temporaries deleted.

Icon-only buttons rendered a flat 2px stroke at every size, which reads as a blob at 12-14px. Fixed 2026-07-25: each variant's icon vectors now carry 2 x size / 24 (XSmall 1.0, Small 1.167, Default 1.667, Large 2.0), matching the browser. Stroke colour bindings were also restored — swapComponent had discarded them.

Leading and trailing icon slots added 2026-07-25 to all 120 labelled variants — a boolean plus an instance-swap each. A LABELLED button's icon sizes are --w-3/-3-5/-4/-5 (12/14/16/20), which differ from icon-only's 12/14/20/24; each variant sets the matching Icon-collection mode so stroke weight stays right and survives a glyph swap.
Button.props: VARIANT Variant (6) x Style (5) x Size (4) x Disabled (false|true) = 240 per set, on BOTH Button and Button/Icon-only. TEXT Label; BOOLEAN isLoading / Leading icon / Trailing icon; INSTANCE_SWAP Leading glyph / Trailing glyph (Button/Icon-only has Icon instead of Label).
Button.notes: | [1.3 — 2026-08-26] Owner reported that Button had no hover/disabled states. Correct: it had none, while 20 other sets in the file DO carry a state-like axis. Added Disabled (120 -> 240 variants on each of the two sets) by cloning every variant and setting opacity 0.5, which is the whole visual difference in code (&:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: var(--o-50) }). DISABLED MUST BE AN AXIS, NOT A BOOLEAN — a Figma boolean can only drive `visible`, and disabled is an opacity change. Hover and focus deliberately NOT added: Input, Textarea, NativeSelect and Slider all carry Disabled and nothing else, and Button's Spec frame already paints Enabled/Hover/Focus/Disabled properly (339 instances, 60 at half opacity, 143 carrying Focus/* effect styles). The gap was composability, not documentation. Verified: all 420 Button and 37 Button/Icon-only instances resolved to Disabled=false, none broken, none landing on true. | [naming 2026-08-26] The 62 layers named "group" were renamed. They were the Spec table ROWS — [annotation, cell x4] = one style across Enabled/Hover/Focus/Disabled, 6 variants x 5 styles x 2 tables = 60 — plus the 2 Theming brand rows. Named from their own annotation and lowercased to match the Style variant options exactly (row — default | secondary | outline | ghost | link), so a layer name maps 1:1 to the API value. The 2 theming rows read brand row — light / dark, resolved from each row's explicit Mode override rather than from position.
Button.figmaFixes: Overview frame was FIXED height and overflowed by 556px once the sets doubled — set to hug. Both example bars (Examples — Light / Dark) were overflowing by 228px BEFORE this change, a pre-existing NO_WRAP horizontal row needing 1444px in a 1216px frame; fixed with layoutWrap=WRAP.

linkPadding2026_08_31.what: All 48 `Style=link` variants in set 76:300 now have paddingLeft/paddingRight 0, bound to spacing/0 (VariableID:1:3). Mirrors the code change making `style="link"` padless.
linkPadding2026_08_31.why: A link button is inline text; the size padding (10/12/16/24) made it read as indented by its own size and it never aligned with the copy above it.
linkPadding2026_08_31.notDrawn: The hit-target ::after that re-expands the click area by the removed padding has NO Figma equivalent and is deliberately not drawn — the variant shows the visual box, not the target. Stated in the set description.
linkPadding2026_08_31.iconOnlyUntouched: Button/Icon-only (260:1600) was NOT changed. In code `&--icon-only.ui-button--sz-*` is two classes and authored later, so an icon-only link keeps its square padding.

Spinner.themed: indirectly — no colour prop; renders currentColor, so a themed parent colours it
Spinner.notes: Non-interactive: no hover/focus/disabled, so the Spec frame is sizes × colour contexts plus a rotation-phase strip (Figma can't animate). Icon built via figma.createNodeFromSvg with lucide's LoaderCircle path, then rescale(size/24) so stroke stays 2÷24 of the box. Colour is set per-instance on the child VECTOR named 'loader-arc'.

Label.themingFrame: OMITTED — Label is neutral chrome (foreground / muted-foreground / error only). The omission is stated in the TOKENS section so it reads as a decision, not a gap.
Label.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × VARIANT Disabled (False/True) = 6 variants; BOOLEAN Required + 'Show description'; TEXT Label + Description.
Label.notes: Disabled had to be a VARIANT, not a BOOLEAN: Figma booleans can only drive layer visibility, and disabled is opacity 50%. Overview carries an ANATOMY section because six components reuse the .ui-label__* class names rather than nesting <Label> — that split (5 render it / 6 borrow the classes) is the page's most important content.

Input.themingFrame: OMITTED — --ring / --focus / --border-hover / --bg-input-30 are Mode-level neutrals that no data-theme remaps. Stated in the TOKENS section.
Input.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × Error (False/True) × Disabled (False/True) = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message' / 'Icon left' / 'Icon right'; TEXT Placeholder / 'Error message'.
Input.notes: Nests a live Label instance with isExposedInstance=true, so Label's Required / Show description surface on any Input. Owns .ui-input-wrap — documented in the Overview as a CONTRACT because Textarea, NativeSelect, InputGroup and the Chat composer apply the class to their own markup rather than importing Input. When building those four, reuse this wrap spec verbatim; do not redefine borders. [Test-drive fix 2026-07-27] Added swappable Leading glyph (Leading glyph#668:0) + Trailing glyph (Trailing glyph#668:13) INSTANCE_SWAP properties across all 12 variants (default = Icon/search 312:20402), mirroring the code IconLeft/IconRight props — previously the icon was a hard-baked search vector with only a show/hide boolean. Verified: default shows search, swaps to any Icon/* (tested mail 312:19670).

filledAxis2026_09_01.what: Added a `Filled` axis: 12 -> 24 variants. Filled=True renames the text node to `ui-input (value)` / `value` and binds its fill to text/foreground; Filled=False keeps the placeholder on text/muted-foreground.
filledAxis2026_09_01.figmaOnly: FIGMA-ONLY, and the set description says so. In code an input is filled when it HAS A VALUE and `::placeholder` handles the colour — there is no `filled` prop and one must not be added. Same category as Accordion's `Show divider`.
filledAxis2026_09_01.variantNotBoolean: The owner asked for a boolean. It cannot be one: a Figma BOOLEAN can only drive `visible`, and this changes a FILL — the rule already recorded in the playbook (Label's `disabled` became a variant for the same reason). A two-node boolean approach (placeholder node + value node toggled by visibility) also fails, because Figma has no NOT: one boolean cannot show one node and hide the other.
filledAxis2026_09_01.whyItMattered: Before this, mocking a filled form meant hand-overriding the text colour on every instance. Forget it and every entered value renders as a placeholder — which is exactly what the page-102 ready-to-submit frames had to do by hand before the axis existed. NativeSelect never had the problem; its value node is already bound to text/foreground.
filledAxis2026_09_01.cloneStripsRefsAtEVERYDepth: The 12 new variants were made with clone(), which strips componentPropertyReferences — the bug already recorded for Button and the clone-built variants. The first repair pass walked only TWO levels and looked clean, but the trailing-icon glyph sits at level THREE, so `Trailing glyph` silently stopped driving it and every date field fell back to the master's default search icon. Repair must walk to any depth, descending through non-instance containers and stopping only at instance SUBLAYERS (an instance's own refs are settable; its sublayers' are not — setting them throws 'Cannot set component property references on instance sublayer').
filledAxis2026_09_01.verificationTrap: After an INSTANCE_SWAP the instance node takes the SWAPPED COMPONENT's name — the node is called `Icon/calendar`, not `glyph`. A check that locates it by the original layer name reports MISSING on a perfectly wired instance. Locate by componentPropertyReferences.mainComponent instead.
filledAxis2026_09_01.setHousekeeping: Both wrappers re-tidied after doubling: VERTICAL auto-layout, 16 gap and padding bound to spacing/4, radius 8 bound to radius/lg (a set that grows keeps Figma's default container radius of 5, which matches no token).

Textarea.themingFrame: OMITTED — same neutral surface as Input; stated in TOKENS.
Textarea.props: VARIANT Size × Error × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message'; TEXT Placeholder / 'Error message'. No icon slots (a textarea has no room).
Textarea.notes: Reuses Input's wrap via --multi: wrap height auto + padding 0 + align stretch, padding moved onto the .ui-textarea so the native resize grip lands in the true corner. Min-heights 64/96/128 bound to height/16|24|32. The grip is drawn as an absolutely-positioned 2-tick vector named 'resize grip (native)' pinned to MAX/MAX constraints. TextareaSize re-exports InputSize so the two can't drift.
