NativeSelect.themingFrame: OMITTED — same neutral surface as Input; stated in TOKENS.
NativeSelect.props: VARIANT Size × Error × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message'; TEXT Value / 'Error message'. No icon booleans — the right slot is permanently the chevron.
NativeSelect.notesInputGroupSibling: see InputGroup below — fourth and last wrap consumer
NativeSelect.notes: Third wrap consumer and the only one that uses .ui-input-wrap completely unmodified. Two things the page exists to teach: (1) the ours/browser boundary — the closed control is ours, the open list is browser/OS-rendered and unstylable (option color/background honoured on Windows+Linux, ignored on macOS), which is precisely why the floating Select exists; (2) the hit-area trick — the <select> gets margin-right -(--w-4 + --p-2) and equal padding-right so it bleeds under the pointer-events:none chevron, making the whole trailing edge open the menu, size-independently. NO open-state frame is drawn, deliberately: mocking one OS's menu would document a lie. NativeSelectOption/OptGroup get no Figma components (no visual form of ours).

InputGroup.setNote: 208:97 is InputGroup/Button — the ONLY sub-part modelled as a component set. 16 variants (4 variants × 4 sizes).
InputGroup.themingFrame: PRESENT — the first field component with one. InputGroupButton variant=default fills with --primary (Theme collection) and takes the Aiden gradient under data-surface. Everything else in the family is neutral.
InputGroup.props: InputGroup/Button: VARIANT Variant (default/outline/ghost/destructive) × Size (xs/sm/icon-xs/icon-sm) = 16; TEXT Label.
InputGroup.notes: COMPOUND-FAMILY PATTERN worth copying: of the 6 exports only InputGroupButton has real visual decisions, so only it becomes a component set. Addon / Text / Input / Textarea are layout containers whose look comes from the wrap plus their own padding — documented as SLOTS (a labelled order-0..4 diagram) plus a composition gallery of assembled examples, not modelled as components. Two techniques documented: (1) CSS order decouples visual placement from DOM order so the input always gets Tab first; (2) the doubled selector `.ui-input-field .ui-input-group__wrap` is required to out-specify Input's per-size padding rule — without it the leading edge double-pads (owner hit this bug in code earlier). In Figma the block addons are built as VERTICAL rows rather than emulating flex-wrap + flex-basis:100%; visually identical, far simpler.
InputGroup.slots: InputGroup/Button's `glyph` is a SLOT on the 8 icon-* variants (the icon was fixed geometry, changeable only by detaching). The 8 labelled variants keep the Label TEXT property — a short label is better served by text than by a slot. Matches the code: InputGroupButton takes children: React.ReactNode.

InputOTP.themingFrame: OMITTED — slot surface is neutral; stated in TOKENS.
InputOTP.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Empty/Focused/Partial/Complete/Error/Disabled) = 18; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / Separator / 'Show error message'; TEXT Label / 'Error message'.
InputOTP.notes: The ONE form control that does NOT reuse .ui-input-wrap — slots own their border, radius and focus ring, so forcing them through the wrap would mean fighting its padding/height per size. State is a WHOLE-CONTROL axis, not a per-slot one, because a slot is never designed alone; the Spec adds an isolated slot-state strip (default/active/filled/error/error-active) for the atomic view. Built at length 6 with a toggleable groupSize-3 separator. Caret = 2px bar, --w-0-5 wide, steps(1) blink on --duration-shimmer, shown only in the active EMPTY slot.

Checkbox.themingFrame: PRESENT — checked AND indeterminate fill with --primary (Theme collection); mark is --primary-foreground. Unchecked stays neutral.
Checkbox.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Unchecked/Checked/Indeterminate) × Disabled (False/True) = 18; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
Checkbox.notes: First Phase 2 page. Hidden-input pattern: the native <input> is opacity-0/0x0 (NOT display:none) so it stays focusable + submittable, and every visual state is a CSS sibling selector. Both SVGs (check + dash) are always mounted and overlaid so checked→indeterminate CROSS-FADES; stroke-dasharray 24 → dashoffset 0 draws the stroke in. Box carries margin-top --p-0-5 to sit against the first text line — in Figma that is a 'box align' wrapper frame since auto-layout has no per-child margin. Aiden is a SURFACE effect here (not a variant like Button), so it is documented in text only. Uses .ui-label__* classes rather than nesting <Label> (a label can't contain a label).

RadioGroup.setNote: 223:129 is RadioGroup/Item — the group root is a layout container + context provider, documented as composition per the compound-family rule.
RadioGroup.themingFrame: PRESENT — checked circle fills with --primary (Theme collection), dot is --primary-foreground.
RadioGroup.props: RadioGroup/Item: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Unchecked/Checked) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
RadioGroup.notes: Same hidden-input pattern as Checkbox. DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE: in code `size` is set ONCE on the group and cascades to every item via CSS descendant selectors; Figma cannot model a descendant selector reaching into instances, so each item carries its own Size and the Overview says so explicitly under a '⚠ CODE vs FIGMA' section. The group owns three things the items never receive as props: name/value/callbacks via React context, the size cascade via CSS, and role=radiogroup + aria-labelledby via ARIA. RadioGroupItem throws outside a RadioGroup because a nameless radio silently stops excluding its siblings. Label visibility bound to the ui-label CONTAINER (Checkbox lesson). — UPDATED 2026-08-26 (v1.2): the assembled set was loose on the canvas with a single Orientation axis and no way to change a word of it. Adopted into the Overview, given Label, and all six items exposed.

assembledSet.props: Label (TEXT) + 6 exposed RadioGroup/Item instances (3 per variant)
assembledSet.note: Size is a GROUP prop in code that cascades to every item via one root class and descendant selectors. Figma cannot express that cascade, so Size is set per exposed item instead — stated in the set description.

Switch.themingFrame: PRESENT — on-track fills with --primary (Theme collection). Off stays --switch-track in every theme, deliberately (was --muted until 2026-09-01).
Switch.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Off/On) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
Switch.notes: Third and last of the hidden-input trio. role='switch' on a native type=checkbox — keeps every native behaviour, only changes the announcement to 'switch, on/off'. Thumb travel (12/16/20px) is an intentional hard-coded literal per CLAUDE.md: travel = track − thumb − 2×2px inset. In Figma the thumb is an absolutely-positioned ellipse at x=2 (off) / x=2+travel (on). Overview carries a Switch-vs-Checkbox-vs-Radio decision guide (the distinction is immediacy, not appearance).
resolved: The 'default sits 2px low' alignment inconsistency was a SYMPTOM, not the cause: Switch never passed a size class to its label, so .ui-label__text stayed at --leading-5 (20px) at every size while the track scaled 16/20/24. The margin was patching that mismatch on the one size that least needed it. Fixed 2026-07-25 by adding ui-label--sz-{size} (matching Checkbox and RadioGroup) and deleting the --sz-default margin-top. Track height now equals label line-height at all three sizes (16/16, 20/20, 24/24), so every track is flush with no nudge. The ramps are now coupled — a comment in Switch.scss records that.

switchTrackTokens.why: The off track was surface/muted: 1.48:1 against both the page and the white thumb, and the hover used surface/accent, which is LIGHTER than muted — so hovering an off switch in light mode made it fainter (1.10:1), the opposite of what hover should do.
switchTrackTokens.namespaceRule: Component-scoped colours get their OWN top-level namespace in the Mode collection — avatar/*, tooltip/*, sidebar/*, chat/*, and now switch/*. They are NOT filed under surface/*. Scopes match avatar/background: ['FRAME_FILL','SHAPE_FILL'].
switchTrackTokens.rebind: 12 fills rebound on page 227:32 — the 6 State=Off masters (227:35/43/51/83/91/99) and 6 local surface/accent overrides in the Hover (off) spec column. The other 30 instances inherited from the masters with no per-instance work. Final: switch/track 36, switch/track-hover 6, primary 41, zero left on muted/accent.
switchTrackTokens.staleTextFixed: Five TEXT nodes still NAMED the old tokens and would have been lying after the rebind: TokenPills I229:817 / I229:819, the Theming section blurb I229:264, the Theming note 229:669, and the Examples blurb I229:808. A fill rebind is only half the job on a doc page — grep the page's text for the old token name too.
switchTrackTokens.columnsNotRows: The Spec table's STATE lives in the columns (Off / Hover (off) / Focus / On / Disabled (on)); rows are sizes. The three muted/accent/muted cells are Off/Hover/Focus — NOT Off/Hover/Disabled as the colour pattern suggests. Read the header row before rebinding.

Slider.themingFrame: PRESENT — filled range AND the 3px thumb border read --primary. Unfilled track stays --muted.
Slider.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × Mode (Single/Range) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show value'; TEXT Label. Value text is intentionally NOT a bound property so Range variants can keep '25 – 75' while Single keeps '60' — text in an instance is directly editable anyway.
Slider.notes: The ONE form control with no hidden native input: <input type=range> has a single thumb, so range mode would need a second implementation. Each thumb is its own role='slider' span; ARIA here IS the implementation. Neighbour clamp lives in each thumb's aria-valuemin/max (announced, not just enforced). Position/width are deliberately NEVER transitioned — easing would lag the pointer during a drag; only box-shadow and border-color ease. Track uses overflow:visible so the focus ring escapes a 4px sm track. In Figma the thumb is an absolutely-positioned ellipse; Single sits at 60%, Range at 25%/75%.
Slider.layoutNote: Spec card is 1440 wide (not the usual 1280): 4 state columns × 290px cells overflowed a 1280 card by 22px. Measure row content against the TABLE's inner padding, not just the card bounds — the card-level lint misses this.

Badge.setNote: TWO sets: 236:70 'Badge' (12 status variants) and 236:161 'Badge/Category' (15 hues × soft|solid = 30). Split because `category` OVERRIDES `variant` in code — they are two modes, not two axes.
Badge.themingFrame: PRESENT — only default + outline follow the brand (--primary / --primary-text / --primary-border). The semantic four keep their own colour in every theme; the 15 category hues are a fixed palette and never theme.
Badge.props: Badge: VARIANT Variant (12) + TEXT Label. Badge/Category: VARIANT Hue (15) × Style (soft|solid) + TEXT Label.
Badge.notes: Category variables are NESTED in Figma: category/{hue}/base | /bg | /text (NOT hyphen-suffixed), plus a single category/foreground. The aiden variant is a real gradient variant (unlike Checkbox/Switch where aiden is only a surface effect), so it carries the aidenDarkPattern overlay bound to flag/is-dark — verified flipping. No size prop and no brand variant, both deliberate; stated on the page. Not interactive: a <div> with no role/tabindex, so the Spec has no hover/focus/disabled axis.
Badge.contrastNote: Soft category style is AA-gated (all 15 -text-on--bg pairings in npm run test:contrast). Solid is deliberately NOT gated — inverted --category-foreground dips under AA on amber/green in light. Owner's accepted call; the page says so plainly rather than hiding it.

Kbd.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome (--secondary surface). A keycap that changed colour per brand would read as a button.
Kbd.notes: The keycap look is an ASYMMETRIC border: strokeTopWeight/Left/Right bound to border-width/100 and strokeBottomWeight to border-width/300 — that thicker bottom edge is the whole illusion. minWidth is bound per size (width/4|5|6) so single characters (K, ⌘, ⇧) stay square while multi-character caps (Esc, Enter) widen past it. Font sizes come straight from the SCSS: sm and default are BOTH --text-xs (12px), only lg steps up to --text-sm (14px) — sm differs from default in box size, not type.

Separator.themingFrame: ABSENT — a rule that changed colour per brand would fight the content it divides.
Separator.notes: The labeled variant is a horizontal auto-layout of line/label/line with both lines set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' — that mirrors the CSS flex:1 on ::before/::after, so the word stays centred at any width. In code, setting a label forces orientation to horizontal. The vertical variant relies on align-self: stretch, so it needs a parent that gives it height; dropped into a block container it collapses to nothing (noted on the Spec frame). decorative → role='none' is the documented a11y decision.

StatusDot.themingFrame: ABSENT — semantic, not brand. A green 'online' must stay green in every sub-brand.
StatusDot.notes: The idea worth copying: each status sets ONE custom property (--ui-status-color) and both the dot and the ::after pulse ring read it back, so the colour is written once rather than twice per status. Modeled in Figma as a hidden 'pulse ring' ellipse at 0.35 opacity whose visibility is bound to a Pulse boolean. offline and neutral both resolve to --muted-foreground and therefore render identically — that is faithful to the code and deliberately called out on the page rather than hidden.

Skeleton.themingFrame: ABSENT — the --bg-primary-10 shimmer highlight IS technically themed, but a 10%-alpha sweep is imperceptible as a brand demo.
Skeleton.props: VARIANT Shape (default|circle|text). Width/height are free-form in code — resize the instance in Figma.
Skeleton.notes: The shimmer is a background-position animation on a 200%-wide gradient, not a moving element — nothing in the layout moves, which is why a page of skeletons stays smooth. Figma variables hold solid colours only, so the sweep is drawn as a white low-alpha GRADIENT_LINEAR overlay rather than bound. Make that overlay FULL-BLEED (same size as the shape, x=0, STRETCH constraints): a narrower band's own rect edge shows through the circle's round clip as a hard vertical line.

Code.setNote: TWO components: 252:35 'Code' is a single COMPONENT (inline chip, no variant axis — only a Label text prop); 252:59 'CodeBlock' is a 3-variant SET on a Header axis (filename | copy | none).
Code.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral in every brand. Code should not change colour with the sub-brand.
Code.props: Code: TEXT Label. CodeBlock: VARIANT Header (3) + TEXT Filename + TEXT Code.
Code.notes: The Header axis mirrors real CSS behaviour: with no filename the header switches to justify-content: flex-end (hence the 'copy' variant pushes the button right), and with showCopy=false and no filename there is no header element at all. Documents the deliberate no-syntax-highlighting decision AND that 11 --code-* syntax tokens already exist in tokens.scss (mirrored to Figma as code/*) with zero consumers (now at least AA-gated) — a palette pre-picked for a highlighter we do not have. The Overview carries a syntax-palette REFERENCE (node 265:53) — 11 swatches rendered in mono on the real code/block surface, light and dark side by side, each labelled with its measured contrast. Deliberately a swatch table, NOT a highlighted CodeBlock instance: rendering one would document a capability the library does not have (same rule as NativeSelect's undrawn open state). It also makes both remaining judgment calls visible — attr-vs-number now separate in both modes, selector sharing string's hue obviously enough to read as intended. OWNER DECISION 2026-07-25: the Overview also carries two HIGHLIGHTED MOCK-UPS (node 267:57) — a .tsx and a .scss block, light and dark, between them exercising all 11 code/* tokens with every span bound to its variable. These are NOT CodeBlock instances and the component cannot render them; the owner accepted that designers may build with them and chose to defer the code decision (add a tokenizer dependency vs keep flat rendering) until something actually needs it. The labelled separator and the note directly beneath say so explicitly. Layer names mirror the real component so the intent transfers if it is ever built. This is a deliberate, owner-approved exception to the 'don't draw what isn't ours' rule — do not silently delete it, and do not treat it as licence to mock other unbuilt behaviour.
Code.figmaDivergence: Inline chip vertical padding is 0.1em in CSS (em-relative, ~1.3px at --text-code); Figma variables cannot express em, so it is bound to spacing/0-5 (2px). Stated on the Avatar Overview note covering both divergences.
resolved: The scrollable <pre> had overflow-x: auto with no tabindex, making overflowed code unreachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1 / axe scrollable-region-focusable). Fixed 2026-07-25: tabIndex={0} plus an inset --focus ring in Code.scss. No ARIA role added, so it stays announced as preformatted text.

The 11 --code-* syntax tokens were an exact Tailwind 500/600 mapping that had never been contrast-checked; the script confirmed 10 of 11 below AA in light (2.22-4.29). Fixed 2026-07-25: light values darkened to Tailwind 600/700 (comment uses a derived slate #5e6d7d — the lightest that clears AA, so it stays recessive against --code-variable), and dark --code-attr moved orange-400 → amber-300 to break a collision with --code-number that existed in dark only. All 11 now gated in scripts/contrast-check.mjs (49 pairings, 0 below AA). Figma code/* variables synced. STILL A JUDGMENT CALL, deliberately left alone: --code-selector shares --code-string's hue in both modes (consistent, so it reads as intentional), and in dark --code-type (cyan-400) sits close to --code-function (sky-400).

The Overview composition note claimed the Figma Button set did not model iconOnly. Stale once Button/Icon-only shipped; corrected 2026-07-25. It now states that the copy control corresponds to Variant=Default/Style=Ghost/Size=XSmall/Icon=Copy and explains why it is still DRAWN rather than instanced inside the CodeBlock variants — the 2-second copied→check glyph swap would otherwise need a CodeBlock variant axis for a transient state no consumer controls.

CloseButton.themingFrame: ABSENT — a dismissal is never the themed action on a surface.
CloseButton.notes: The two variants are pixel-identical at rest and differ ONLY on hover (default shifts icon colour; background additionally fills --accent), which is why they are variants rather than separate components — the Spec matrix is built to make that the visible conclusion. Two a11y guarantees are designed in rather than documented around: the native aria-label is Omit-ed and replaced by an ariaLabel prop defaulting to 'Close' (so it can never ship nameless), and type='button' is hard-coded (so it can never submit a form). Focus is a box-shadow, not an outline, because the button is round and transparent. | [1.1 — 2026-08-26] Added a Disabled axis (6 -> 12). Spec documented enabled / hover / focus-visible / disabled; the set had only Variant x Size. The disabled rule lives in the shared .ui-icon-button shell, NOT in CloseButton.scss — searching the component's own stylesheet for :disabled finds nothing, which is why this looked unsupported. 134 instances across eleven pages all resolved to Disabled=false. Also fixed a pre-existing defect: both "ui-dialog (excerpt)" frames in the examples were frozen at a 10px placeholder height holding 78px of content and spilling over the siblings below; both now hug at 78.
resolved: Three defects fixed in code and mirrored 2026-07-25. (1) The hit target was 16x16, failing WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum on the library's most-tapped control; a transparent ::after now widens the pointer target without changing what is drawn. (2) stroke-width was pinned to --icon-border-width (1.33 VIEWBOX units), which halved to a 0.665px hairline at a 12px icon — the thinnest stroke in the library; removing the pin lets lucide's own width scale (1.0/1.33/1.67px), and at a 16px icon that lands on exactly 1.33px, so the token's VALUE was right and only the mechanism was wrong. (3) No size prop, leaving it the last interactive holdout of 26 components that have one — same reasoning that added size to Checkbox and RadioGroup in July. Toast keeps its density with size='sm' (that surface is why the small box existed); Dialog, Drawer, Alert and Banner move to default, whose X grows from a 12px icon in a 16px box to 16px in 24px.

Avatar.setNote: TWO sets: 254:69 'Avatar' (3 sizes × 2 shapes = 6, plus Image + Badge booleans and a Fallback text prop) and 254:184 'AvatarGroup' (3 Spacing variants, each holding 4 nested Avatar instances).
Avatar.themingFrame: ABSENT — a person's avatar is not a brand accent.
Avatar.props: VARIANT Size (sm|default|lg) x Shape (circle|square) = 6. TEXT Fallback; BOOLEAN Image, Badge; SLOT ui-avatar__badge#1543:0 with preferredValues [StatusDot, Badge].
Avatar.notes: The fallback is ALWAYS mounted at z-0 under the image rather than swapped in on error, so a slow image shows initials then resolves and a broken one shows initials permanently — no flash of empty space either way. The badge lives OUTSIDE __inner because __inner owns overflow:hidden to clip the image to the shape; a badge inside it would lose the half that overhangs. Modeled the image as a gradient placeholder rect (no asset uploads). Page updated to v1.1 after both defects were fixed in code — the Spec note now documents the resolution, not a reproduction. | [1.3 — 2026-08-26] Owner asked how to make the badge red with a notification count. The CODE already supported it — badge is an open React.ReactNode whose JSDoc literally reads "Corner slot for a StatusDot or count" — but FIGMA modelled it as a BOOLEAN over an empty 12/14/16px --muted frame, so neither a colour nor a number was possible. Converted the badge to a real SLOT on all six variants (the visible boolean coexists, as recorded) and wired preferredValues to StatusDot and Badge. Also made the slot HUG above a min size, mirroring the CSS `inline-flex` + `min-width` + `padding: 0`: it was a fixed box, so a count would have clipped. With a Badge in it the slot grows 16 -> 24 and extends leftward from the bottom-right anchor, exactly like the CSS. Examples gained a notification count cluster in both bars, and the presence example now holds an ACTUAL StatusDot — it had been an empty muted dot while the caption already said "badge slot — usually a StatusDot". The prose was ahead of the component.
Avatar.figmaDivergence: Initials carry --tracking-wide (0.025em) in code but plain tracking in Figma — pinning letterSpacing detaches textStyleId and 0.35px on two letters did not justify three new Semibold-Wide styles. Noted on the Overview frame.
resolved: AvatarGroup spacing ramp was non-monotonic (sm -8 / default -12 / lg -4). Fixed 2026-07-25 by reassigning the same three values in order: sm -12 / default -8 / lg -4. `spacing` names the visual gap, which runs inversely to the overlap. Groups that never set spacing loosen from -12 to -8, since default was the value out of place.

AvatarGroup `size` reached only the +N chip. Fixed 2026-07-25: the group now cloneElement's direct Avatar children that have no explicit size. Guarded on `child.type === Avatar` so a wrapping element (Tooltip, link) never receives `size` as an unknown prop; an explicit child size still wins.
Stories added: GroupSpacing + GroupSizeInheritance — the absence of these is why both survived.

AvatarGroup rendered flat-sided notches where avatars overlapped. Cause: the group's separating ring was applied to the instance ROOT, which had radius 0 — the circular shape lived only on ui-avatar__inner — so a 3px SQUARE ring was drawn around a circular avatar and its straight edge cut into the neighbour. Fixed 2026-07-25 by binding the root's radius per shape (circle -> radius/full, square -> radius/md), which also closes a fidelity gap: the CSS applies the radius to BOTH .ui-avatar and .ui-avatar__inner, and only the inner had been modelled.
Avatar.note: At Spacing=sm (-12px on a 40px avatar) the next circle clips part of the previous one's initials. That is faithful to the CSS, not a modelling error — worth knowing when choosing a spacing for two-letter fallbacks.
Avatar.figmaOnlyNote: The badge pill is --muted with padding 0 in CSS, so a BARE number renders neutral and cramped. Red-with-a-count comes from composing a Badge (variant=error, label="3") in the slot, which brings its own fill and padding and paints over the muted. The Figma slot steers there via preferredValues. If bare counts are ever wanted, the CSS needs horizontal padding — not done.

AspectRatio.themingFrame: ABSENT — and this one is absolute: AspectRatio.scss contains ZERO var(--…) references. It is the only component in the library that consumes no design token at all. Nothing to theme, and it never appears in the contrast script because it renders no text and no surface.
AspectRatio.notes: `ratio` is a CONTINUOUS number, not a union — any value is valid. Figma variants must be discrete, so the six are REPRESENTATIVE and the set description says so explicitly; this is a case where the Figma model cannot be faithful and the honest move is to label the shortcut. Also one of the few components with NO required `id` (rule 6 exception, like Toaster): no children of its own, no ARIA to wire, no state to announce. Documents the inline-style decision (ratio is per-instance, not a token; consumer `style` is spread after so it wins) and the one a11y trap — overflow: hidden clips the focus ring of any interactive child near the edge.
AspectRatio.manualStep: ⚠ Figma's aspect-ratio lock is READ-ONLY to plugins (node.targetAspectRatio cannot be assigned), so the six variants are sized correctly but not constrained — drag-resizing distorts them instead of deriving the height. Someone must select the six variants and enable the aspect-ratio lock (or set W and H to Scale) in the UI. Noted on the Spec frame and in the set description.

Blockquote.themingFrame: ABSENT — all neutral. Noted on the page that the 4px rule is a plausible place a brand accent COULD live (several design systems tint it) but this one keeps it --border, consistent with the rule that chrome stays neutral. Changing that would be a system decision, not a component tweak.
Blockquote.props: VARIANT Content (single|multi) + TEXT Quote + TEXT 'Quote 2' + BOOLEAN 'Show attribution' + TEXT Attribution.
Blockquote.notes: The Content axis exists to show the paragraph rule: `> p` has margin zeroed so a single-paragraph quote sits flush against the rule, and `> p + p` adds --p-3 back only between consecutive paragraphs — the default state needs no correction. `cite` is Omit-ed from the native props and REDEFINED as displayed content: HTML's own cite attribute takes a source URL that browsers never render, so the component trades machine-readable provenance for a better call site. No required `id` (leaf, no ARIA to wire). Added one text style, base/leading-7/Italic — the only 16/28 pairing in the system; the CSS is --text-base on --leading-7 and no existing style carried it.
Blockquote.specDeviation: ⚠ The HTML spec says a quotation's attribution must be placed OUTSIDE the blockquote (the canonical markup is <figure> + <figcaption>). This component renders a <footer> INSIDE, which is what most component libraries do and degrades gracefully, but strictly makes the attribution part of the quoted material. Documented on the a11y section rather than silently modelled as correct; fixing it would be a breaking DOM change.

ScrollArea.themingFrame: ABSENT — scrollbar chrome stays neutral; nothing reads --primary.
ScrollArea.props: VARIANT Orientation (vertical|horizontal|both). `type` (auto|hover) is NOT a variant — it changes nothing at rest that Figma can show, so it is a note.
ScrollArea.notes: The rails are LAID OUT, not overlaid: the inner element is a CSS grid where the viewport takes cell 1/1 and each rail gets its own fixed column/row with a --p-4 gap, so the thumb can never sit on content in any browser. The viewport needs min-width:0 / min-height:0 or the grid item refuses to shrink and the thing silently never scrolls. Thumb length and offset are computed at runtime from scrollTop/scrollHeight with a 20px floor, so the offsets drawn in Figma are ILLUSTRATIVE and the page says so. ResizeObserver watches the viewport and the children present AT MOUNT; a child that grows later is only caught by the layout effect keyed on `children`.
ScrollArea.codeFixesLandedSameDay: WCAG 2.1.1 — the viewport had no tabIndex, so 474px of content in a 206px box was unreachable by keyboard. Worse than the identical CodeBlock bug because the native scrollbar is hidden, leaving no fallback affordance, and because type='hover' keeps the rail at opacity 0 until :hover or :focus-within — which could never fire with nothing focusable inside. The two defects concealed each other; one tabIndex={0} fixed both. Also tokenized 5 raw opacity literals (ScrollArea x2, CloseButton, Chip, Command) and moved the thumb from cursor:pointer to grab/grabbing.

Chip.themingFrame: PRESENT — only the ACTIVE chip themes: it reads --primary for fill and border and --primary-foreground for the label. A resting chip is --bg-input-30 on --border, both neutral, so it is identical in every brand. The selection is the branded moment; the unselected state is chrome.
Chip.props: VARIANT Size (xs|sm|default) x Active (false|true) x Disabled (false|true) = 12. BOOLEAN Icon left / Icon right; INSTANCE_SWAP Left glyph / Right glyph; TEXT Label.
Chip.notes: Active is a VARIANT axis, not a boolean — it changes fill, border and text colour, and a Figma boolean can only drive visibility. Hover moves only the resting chip (--bg-input-30 → -50); the active rule re-states --primary so a selected filter does not shift under the cursor, and the base hover is scoped :not(.ui-chip--active). Verified the SCSS `:not(&--active)` compiles correctly to `:not(.ui-chip--active)`. Hit targets measured 26 / 34 / 38px tall — all clear the 24px minimum, xsmall being the tightest. | [1.2 — 2026-08-26] Owner: the Chip has no disabled, focused or hover state "like the documentation says it does". Correct, and the Spec table had said so all along — its column labels read enabled / hover / focus-visible / disabled in both light and dark — while the set carried only Size x Active. disabled is a real prop in code (.ui-chip:disabled { opacity: var(--o-50); cursor: not-allowed }), so the page documented a state the component could not produce. Added Disabled as an axis (6 -> 12 variants, opacity 0.5). Hover and focus-visible stay painted in Spec, matching Button, Input, Textarea, NativeSelect and Slider. All 82 instances resolved to Disabled=false; the 12 variants still fit one wrapped row so nothing reflowed.
openQuestions: IconCenter is in ChipProps but does nothing distinct: the JSX renders {IconLeft}{IconCenter}{label}{IconRight}, so it occupies the same slot as IconLeft. With a label present the two are identical; without one it produces the same icon-only chip IconLeft would. Chip has no `iconOnly` switch (unlike Button) to suppress the label, and the container is justify-content: flex-start so nothing ever centres. Either wire it to suppress+centre like Button, or remove it — removing is breaking. Documented on the Overview as an alias for now.

An icon-only Chip has NO accessible name. `aria-label` is an optional prop with no fallback, so <Chip IconLeft={X} /> announces only 'button, not pressed'. CloseButton solves the identical problem by defaulting ariaLabel to 'Close'. Consider the same default, or requiring aria-label when no label is passed (a discriminated union would enforce it).

Toggle.themingFrame: ABSENT and DELIBERATE — pressed fills neutral --accent, never --primary. A toolbar is a row of toggles and a screen has one primary action; if Bold/Italic/Underline all lit up in the brand colour they would out-shout the CTA beside them. Same reasoning as the ghost-button carve-out. Chip is the component that DOES take the brand when pressed.
Toggle.props: VARIANT Variant (default|outline) × Size (sm|default|lg) × Pressed (false|true) = 12, + BOOLEAN Icon + INSTANCE_SWAP Glyph + TEXT Label.
Toggle.notes: Chip-vs-Toggle is the decision this page exists to settle: does the on-state change WHAT DATA is shown (Chip, brand fill) or HOW A TOOL BEHAVES (Toggle, neutral fill)? ToggleGroup does not re-implement any of this — its items reuse .ui-toggle and collapse shared borders ButtonGroup-style, so changing Toggle changes the segmented control. Controlled/uncontrolled boundary is `pressed !== undefined`, so pressed={false} is controlled but omitting it is not — a computed prop that flips to undefined silently hands control back. | [1.2 — 2026-08-26] Added a Disabled axis (12 -> 24). Its Spec table documents hover / focus-visible / pressed / disabled while the set carried only Variant x Size x Pressed. Pressed is a VALUE (is it on), not an interaction state — independent of Disabled, so a pressed toggle can also be disabled. Hover and focus-visible stay painted. All 182 instances resolved to Disabled=false, including the 78 nested inside ToggleGroup, which is the case that would have broken loudest.
Toggle.openQuestion: ⚠ Hover and pressed resolve to the SAME fill (--accent), so an unpressed toggle under the cursor looks identical to a pressed one at rest. In a toolbar this reads fine because the pointer is over only one item and the rest show true state; a LONE borderless toggle is genuinely ambiguous. Documented on the Spec frame with the outline variant recommended as the mitigation. Not changed — distinguishing them would mean a new hover token or a pressed treatment beyond fill, which is a system decision.
Toggle.figmaOnlyProp: Show label#1324:0 (BOOLEAN, default true), added 2026-08-25 and wired to the label TEXT's visibility on all 12 variants. Without it an icon-only toggle could not be drawn at all, even though the code has supported it via IconCenter / .ui-toggle--icon-only since the component shipped. Default true, so no existing instance moved.

ToggleGroup.themingFrame: ABSENT — inherits Toggle's neutral pressed state, deliberately.
ToggleGroup.notes: Items are NOT Toggle instances in code either — ToggleGroupItem is a <button> wearing .ui-toggle, because it reads pressed state from context rather than owning it. ToggleGroup.scss therefore has NO colour/size/state rules; it only arranges. The segmented recipe is three rules: flatten inner radii, collapse borders with margin -1px (--border-w-100), and lift the active item to z-index 1 so its ring/fill is not clipped by an overlapping neighbour. In Figma the items are DRAWN, not Toggle instances, because per-item corner flattening cannot be expressed by an instance whose radius is bound uniformly — stated in the set description.
openQuestions: No arrow-key navigation. The WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern expects a roving tabindex (one tab stop, arrows move within); here every item is its own tab stop. Workable at 3-5 items, which is why the page caps the recommended length. Menubar in this library DOES implement roving tabindex, so the pattern exists if this is worth closing.

The group has no accessible name. role="group" with no aria-label announces just 'group'. Unlike the item-level name (now type-enforced), nothing requires this. Could default one, or require aria-label on the root.
type="single" deselect passes an EMPTY STRING, not undefined — onValueChange is typed (value: string) => void and the code sends `next ?? ''`. Consumers must treat '' as 'nothing selected'.

rebuilt.what: The three segments were hand-drawn FRAMEs named ui-toggle, each with its own glyph instance and label text. They are Toggle instances now (Size=default, Variant tracking the group, middle segment Pressed=true), exposed for per-segment editing, with the end radii overridden 6/0/0/6 and 0/6/6/0 and the parent's -1 gap left alone to collapse the borders.
rebuilt.geometryUnchanged: 118x36 horizontal and 40x106 vertical, before and after — verified by measurement, not by eye.
rebuilt.propsRemoved: Label 1 / Label 2 / Label 3 / Show labels / Show icons. Per-segment values live on the nested Toggle instances now; a set cannot own a TEXT property that points into a nested instance.
rebuilt.instancesRepaired: 17 instances survive the rebuild. 14 wanted icon-only and match the new default. The 3 that showed text were re-set through their exposed toggles: Dashboard 1105:245 and 1107:22233 (Weekly/Monthly/Yearly) and Page 95 I1306:7159;503:61;1306:7395 (Summary of data / Full data set / Full data set) — the last of which is nested three instances deep, and was only reachable BECAUSE of the exposure.
rebuilt.noteVsCode: ToggleGroupItem is not a <Toggle> in code — it is a <button> wearing .ui-toggle, reading pressed from the group's context. Figma has no equivalent of 'reuses a stylesheet', so instancing Toggle is the only way to keep one source of truth for the item's visuals. The Overview prose already explains the code side; do not 'correct' one to match the other.
rebuilt.openFollowUp: The Spec frame is still 'orientation x variant' with no sizes strip — the size pill was corrected to '32 / 36 / 40px' but the v4 convention wants a sizes strip under the header. Small build, not done.
rebuilt.sizeAxis: Added 2026-08-25. Orientation x Variant x Size (sm|default|lg) = 12 variants, built by cloning the four Size=default variants and setting each nested Toggle's Size. Group-level, not per-segment, because code passes size to every item — per-segment sizes could disagree and would teach a control the code cannot build. Horizontal 100/118/154 wide x 32/36/40 tall; vertical 34/40/52 x 94/106/118. All 23 existing instances resolved to Size=default with zero missing-variant errors. The set is a horizontal auto-layout, so it needed layoutWrap='WRAP' to hold 12 cells inside the 1216 column.

ButtonGroup.themingFrame: ABSENT — every token ButtonGroup itself reads is neutral (--border, --secondary). Stated in TOKENS. The colour in the examples belongs to the child Buttons, which do theme.
ButtonGroup.props: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) = 2. Deliberately no Style/Size axis — those belong to the child Buttons, not the group.
ButtonGroup.notes: Three components, mirroring the three exports: ButtonGroup (2 variants), ButtonGroup/Separator (Orientation, 2) and ButtonGroup/Text (1). The root models ONLY orientation because that is its only prop — adding a style axis would have repeated Badge's variant/category mistake of offering choices the API does not have. Spec is 'anatomy x orientation' rather than 'matrix x states': the group is a div with role=group and has no states of its own, so the table breaks down seam treatment by position (first/middle/last), orientation, the two drawn parts, and the focus lift. Shipped WITH a code fix — see the ButtonGroup entry in git history.
openQuestions: role="group" has no accessible name and nothing enforces one; consumers must pass aria-label. Same gap as ToggleGroup.
ButtonGroupText is a <div>, not a <label>, so a visible 'Sort by' cell is not programmatically tied to the buttons.

On the solid default style the focus ring is --primary-focus — the fill colour at 40% alpha — so where it crosses a neighbouring solid button it is invisible even with the z-index lift. Fixing it means changing Button's focus token globally, not ButtonGroup. Ring reads fully only on transparent-fill styles.
ButtonGroupSeparator exposes role="separator" to AT; aria-hidden may be more honest where it is decorative.

Card.themingFrame: ABSENT — Card is neutral chrome; nothing in it reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Card.props: NO variant axis. One assembled `Card` COMPONENT with TEXT props (Title, Description, Body) and BOOLEAN props (Show description, Show header action, Show footer), plus Card/Header, Card/Body and Card/Footer as standalone region specimens. `interactive` is modelled as code-only: it has NO resting appearance, only cursor + hover/focus, which are drawn in Spec.
Card.newTextStyle: base/leading-5/Semibold (16/20) — created for the card title; base/leading-normal is 24 and base/leading-none is 16.
Card.notes: First Phase 3 page. Deliberately NOT a variant set: the only prop that could be an axis (`interactive`) looks identical at rest, and this file's convention (set by Button) is that states live in the Spec table, not as variants. Region components exist because a Figma instance cannot take children, so a designer building a custom card needs the three parts separately. Spec is 'anatomy x states'. Ships with a code fix — the interactive card now carries the system focus ring. | 2026-08-08: gained CardMedia. Also note a SLOT conversion does not report its new type within the SAME use_figma call — the node still reads FRAME and only reads SLOT on the next call. Verify conversions in a fresh call or you will conclude, wrongly, that it failed. | [1.2 — 2026-08-26] Three findings from an owner review, all Figma-only. (1) Card/Media had been sitting LOOSE ON THE CANVAS since it was added on 2026-08-08 — outside every frame, ZERO instances, and not named anywhere in the page prose; the COMPONENTS section said "One assembled Card, plus each region on its own" and listed three. Nothing looked broken because the assembled Card already carried Show cover and a ui-card__media slot, so cover support was wired and only the standalone master was stranded. Adopted into a fourth region cell, captioned, and the section copy now names it. (2) The region components read as ONE borderless card. They are correctly borderless — in code the border belongs to .ui-card and a region owns only its own hairline — but they are --card surfaces on a --card panel, so their edges were invisible. Each now sits on its own bounded stage. Note --background and --card are BOTH #ffffff in light, so a fill alone would have done nothing; the hairline is what draws the boundary. (3) The "grid of equal cards" example was neither equal nor buildable: at 180px the title had 56px left after padding, the leading icon and the Live badge, so Figma broke words mid-way and the cards came out 108 / 124 / 124. Widened to 220 — titles on one line, all three 108.
openQuestions: CardHeader generates `${id}-title` on its heading but nothing in the library references it — it exists for a consumer to point aria-labelledby at.
CardBody and CardFooter take no `id` prop, unlike Card and CardHeader — inconsistent with hard rule 6, probably deliberate since they are layout-only.
overflow:hidden clips any menu/popover/tooltip opened inside a card; those need a portal.
CardHeader always renders an <h3>; the level is not configurable, so a card can produce a heading order that does not match its document position. Still open after the media addition.
Card.slots: FIVE slots: ui-card__media (NEW), ui-card__header-media, ui-card__header-action, ui-card__body, ui-card__footer — on the assembled Card and on each region component. All are React.ReactNode in code. Title/Description/Body stay TEXT props.
Card.codeChange: CardHeader gained `media?: React.ReactNode` (2026-07-26). Card was the only one of the four media families without a leading slot — ItemMedia, EmptyMedia and AttachmentMedia already existed. Driven by the Figma side: a whole-header slot would have let a designer draw a featured icon no developer could build.
Card.cardMedia:
ADDED 2026-08-08, code first then mirrored — the playbook's own rule, and the same route that produced CardHeader.media.

THE TWO MEDIA ROLES ARE NOT THE SAME THING, and conflating them is what made this confusing. ui-card__header-media is a LEADING visual on the title's own line — avatar, status dot, featured icon. It can never be a cover: in CSS it is flex-shrink:0 inside the header's flex row, icon-sized, floored at one line of title. ui-card__media is the full-bleed COVER.

It is a sibling PART, not a `media` prop on Card, because a prop must choose an order; as a part the caller can place the cover above the header, between header and body, or last.

Code composes AspectRatio at a default 16 / 9 so a grid keeps a level top edge and nothing shifts as images load. It declares NO radius — .ui-card is overflow:hidden, so a cover touching an edge inherits the rounding; adding one shows as a hairline of card background in the corners.

Figma: "Show cover" BOOLEAN defaults to FALSE, so no existing Card instance grew a cover when the property landed. Card/Media (1233:25901) is the standalone region component.
Card.exampleFix: The mid-word break was the important half. .ui-card__title has no word-break, so a browser would wrap "Engineering" whole or overflow — never Engine/ering. The example was showing a rendering no developer could produce, which is the same class of error as a hand-drawn example, just harder to spot because the node WAS a real instance.

dividerAxis.summary: Show divider was promoted from a BOOLEAN to a Divider variant axis. The set is now 10 variants: Size(default|sm|lg|xl|2xl) x Divider(on|off). A boolean could only hide the rule; the axis also carries the collapsed spacing, so the Figma card finally matches the CSS.
dividerAxis.ownership: The HEADER owns the gap (padding-bottom 16, or 12 at sm) and the body takes padding-top 0 — matching the code, and keeping the body slot uniform on all four sides in both divider states.
lessons: clone() ON A COMPONENT STRIPS EVERY componentPropertyReference IT OWNS. This is the big one, and it cost a scare: the five Divider=off variants were made with clone() + appendChild, and each came out with 4 references instead of 16. The 4 survivors all belonged to NESTED components (Badge/Button/Code Label props); every reference to Cards own properties — Title, Description, Overline, the Show* booleans, the slot bindings — was gone. Nothing errors and the variant looks perfect on canvas, because the clone keeps the literal text it was cloned with. combineAsVariants does NOT do this; clone() does.

The symptom is a variant that ignores setProperties. A fresh instance of the broken variant accepted Title=... , reported it back correctly from componentProperties, and rendered the master demo text. Property VALUES live on the instance; without a reference no node consumes them. Test a new variant by reading back the rendered characters, never the property value.

Switching pre-existing instances onto a reference-stripped variant empties them. Eight live cards on the Whats New page lost their entire body-slot content — bullets, footers, badges, cover — and reverted to the master demo. It was fully recoverable by switching the variant back, which restored every override, but nothing warned before or during.

Repair is a node-for-node copy of componentPropertyReferences from the matching on-variant, matched BY PATH not by index — one xl clone had 23 nodes to the originals 24 (a nested Code instance internal), so an index zip silently skipped that whole variant.

ONE reference cannot be restored: `Cannot set component property references on slot sublayer`. The Body text sits inside the ui-card__body SLOT, so the Body TEXT property does not drive the off-variants default body copy. Authoring in the Figma UI can do it; the plugin API cannot. Irrelevant to any card that puts real content in the slot, which is all of them.

Verify a migration with an exact comparison. A first pass compared a full rendered title against a 34-character truncation of the property value, declared failure, and reverted a card that had in fact migrated cleanly. The check was wrong, not the migration.

mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.what: `CardHeader` gained a `mediaPlacement` prop in CODE (`leading` default | `above`). It has NO Figma variant axis, and cannot be given one by plugin.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.why: THE PLUGIN API CANNOT CREATE OR RESTORE A SLOT. There is no figma.createSlot and no node.convertToSlot (accessing it throws). `variant.clone()` silently converts every SLOT descendant to a plain FRAME — verified: a clone of `Size=xl, Divider=off` came back with ui-card__header-media and ui-card__header-action as FRAMEs while the source had SLOTs. Ten cloned `above` variants would therefore have shipped with all four slots dead, and an instance switched to them loses every slot with no error.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.alsoExplains: Near-certainly the origin of the broken `Divider=off` half found earlier the same day — five variants with frames where the originals had slots. The owner repaired them in the Figma UI during the session.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.reverted: The axis was built, screenshotted, found broken and fully reverted. Card is back to 10 variants on Size × Divider with all four SLOTs intact on every one — verified by re-reading every variant's children types.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.manualStep: To mirror `mediaPlacement`, author the `above` variants BY HAND in the Figma UI: duplicate each variant, add a VERTICAL `ui-card__header-stack` frame inside ui-card__header, move ui-card__header-media and ui-card__header-content into it (gap 16 bound to spacing/4, counterAxisAlignItems MIN, media minHeight cleared, content layoutSizingVertical HUG — a moved child gets reset to FILL and collapses to 1px), and re-make the slots. Leave the action and the absolutely-positioned divider as siblings of the stack.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.secondBugFixed: `showDivider={false}` zeroed a following CardFooter's padding-top but not the footer's own border-top, so the hairline sat flush against the footer's first line. Fixed in Card.scss; code-only, no Figma change.
mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked.bodyIsAStretchColumn: .ui-card__body is a flex column with default align-items: stretch, so a Button dropped straight in fills the card and centres its label. Neither CardBody nor CardFooter gives a left-aligned hugging action row — CardFooter is the dialog-shaped bar (right-aligned, own rule). OPEN: whether CardFooter should take an alignment prop.

partsExposed2026_08_31.why: CardHeader is prop-driven and expresses ONE arrangement; every new layout had cost another prop (media, then mediaPlacement). Of 40 call sites outside Card.stories.tsx, 18 used CardHeader — all the same trivial title + description — and 22 bypassed it: 7 stat cards (the header makes `title` the biggest text; a stat wants a small label over a big value), 4 pricing cards (a Badge BESIDE the title, not pinned right), 3 icon-above-title, 4 legitimately headerless.
partsExposed2026_08_31.code: Five new exported parts — CardTitle, CardDescription, CardOverline, CardVisual, CardActions. CardHeader's API is UNCHANGED and now renders those same parts internally, so the preset cannot drift from them. Matches the model Item/Empty/Attachment already use; Card was the library's only hybrid.
partsExposed2026_08_31.whyItWasCheap: The size cascade was already part-based — `.ui-card--sz-xl .ui-card__title` is a DESCENDANT selector, so a part picks up the card's ramp wherever it sits, body slot included. Nothing had to be rewired.
partsExposed2026_08_31.titleProps: `as` (default h3) closes the hard-<h3> openQuestion — a stat card's biggest text is a VALUE, and marking 1,284 as an h3 puts a number in the document outline. `scale` renders the title at another CardSize's type WITHOUT moving padding; that does not contradict 'size lives on Card', which exists because PADDING must move together across regions. Rules are `.ui-card__title.ui-card__title--scale-*` — doubled class on purpose, since the size cascade is (0,2,0) and a single modifier would lose to it.
partsExposed2026_08_31.cssGotcha: CardVisual needs `align-self: flex-start`. `.ui-card__body` is a flex column with the default `align-items: stretch`, so without it the inline-flex box spans the card and its own `justify-content: center` parks the glyph in the middle. Same root cause as the Button-fills-the-body trap that CardActions now fixes.
partsExposed2026_08_31.classSplit: `.ui-card__header-media` was split: the generic tile styling moved to `.ui-card__visual`, and `__header-media` keeps ONLY the `min-height: var(--leading-5)` floor, which is true of the header ROW and wrong when the visual is stacked. CardHeader renders `<CardVisual className="ui-card__header-media">` so the element carries both — which keeps the Figma slot name `ui-card__header-media` and preview/layout/card.html valid.
partsExposed2026_08_31.figma: Five atom components added to the Overview `parts` frame — Card/Title (1845:873), Card/Description (1845:876), Card/Overline (1845:880), Card/Visual (1845:37030), Card/Actions (1845:37042). PLAIN COMPONENTS WITH NO SLOTS, so the plugin can build them — the constraint that blocks a mediaPlacement variant axis does not apply here. Title/Description/Overline were cloned out of the assembled Card's own text nodes so text styles and fill bindings are exact; Visual and Actions hold exposed instances (FeaturedIcon, Button ×2 with a `Show second` boolean).
partsExposed2026_08_31.figmaWhyItMattered: The four region components had ZERO instances between them. A designer composing inside a body slot had no typography atoms to drop in and hand-drew text instead — the same gap on the design side that the code side had.
partsExposed2026_08_31.mediaPlacementBug: SHIPPED BROKEN AND FIXED THE SAME DAY. Card.tsx emitted `ui-card__header--media-above` while Card.scss authored the block one nesting level too high, compiling to `.ui-card--media-above` — a class nothing carries. The stack fell back to block layout that looked close enough to pass both a screenshot and a left-edge measurement. Verified fixed by reading the COMPILED selector and measuring the 16px stack gap, not by looking at the render. The generalisable guardrail: compare every `ui-x--mod` literal in the .tsx against the .scss.
partsExposed2026_08_31.duplicateIds: Card and CardHeader each apply their own `id`, and 21 call sites passed the same string to both — two elements with one id. All disambiguated to `{id}-header`. CardHeader putting its id in the DOM was a deliberate fix for audit bug #11 and was NOT reverted.
partsExposed2026_08_31.migrated: 5 of the 22 bypasses moved onto the parts as proof: MarketingPage (icon-above-title, now CardVisual + FeaturedIcon, deleting 8 inline style properties), DeeperTheming + DeeperThemingV2 (same shape), ConsoleDashboard + DashboardHandoff (stat cards → CardOverline + CardTitle as="p" scale). 17 remain, plus the local Card shim shadowing the real component at src/foundations/Overview/Overview.stories.tsx:39.

`overflow: hidden` clips a menu or popover opened inside a card; needs a portal.
Whether CardFooter should take an alignment prop now that CardActions covers the leading-aligned case.

textStyleRepair2026_08_31.trigger: Cloning the overline into the new Card/Overline atom surfaced an unstyled text node in the assembled set. A page-wide scan found not 1 but 34 — every title, description, body and overline in the SIZE variants, not just the overlines. Only the original Size=default, Divider=on kept its styles.
textStyleRepair2026_08_31.cause: Same root as the componentPropertyReference stripping already recorded under dividerAxis: the size and divider variants were produced by clone() and then restyled by setting fontSize/lineHeight literals, so they never carried a textStyleId.
textStyleRepair2026_08_31.method: MATCH BY EXACT VALUE, NEVER BY NAME. Applying a text style overwrites fontSize, lineHeight, fontName AND letterSpacing, so a style picked by its plausible name can silently change the render. Each node was matched on all four properties together and only applied on an exact hit; width and height were measured before and after every application. 32 matched, 0 drift.
textStyleRepair2026_08_31.newTextStyle: lg/leading-6/Semibold (18/24) created for the two remaining nodes — the Card title at size lg. The lg rung ships leading-none (18) and leading-normal (28); neither is 24. Exactly the situation that produced base/leading-5/Semibold for the default rung, and named the same way. Applied with 0 drift.
textStyleRepair2026_08_31.result: ZERO unstyled text nodes on the Card page. Fills, strokes, layer names and component descriptions are also at zero.
textStyleRepair2026_08_31.stillOpen: CLOSED — see paddingRepair2026_08_31 below. The 88 unbound padding values were bound in the same pass.

paddingRepair2026_08_31.what: Every unbound padding and gap inside the Card component set is now bound: 92 padding values + 10 itemSpacing values across the 10 variants, plus the set wrapper's own 16px padding on all four sides. Zero unmapped, zero drift, zero remaining.
paddingRepair2026_08_31.cause: The same clone-derived loss as the text styles. The size and divider variants were produced by clone() and their padding re-set as literals, so they carried no variable binding — ui-card__header / __body / __footer at 12, 16, 20, 24 and 32.
paddingRepair2026_08_31.method: MATCH BY RESOLVED VALUE, not by name. A value→variable map was built by reading each spacing/* variable's number out of the Primitives collection's only mode, and a binding was applied ONLY where the node's current number matched exactly. Every variant's width and height was snapshotted before and after; all ten were byte-identical, which is the proof that binding changed no geometry.

Binding them is a file-wide convention decision, not a Card one.

dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.question: Why does a Page 102 card show Divider=on but render no divider?
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.answer: The `divider` is a RECTANGLE **inside** ui-card__header, not a sibling of the regions. These cards set Show header=false, so Figma drops the header from the instance entirely — the instance's only region is ui-card__body and the header node is ABSENT, divider included. Correct, and it matches code: showDivider is a CardHeader prop painting border-bottom on .ui-card__header, and a card with no header has no divider.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.theMisleadingPart: The axis lives on **Card** while the code prop lives on **CardHeader**, so it stays selectable and assertive on cards that have no header. The panel says `on` while nothing renders.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.theTrap: Setting it to `off` to make the panel honest is WRONG and was tried: all four cards lost 24px (222 → 198). The Divider=off variants bake `padding-top: 0` into ui-card__body UNCONDITIONALLY — measured [0, P] against the on variants' [P, P] at every size. In code that zeroing is an ADJACENT-SIBLING rule, `.ui-card__header--no-divider:not(:last-child) + .ui-card__body`, conditional on a header actually preceding the body; Figma has no adjacent-sibling concept, so the variant bakes it in. On a headerless card the body is the FIRST child and code would keep its full padding.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.rule: ON A HEADERLESS CARD, USE Divider=on. It is the only variant whose body keeps its top padding, even though the name suggests otherwise. Reverted and verified: 222 tall, body padding-top 24.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.secondDiscrepancy: CORRECTED. My first reading — 'code zeroes both the body and the footer, Figma only zeroes the body' — was WRONG. The rule is `+ .ui-card__body, + .ui-card__footer`, an ADJACENT-SIBLING selector, so it collapses only the region DIRECTLY after the header. Measured in the browser against the compiled CSS: with a body present the footer keeps padding-top 16px and a 1px border-top; remove the body and the footer goes to 0 and none. So Figma's Divider=off is CORRECT for header+body+footer, the common shape, and a blanket 'zero the footer' change would have introduced a new bug in it. The real gap is one configuration only: Show body=false with a footer, where code collapses the footer and Figma does not. Documented on the set rather than baked, because no single value is right for both shapes.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.properFix: The axis is modelling a CardHeader prop at the Card level, which is what makes it both misleading and unconditional. The faithful model would put it on Card/Header — which needs the header to be its own component set, and a slot-bearing set cannot be rebuilt by plugin (see mediaPlacementFigmaBlocked). Owner call, hand-authoring required.
dividerAxisOnHeaderlessCards.codeCommentFixed: The no-divider block's own comment claimed 'the body slot keeps a uniform padding on all four sides whether the divider is on or off', which the rule three lines below contradicts — it sets the body's padding-top to 0. Rewritten to state what the code does and why the adjacent-sibling selector is load-bearing, with the measured footer numbers and a pointer to this entry.

partScaleAxes2026_08_31.what: Card/Title, Card/Description and Card/Overline each gained a `Scale` VARIANT axis (sm|default|lg|xl|2xl), mirroring the ramps .ui-card--sz-{size} produces for each part.
partScaleAxes2026_08_31.whyFigmaNeedsIt: THE CENTRAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO SIDES. In code the ramp is a DESCENDANT selector, so a part picks up its host card's Size wherever it sits and needs no prop. A Figma component cannot inherit anything from the instance that contains it, so without an explicit axis the atoms were frozen at the default rung and unusable inside any other card size.
partScaleAxes2026_08_31.ramps: Title: sm 14/20, default 16/20, lg 18/24, xl 20/28, 2xl 30/36, all Semibold. Description: sm 12/16, default and lg 14/20, xl and 2xl 16/24 (lg has no override in code, so it equals default). Overline: 12/16 at sm/default/lg/xl, stepping to 14/20 ONLY at 2xl. The four identical Overline rungs are deliberate so one Scale value can be set across all three parts together.
partScaleAxes2026_08_31.codeParity: `scale` exists as a prop on CardTitle only in code. CardDescription and CardOverline get their type from the card's `size` cascade, which Figma cannot reproduce — so the Figma axis is WIDER than the code prop on those two, by necessity. Stated in each set description.
apiLessons: combineAsVariants DOES NOT MERGE SAME-NAMED COMPONENT PROPERTIES. Combining five components that each declare a `Text` TEXT property yields `Text` AND `Text2` on the set, with the original variant on one and the clones on the other. Unify by re-pointing every variant's componentPropertyReferences at the property the ORIGINAL variant uses — that is the one existing instances are bound to — then deleteComponentProperty the orphan.
clone() strips componentPropertyReferences, confirmed a third time. Each clone had to re-add its TEXT (and, on Overline, its BOOLEAN) property before combining.

node.children.indexOf(someNode) RETURNS -1. The children array hands back fresh proxies each access, so reference equality fails; insertChild then throws 'Cannot insert node at a negative index'. Use children.findIndex(c => c.id === node.id).
Keep the ORIGINAL component as one of the variants rather than rebuilding all five — its instances survive the conversion and land on that variant. Card/Title kept 12 instances, Card/Description 8.

Item.themingFrame: ABSENT — Item is neutral chrome; nothing reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Item.props: Item: VARIANT Variant (default|outline|muted) x Size (xs|sm|default) = 9. Item/Media: Variant (default|icon|image) x Size = 9. Item/Separator: 1 component. TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description/media/actions/header/footer; SLOT media/actions/header/footer, each with preferredValues + description. href / onClick / disabled are code-only — they change the ELEMENT, not the look.
Item.slots: FIRST page built slots-first. header and footer are PURE slots with NO text property — ItemHeader/ItemFooter take children: React.ReactNode in code, not a string. Title and description remain TEXT props because they are genuinely strings.
Item.notes: The row is a CSS GRID (grid-template-areas: header spans / media-content-actions / footer spans). Figma has no grid, so each variant nests an auto-layout row named 'row — media · content · actions'; identical render, stated on the page. Ships with a code fix — grouped rows now collapse touching borders and the focused row lifts to z-index 1, the third component to need that after ToggleGroup and ButtonGroup.
openQuestions: ItemGroup is role="list" and ItemSeparator role="separator", but the rows are NOT role="listitem" — the list is announced with no matching item count.
The actions slot sits inside the row, so if the row is a link or button anything interactive in actions is a nested interactive. Nothing prevents it.
Title is nowrap+ellipsis and description clamps to 2 lines, both with no title attribute — truncated text is unavailable to hover and to assistive tech alike.
disabled sets pointer-events: none, so a disabled row cannot show a tooltip explaining why.

Attachment.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome plus the error family; nothing reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Attachment.props: Attachment: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) x Size (xs|sm|default) = 6. Attachment/Media: Variant (icon|image) x Size (xs|sm|default|vertical) = 8. TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description/media/actions; SLOT media + actions with preferredValues and descriptions.
Attachment.axisDecision: `state` is deliberately NOT a variant axis, following the Spinner precedent of adapting axes with a stated reason. It has 5 values but only 3 renderings — idle==done, uploading==processing (shimmer only), error is the single real repaint. Five near-identical variants would have been noise; the five are laid out as a row in Spec instead and the reasoning is on the Overview.
Attachment.notes: Parallel family to Item. The interesting technique is the two-layer overlay: __trigger is position:absolute inset:0 at z-index 1 so the whole card is clickable, __actions sit at z-index 2 so buttons are not swallowed, and isolation:isolate on the root keeps both out of the page stacking context. Neither layer is drawable (a transparent overlay renders as nothing) so Spec specifies rather than mocks it. Content is NOT a slot — see lessons.
openQuestions: `state` drives colour and a shimmer only; nothing is announced. A screen reader is told nothing when a file goes uploading -> done. Needs the state in the description text or a consumer-supplied aria-live region.
A card with a trigger plus three actions is four tab stops.
AttachmentTrigger's accessible name is entirely whatever children the consumer passes into the sr-only span; an empty trigger announces as a blank link the size of the card. Nothing enforces it.
Attachment.codeChanges: Three fixes shipped with this page: the error description no longer fades to 3.68:1 (last component applying o-80 to semantic text); AttachmentGroup is a keyboard-reachable scroll region; and the action button's hit target expands to 24x24 at xs. That last one exposed that CloseButton, AttachmentAction and the Chat composer tools had each hand-rolled the same shell, so `.ui-icon-button` was extracted to src/styles/icon-button.scss and all three now sit on it.

Collapsible.themingFrame: ABSENT — reads no colour beyond --foreground on the root. Stated in TOKENS.
Collapsible.props: VARIANT State (closed|open) = 2. EVERY prop is code-only: open/defaultOpen drive the one visual axis, onOpenChange and disabled have no resting appearance — a disabled Collapsible looks exactly like a closed one, because the disabled styling belongs to whatever Button was passed to the trigger.
Collapsible.notes: Spec IS the three-layer clip — that is the whole component. Ships with a code fix: the third clip layer was missing.
openQuestions: CollapsibleTrigger clones its child with `disabled`. Give it a non-button element and React warns about an unknown DOM attribute; nothing in the types prevents it.
`disabled` has no root-level styling — a disabled Collapsible is visually identical to a closed one. Consumers who care must style off data-disabled themselves.

Accordion.themingFrame: ABSENT — reads only neutral tokens. Stated in TOKENS.
Accordion.props: Accordion/Item (410:70): VARIANT State (closed|open|disabled); TEXT Label (all variants) and Content (State=open only); BOOLEAN "Show divider". Accordion (1533:686): VARIANT Rows (3|4|5|6|7|8) = 6 variants, each a stack of EXPOSED Accordion/Item instances with the last row's divider already off. type / collapsible / value / defaultValue / disabled / headingLevel stay code-only; Rows and "Show divider" are Figma-only.
Accordion.notes: NO code change — the component was already sound: three-layer clip, inert-when-closed, roving arrow-key focus (Up/Down + Home/End, disabled triggers skipped), single/multiple modes, all verified in the browser. Modelled as Accordion/Item (the repeating unit with the visual decisions) plus assembled 3-item lists drawn from mkItem, since the divider hairline is per-item (removed on the last). Shares Collapsible's grid-rows clip; the page cross-references it rather than re-explaining. | [1.1 — 2026-08-26] Audited by asking the designer question directly: could someone build an FAQ for a help page with this? No. The page proved it against itself — ALL SEVEN accordions on it were hand-drawn geometry, including the one labelled "an FAQ", because the component could not produce them. The item had NO properties beyond State (a question could not be typed from the panel) and NO divider at all, so a stack of real instances ran together with no hairlines. Only 3 instances existed file-wide, none on the doc page. Fixed: added Label / Content / "Show divider"; rebuilt all 28 hand-drawn items as instances (7 example containers, 6 Spec state cells, 1 anatomy row); named the Overview assembly "Accordion — template (copy me)" and gave it a 4th row. Instances 3 -> 32. The container is an EDITABLE TEMPLATE FRAME, not a component — same call as Sidebar menu, Chat transcript, TabBar bar and Table. | [1.2 — 2026-08-26] CORRECTION TO 1.1. Shipping only an editable template frame was wrong for this component. Owner asked why the Accordion was not in the Assets panel; the answer is that ONLY COMPONENTS APPEAR THERE — a FRAME never does, whatever it is named — so a designer searching "Accordion" still found nothing but the item. The Sidebar/Chat/TabBar/Table precedent was over-applied: those lists are UNBOUNDED and HETEROGENEOUS (a sidebar menu mixes menu buttons, sub-buttons, group labels and separators), whereas an accordion is a HOMOGENEOUS list of one atom at a realistic 3–8 rows. The constraint that forced those into frames barely binds here. Added a real Accordion component set on the ToggleGroup model — Rows 3–8, 33 exposed nested Accordion/Item instances, verified on a PLACED instance: all rows reachable, per-row State/Label/Content/Show divider editable, nothing detached, and resizing the accordion to 600 carried through to row, wrap and divider. The template frame stays as the stated escape hatch for >8 rows.
openQuestions: The trigger is a <button>, not a heading — the component makes no assumption about heading level, so a document that needs an outline must wrap the AccordionTrigger in its own <h3>.
A full-width trigger's 3px focus ring exits the container on both sides; fine standalone, but a consumer who wraps the Accordion in an overflow:hidden card will clip it left and right.
Accordion.figmaOnlyProp: "Show divider" (BOOLEAN, default true). The code removes the hairline with a :last-child rule, which Figma cannot express, so the last item in a stack turns it off by hand. There is no showDivider prop in React — the set description says so.
