Icon is a LucideIcon prop with a per-variant default; the Figma set draws the default but does not model icon-swap (no INSTANCE_SWAP) — a designer changing the icon detaches.

actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.found: Owner flagged the Alert CTA in the Banner preview as looking wrong. Measured: the action button's text bound to Brand `primary-text` (35:65) and its stroke to Brand `primary-border` (2:49) — BOTH THEME.
actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.codeDoesTheOpposite: Alert.scss rebuilds the WHOLE --primary-* family on `.ui-alert__action` from --primary-main, which no [data-theme] scope remaps, precisely so an Alert reads as its own control rather than competing with the page CTA. The rule is scoped to the action slot, not .ui-alert, because the `brand` variant reads --primary-light/-text/-border on the SURFACE and is meant to follow the theme.
actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.whyItHidSoLong: On the main brand (Slate) the themed path and the primary-main path resolve to the SAME value — measured #d2dbe5 text and #cbd5e1@40% stroke either way. So the mirror looked correct and would only have diverged the first time someone viewed an Alert under a brand, at which point every product's warning would wear a different colour. A binding check catches this; a screenshot never would.
actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.figmaHadNoTokens: There were NO primary-main variables in Figma at all. Created two Mode-collection variables holding the resolved values of the CSS color-mix steps Figma cannot express: text/primary-main-text (VariableID:1983:44, light #2e3b4f / dark #d2dbe5 = 85% primary-main + 15% foreground) and surface/primary-main-border (VariableID:1983:45, primary-main at 40% alpha). Rebound across all 12 Alert variants.
actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.instanceOverrideGotcha: The master rebind reached the STROKE on existing instances but not the TEXT FILL: editing the button's label earlier had left an override on that text node, and an override wins over the master. Had to rebind the instance directly. After changing a master, re-read the instances you have already customised — the fix does not necessarily reach them.
actionButtonNeverThemed2026_09_01.openDesignQuestion: Separate from the binding bug: the action is deliberately NEUTRAL slate inside a semantic alert. On a warning tint a grey outline button can read as disconnected or disabled. Whether an Alert's action should instead take the alert's own semantic colour is an owner decision that CLAUDE.md currently answers as 'neutral'.

actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.question: Owner: shouldn't the Alert's action just be a warning button? The rationale in Alert.scss only argues against BRAND theming — it never argues neutral over SEMANTIC, and semantic tokens never theme either, so the owner's instinct was not covered by the existing reasoning.
actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.panel: PROPOSAL — Alert action treatment (1988:1884) on Page 102 at 1312,2512. Three options x three severities (warning/error/info), dark mode, labelled as a proposal and carrying its own measurements.

measuredDark.A neutral outline (ships today): label vs button 8.12-8.63 PASS · button fill vs alert 1.13 · BORDER vs alert 2.69-2.75 — FAILS the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a component boundary. The border is the ONLY thing defining the button, so the control has no perceivable edge. The owner's 'doesn't look right' is a real failure, not a preference.
measuredDark.B semantic outline: label vs button 4.37 (error) to 6.89 · edge vs alert 1.89-2.51 — WORST of the three. Border and tint share a hue, so matching the alert is exactly what erases the button.
measuredDark.C semantic solid: label vs button 6.45-10.79 PASS · fill vs alert 4.91-7.76 PASS. The only option where the button is a perceivable component in all three severities.

actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.recommendation: C. It is the only treatment that clears both bars. Caveat recorded on the panel: a solid red chip on an error alert could be read as a destructive action, though the dark label (#0f172a on the fill) keeps it reading as a chip rather than a danger button. If that is a problem the answer is probably a distinct treatment for destructive actions, not a retreat to outline.
actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.notYetChecked: LIGHT MODE. All figures are dark-on-card. The semantic tints and the neutral both move in light, so the ranking may not hold and must be re-measured before any code change.
actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.ifAdopted: Changing this touches .ui-alert__action in Alert.scss for every variant, and would make the primary-main rebuild there partly redundant — the action would take --{variant} rather than --primary-main. The Figma text/primary-main-text and surface/primary-main-border variables created today would stay useful for any other never-themed control, but Alert would stop being their consumer.

measuredLight.A neutral outline (ships today): boundary vs alert 2.07-2.08 — FAILS 1.4.11, and WORSE than dark's 2.69-2.75. Its label contrast is the HIGHEST of any option at 11.32, precisely because the button is invisible: the fill is opaque white on a 6% tint (1.09) with a 2.08 border, so you get crisp dark text with no discernible control around it. That reads as a link, not a button.
measuredLight.B semantic outline: boundary vs alert 1.55-1.61 — worst in both modes. Border and tint share a hue; matching the alert is what erases the button.
measuredLight.C semantic solid: fill vs alert 4.72-5.37, label on fill 5.18-5.49. Passes in all three severities. Light is the TIGHTER case (dark runs 4.91-7.76 fill / 6.45-10.79 label) but still clears both bars.

actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.conclusion: Light does not just preserve the ranking, it strengthens it: A and B are both WORSE in light than in dark, and C is the only treatment clearing the 3:1 component boundary and AA on its label in every severity and both modes. The caveat on the panel has been replaced with the measured result; both a DARK panel (1988:1884) and a LIGHT twin (1992:2026) now sit side by side on Page 102.
actionTreatmentComparison2026_09_01.worstCase: C light warning — fill 4.76, label 5.18. That is the number to protect if the semantic light hues are ever re-tuned.

optionD.added: Owner did not want C's loudness and asked whether A is passable as-is. It is not — A presents a bordered button whose boundary measures 2.07-2.08 light / 2.69-2.75 dark against the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 requires. So a fourth option was added to both panels.
optionD.whatItIs: D — identical to A in colour, weight and fill; the ONLY change is the border alpha, 0.40 -> 0.60.
optionD.measured: Edge vs alert: light 2.07 -> 3.24, dark 2.70 -> 4.21. Clears 3:1 in both modes across all three severities. Nothing else moves.
optionD.recommendation: D. It resolves the conformance failure at the smallest possible cost and keeps the neutral, quiet treatment the owner wants. C stays on the panel as the option with the most headroom if an Alert action ever needs to be unmissable.
optionD.theOtherQuietOption: Not built: making the action a GHOST or LINK button — no border at all. With no drawn boundary there is nothing for 1.4.11 to fail, and the label alone carries it at 8-11:1. Rejected as the recommendation because CLAUDE.md already records the owner's call that a ghost button on a floating surface 'reads as non-interactive' (the Toast carve-out), and the same objection applies inside an Alert.
optionD.ifAdopted: One line in Alert.scss: the --primary-border step in the .ui-alert__action rebuild changes from color-mix(--primary 40%, transparent) to 60%. It stays scoped to the action slot, so no other consumer of --primary-border moves. The Figma surface/primary-main-border variable (1983:45) would need a matching 0.60 value, or a second variable if 40% is still wanted elsewhere.

SHIPPED.what: Option D shipped 2026-09-01 in CODE: Alert.scss, the --primary-border step inside the .ui-alert__action rebuild goes from color-mix(--primary 40%, transparent) to 60%. Nothing else changed — colour, weight and fill are identical.
SHIPPED.verified: Read back live in a browser at both modes: the declaration resolves to color-mix(in srgb, #334155 60%, transparent) in light and #cbd5e1 60% in dark, and the WithAction story renders correctly in both with no console errors. tsc clean, hex guardrail clean.
SHIPPED.figmaMirror: surface/primary-main-border RENAMED to surface/alert-action-border and moved to 0.60 in both modes. The rename is deliberate: at 60% it is no longer the generic --primary-border step, it is specifically the alert action's border, and a generic name would invite someone to reuse it as a 40% token. All 12 Alert variants were already bound to that variable id, so the master picked the value up with no rebinding.
SHIPPED.panelsBecameADecisionRecord: The two comparison panels were retitled 'DECISION — Alert action treatment · D shipped 2026-09-01' and A/B/C captions marked REJECTED, with their measurements kept. A panel still labelled 'not shipped' containing the shipped option would have been false; deleting it would have thrown away the evidence for why three alternatives lost.
SHIPPED.standingFollowUp: test:contrast gates 71 TEXT-on-surface pairings and nothing else. Three components failed WCAG 1.4.11 today (Switch track 1.4:1, Tabs indicator 1.72:1, Alert action border 2.07:1) and all three passed every automated check. Adding non-text boundary pairings to scripts/contrast-check.mjs is the open follow-up.
SHIPPED.preExisting: The 2 failures the suite reports (error on error-light 4.3:1, error on error-soft 4.07:1, both under specific theme+tint combos) are unrelated and predate this work — no error token is touched anywhere in the working tree.

Banner.themingFrame: PRESENT — brand variant only, same rule as Alert. The theme grid shows full-bleed brand bars across all 9 codes.
Banner.props: VARIANT Variant (default|brand|info|success|warning|error) = 6 (NO style axis, unlike Alert). TEXT Title, BOOLEAN Show icon. Icon, action, onClose and `centered` are code-only. `centered` is a LAYOUT mode (caps content at --max-w-5xl + centres), not a boolean-toggleable property, so it is shown in Examples not modelled as an axis. role derived: alert for error/warning, status otherwise.
Banner.supersedes: Parked pre-v4 Banner set 15:90 DELETED from page 14:60. Both parked sets (Alert + Banner) now retired; the migrate page 14:60 is empty.
Banner.notes: NO code change — the page-level cousin of Alert, verified sound. Full-bleed: a BOTTOM hairline (border-bottom-color) instead of Alert's all-round border, no radius, spans 100% width. Reuses Alert's semantic tint tokens verbatim (do not fork them). No muted description — the whole message takes the accent colour, AA-gated the same way. __close sits OUTSIDE __inner so it stays right-pinned when centred. Same THEME-collection binding for brand as Alert.
openQuestions: A Banner mounted at page load with role=alert (error/warning) announces immediately — intended for an outage bar, but a designer must not set a marketing message to error/warning or it interrupts on load.
`centered` cannot be a Figma property (it changes layout, not visibility); shown in Examples only, so an instance cannot be toggled to centred — a designer wanting it detaches or rebuilds.

Empty.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome; nothing reads --primary. The example Button themes on its own, the Empty container never does. Stated in TOKENS.
Empty.props: VARIANT Media (default | icon) = 2 — the one visual axis (EmptyMedia's variant). TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description / Show action; SLOT media + content. Everything is children in code — Empty has no props of its own beyond EmptyMedia's variant. Static, no interactivity.
Empty.notes: NO code change — a clean static compound. Centred column, generous --p-12 vertical padding, header capped at --max-w-sm. icon media = a --w-12 --muted tile at --rounded-xl; default = an unboxed --w-10 glyph. The tile uses --muted (not --secondary) because it is an image surface carrying an icon, the same call Item/Attachment make. Modelled with Media as the variant axis; the icon and the action row are slots.
openQuestions: Empty is a plain <div> with no role — correct for a presentational block, but when it replaces a live region (a search-results list) the announcement must happen on that region, not here. Nothing enforces it.
The description is capped in Figma at a fixed 250px width; in code it is --max-w-sm (384) and wraps fluidly. The fixed width is a Figma approximation, not the code cap.
Empty.fixNote: 2026-07-27: the icon media tile rendered 48x32 (a wide blob) not 48x48. Cause: after converting ui-empty__media to a SLOT, a blanket layoutSizingVertical='HUG' pass (meant to clear stale slot heights) collapsed the height to hug the 24px glyph while the width stayed pinned at --w-12. Restored to a fixed 48x48 square, both axes bound. Empty was the ONLY slot affected — Item/Attachment media slots hold square Media INSTANCES, so hugging them stays square; Empty's slot held the tile styling directly.

Progress.themingFrame: PRESENT — the DEFAULT variant themes (indicator reads --primary), recoloured across all 9 codes; semantic variants keep their own hue.
Progress.aiden: YES — first Phase 3 component with an aiden gradient. The default determinate bar's indicator takes the violet→blue gradient under data-surface=aiden, built with the dark-overlay pattern (aiden-dark-gradient rect, visibility bound to flag/is-dark 175:26). Plus a completion particle burst (aiden-gated, not drawable). Documented in a dedicated AIDEN SURFACE card, since the flow + particles are animated.
Progress.props: VARIANT Variant (default|success|warning|error|info) × Size (sm|default|lg) = 15, laid out as a 5-row × 3-col grid (manual positioning after combineAsVariants). value/max/indeterminate/valueFormatter are code-only; label + showValue are header shortcuts.
Progress.notes: NO code change — the July a11y sweep already wired aria-labelledby to the rendered label via useId. Track --muted, indicator --primary (or variant colour), heights --h-1/-2/-3. The set cells are bare track+indicator (header shown once in anatomy) to keep the 15-grid tight. indeterminate is a 40% sliding bar with NO aria-valuenow — shown as its resting 40% frame, not drawable. value text uses tabular-nums.
openQuestions: Naming: `label` auto-wires aria-labelledby, but the compound API or a label-less bar needs a consumer aria-label — an unnamed progressbar announces only 'progress bar, 62%'.
The set cells omit the header row for grid density; a designer wanting the label+value composes it (shown in anatomy and examples) rather than toggling a property.

FeaturedIcon.themingFrame: PRESENT — the `default` colour reads --primary and is recoloured across all 7 brand modes. Was documented as the `brand` variant until 2026-08-31.
FeaturedIcon.props: VARIANT Color (20: default + success|warning|error|info + the 15 CategoryColor hues) × Shape (square|circle) × Size (default|sm|lg) × Appearance (soft|solid) = 240 variants. `default` IS --primary and follows data-theme — there is no `brand`. Icon + label stay code-only; the glyph is a nested Icon/* INSTANCE and is swappable per instance.
FeaturedIcon.newComponent: YES — 58th component, added 2026-07-27. Extracted from the boxed icon-tile pattern hand-rolled in Empty, Item and Attachment media. Owner requested it after spotting the Empty tile. Index board got a new FeaturedIcon row (444:289).
FeaturedIcon.notes: Reuses Alert/Badge -light tint tokens, no new tokens. Icon is half the box at every size (16/20/24). Square radius scales md/lg/xl; circle is full. brand binds to Theme collection like Alert/Banner. Follow-up chip spawned to consolidate Item/Attachment/EmptyMedia tiles onto it.
FeaturedIcon.composedBy: WHERE FeaturedIcon should appear as a composed element / slot preferred value: Empty (icon media — code composes it; slot pref + uses-inside updated 2026-07-27), Card (ui-card__header-media slot — pref added 2026-07-27). TODO when built: Dialog + AlertDialog (a featured icon atop a confirmation — especially a red error tile for destructive confirms), ChatGreeting (centered featured icon on the start screen). Wire FeaturedIcon into those header/greeting areas + their slot preferredValues when their pages are built.

colorAxis2026_08_31.why: An owner-supplied chooser screen needed a violet tile. The six semantic colours could not express one — `brand` resolves to neutral slate on the main brand, so two of four tiles rendered identically. Same class of gap Badge closed with its category hues.
colorAxis2026_08_31.shape: ONE set with a 21-option Color axis, NOT a separate FeaturedIcon/Category set. The two-set rule is for MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE props (Badge's `variant` vs `category`, where one overrode the other); here it is a single widened prop, so a second set would fork one axis in two.
colorAxis2026_08_31.notBadgesTwoAxes: Badge refactored to `color` × `appearance` because its variant list was a colour × fill cross-product. FeaturedIcon has exactly ONE treatment (tint + soft border + coloured glyph), so a flat colour list is the whole surface. A flat list only becomes wrong when there is a fill axis to cross it with.
colorAxis2026_08_31.newVariables: 15 `category/{hue}/border` COLOR variables created in the Mode collection (VariableID:1825:44 … 1825:58), scopes copied from status/info/border = ['STROKE_COLOR']. Light 0.3 / dark 0.4 alpha of the hue, matching the semantic `-border` step. Mirrors the new --category-{c}-border tokens.
colorAxis2026_08_31.bindings: Per category variant: tile fill → category/{hue}/bg, tile stroke → category/{hue}/border, glyph path-1 STROKE → category/{hue}/text. The glyph carries its colour as a STROKE on the inner VECTOR, not a fill — check that before rebinding an icon anywhere in this file.
colorAxis2026_08_31.cloneLesson: `variant.clone()` does NOT materialise the clone's INSTANCE children within the same use_figma call — a findOne for the glyph VECTOR returned nothing immediately after cloning and found it on the next call. Bind tile fills in the clone pass, then sweep the glyph strokes in a second call.
colorAxis2026_08_31.prose: Page prose updated in the same pass per the standing rule: the meta pill (12 → 126 variants), the `variant` token pill, two section titles, two labelled separators, the theming caption and the Do card now say `color` and mention the category family. Set description rewritten.
colorAxis2026_08_31.lint: Not re-run over the whole page — the 90 new variants are clones of an all-zeros master with only variable-bound fills/strokes changed.

appearanceAxis2026_08_31.why: The owner spotted that `default` was filled while nothing else could be. It was worse than a two-way split: `default` was an OPAQUE --muted whose border resolved to the same value (a solid chip with no edge), the five semantic colours were a 6% tint with a 30% ring, and the category hues a 10% tint. Three treatments, none of them selectable.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.correction: This reverses the call recorded in colorAxis2026_08_31 that FeaturedIcon had no cross-product to express. It had one; it was just hidden inside the `default` colour rather than exposed as an axis. The lesson generalises: before concluding a component has a single treatment, MEASURE every option's computed background — the odd one out will not be visible in the token names.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.model: Badge's exact mechanism. Each color class publishes --_fill/--_on-fill (solid) and --_soft/--_soft-ink/--_soft-line (tint); the appearance class consumes one pair.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.figmaBindings: solid: tile fill → surface/muted | primary | status/{x}/base | category/{hue}/base; tile STROKES REMOVED (a Figma stroke does not contribute to frame size, so this keeps 40x40 without a transparent stroke); glyph path-1 stroke → text/muted-foreground | primary-foreground | status/{x}/foreground | category/foreground.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.breaking: appearance defaults to `soft`, so every existing tile with no explicit color changes from the solid slate chip to a soft neutral tint. `Color=default, Appearance=solid` reproduces the old tile.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.codeGotcha: Empty.tsx HAND-WRITES the ui-featured-icon class list rather than composing the component, so it silently rendered unpainted until an appearance class was added there too. Grep `ui-featured-icon` across .tsx before changing this component's classes.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.screen: The four tiles on Page 102 were set to Appearance=soft so all four read as the same object; General Request no longer sits heavier than its neighbours.
appearanceAxis2026_08_31.prose: Meta pill 126 → 252, two section titles now say 'fills', set description rewritten around the two axes.

brandRemoved2026_08_31.why: Owner's call: a neutral `default` plus a themed `brand` is two ways to say one thing. Badge had already settled the model — one `default`, and it themes.
brandRemoved2026_08_31.what: `default` took the whole --primary family verbatim (the brand variants' paints were COPIED onto the default variants rather than re-derived, so parity is exact) and the 12 `Color=brand` variants were deleted. 252 → 240 variants, Color 21 → 20 options.
brandRemoved2026_08_31.instanceMigration: 16 brand instances existed — 15 on the FeaturedIcon page (theming grid, both spec tables, the anatomy shape row, both example callouts) and 1 on `Billing — handoff`. All were moved to Color=default BEFORE deletion, and the delete pass re-checked `instances.length` and would have thrown rather than orphan one.
brandRemoved2026_08_31.apiLesson: `ComponentNode.instances` EXISTS and returns instances across every page, loaded or not — no findAllWithCriteria sweep and no loadAllPagesAsync needed. This is the way to answer 'what breaks if I delete this variant?' in a file whose pages load lazily.
brandRemoved2026_08_31.consequence: There is no neutral colour left in the set. A tile that must stay slate inside a themed subtree has to say so itself. In code, EmptyMedia variant="icon" emits --default, so every empty state now themes and its unthemed tile went from an opaque --secondary to the 6% --primary-light.
brandRemoved2026_08_31.prose: Nine text nodes and five layer names on the FeaturedIcon page rewritten off `brand`, including the Theming section title and caption, both spec-table cell labels and both example callout labels. Frame `Spec — size × shape × variant` renamed to `… × color`.

iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.note: Owner: the FeaturedIcon in Figma had no way to change the icon. Correct: the set carried Color x Shape x Size x Appearance and nothing else, so the glyph was whatever its variant shipped with and the only way to change it was to detach the instance or reach in with swapComponent from a plugin. SUPERSEDES this entry's `props` line, which says 'Icon + label stay code-only'; Icon is now a real Figma property. The ledger is append-only, so that line is left as written rather than edited.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.evidence: Two checks decided the shape of the fix rather than taste. (1) src/components/FeaturedIcon/FeaturedIcon.types.ts declares `Icon: LucideIcon` as a REQUIRED prop with no default and no per-colour default, so the master's per-colour glyphs were a Figma-only invention. (2) Every other set in the file that exposes an icon swap carries exactly ONE glyph across all its variants: Badge (Icon/check, Icon/x), Button (Icon/plus, Icon/arrow-right), Button/Icon-only (Icon/plus). FeaturedIcon was the only set with per-variant glyph defaults.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.change: Normalised the 48 semantic variants (success/warning/error/info) from circle-check / triangle-alert / circle-alert / info to Icon/inbox so all 240 variants share one glyph, then added `Icon` as an INSTANCE_SWAP property on the set (key Icon#2576:0, default 312:19472 Icon/inbox, no preferredValues, matching Badge and Button) and bound every variant's glyph layer via componentPropertyReferences.mainComponent. 240 bound, 0 failures.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.tradeoff: Choosing a semantic Color no longer changes the glyph for you: Color and Icon are now set together. This is forced, not chosen. Verified on a scratch instance that a swapped glyph SURVIVES a variant switch, which is the whole point of a property and also means per-variant defaults cannot coexist with it. It matches the code, where the icon is always passed explicitly.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.safety: All 121 instances were censused before the change (Admin Flow 31, Request Flow 43, FeaturedIcon page 44, Card 3) and re-verified after. 22 drifted and were repaired to their recorded glyph: 20 on the doc page's semantic spec rows and 2 on Request Flow (R7.1 and R7.1a's success tiles). Every one of the 22 had INHERITED its glyph from a semantic variant; not a single manual swap override was lost, so message-square, bell, layout-grid, lightbulb and flag all survived untouched. Final mismatch count 0 on all four pages.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.docs: Set description documents the property and the Color/Icon pairing. The Overview anatomy note gained 'In Figma, Icon is an instance-swap property on every variant'. Changelog row 1.4 added. While there, row 1.3 was BACKFILLED: the ledger recorded version 1.3 as the 2026-08-31 colour/appearance rebuild but that change never got a row, so numbering this one 1.3 would have collided. The backfilled row says on its face that it was recorded late.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.apiLessons: ComponentNode.instances per variant is the way to census a variant set cross-page, but an instance living on an UNLOADED page reads back with no reachable ancestors and no children, so its glyph reads null: 32 of the 121 looked like phantoms until each page was censused separately under setCurrentPageAsync. Also, direct child traversal (variant.children[0].children) reaches inside a component-set variant even though findAll does not, which is what made binding all 240 possible.
iconSwapProperty2026_09_07.openNotFixed: 62 unbound itemSpacing values across the four FeaturedIcon doc frames, all pre-existing doc chrome on layout frames, none on anything added here (verified node by node). The Tier 4 sweep bound padding and radius; set- and frame-level itemSpacing on doc pages was left, and Badge and Button/Icon-only carry the same unbound set-level gap. Out of scope for this fix and not swept, since fixing one page of many would be inconsistent.

Tabs.themingFrame: 1430:179 — ADDED 2026-08-26. Was absent, and the page said so on purpose: every surface was neutral. The `line` variant changed that — its active-tab bar is --primary. `default` and `browser` still do NOT theme (their active surfaces are --background and --card, which no brand scope remaps), and the frame says so rather than implying the whole component moves.
Tabs.props: HOST: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) x Variant (default|line|browser) = 6; TEXT Panel; BOOLEAN Show tab 3 / Show tab 4 (bound to the trigger INSTANCE, the container, not a leaf). ATOM Tabs/Trigger: VARIANT Variant (default|line|browser) x State (active|inactive) = 6; TEXT Label; BOOLEAN Show icon; INSTANCE_SWAP Icon. All 24 nested triggers are EXPOSED. value/defaultValue/onValueChange/activationMode remain code-only.
Tabs.notes: NO code change — full WAI-ARIA tab pattern verified: roving tabindex (active=0, rest=-1), arrow + Home/End, automatic (arrow selects) vs manual (Enter/Space selects), focusable tabpanel. Active trigger is a lifted --background pill with --shadow-sm on a --muted list; inactive --muted-foreground. The trigger COLOUR is deliberately NOT transitioned (only bg+shadow) to dodge the Chromium var()-freeze on a live mode switch — documented on the page. | [1.1 — 2026-08-26] Variant axis added and the tablist track moved off --muted onto --accent, mirroring a real code fix: --muted-foreground triggers on --muted measured 5.1:1, the pairing CLAUDE.md forbids and the one the 2026-07-21 sweep moved five other surfaces off — Tabs was simply missed. --accent is 6.92:1 in light and identical in dark (both resolve to the same slate). Variant is presentation only. `Orientation=vertical, Variant=browser` deliberately renders the LINE treatment because browser is horizontal-only and Tabs.tsx resolves that pair to line — the cell mirrors the code fallback instead of leaving a variant hole (which would render a broken instance) or inventing a vertical browser tab. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY EYE, and fixed in BOTH code and Figma: (1) the browser panel overflowed its border after padding was added, because the content frame held a stale explicit height — resize() first to clear it, THEN re-assert hug, or setting AUTO alone silently does nothing; (2) the browser list hairline and the panel border-top sat flush and stacked into a 2px rule under the inactive tabs — the list hairline was dropped, the panel border IS the strip rule, and the active tab seam masks exactly that pixel. | [1.2 — 2026-08-26] THE SET HAD NO NON-VARIANT PROPERTIES AT ALL — owner reported it. Triggers were hand-drawn FRAMEs with an empty componentPropertyReferences, so a designer could not rename a tab, change how many there were, or pick which one was active without detaching. Fixed the way ToggleGroup was on 2026-08-25: extracted a Tabs/Trigger atom (which mirrors the real TabsTrigger export) and nested EXPOSED instances. Chose exposure over an Active variant axis deliberately: an axis would have been 6 x 4 = 24 host variants and would have locked the strip at exactly four tabs. The accepted cost, already accepted for ToggleGroup, is that a nested override does not survive a host Variant switch — flipping default->line resets which tab was marked active. Trigger padding now matches the CODE per variant (default 6/12, line 6/2/10, browser 8/16); the page had used a uniform 6/12 for every variant, which was a parity gap introduced when line and browser were added earlier the same day. iconInheritanceTrap.symptom: Owner: 'you fixed that for the text but the icons can't be switched in figma.' Correct — after the pill went light in dark, the active tab's label was #0f172a but its ICON still rendered #f8fafc, 2.45:1 on the #94a3b8 pill.
iconInheritanceTrap.myFalseClaim: I had reported rebinding 'fill, label and glyph stroke' on Variant=default, State=active. The glyph stroke was NEVER rebound: `master.findAll(n => n.type === 'VECTOR')` returns ZERO on a component-set variant — the playbook's own 'the API can't reach instances nested inside component-set variants' rule. The loop ran over an empty array and reported success. A write loop that finds nothing must be treated as a failure, not a no-op.
iconInheritanceTrap.whyOverridesCannotWork: Even if the vectors were reachable, a stroke override is discarded by an INSTANCE_SWAP — which is exactly what the Icon property does. In CODE this is a non-issue: lucide renders stroke='currentColor', so the glyph follows the label for free. The gap is Figma's alone.
iconInheritanceTrap.fix: Pinned the `icon` INSTANCE inside Variant=default, State=active to Mode=LIGHT via setExplicitVariableModeForCollection. Modes CASCADE and are not overrides, so the pin survives a swap — verified on a fresh instance swapped to a glyph the master had never carried: renders #0f172a. In light mode the pin is a no-op.
iconInheritanceTrap.theDependencyToWatch: This works because --tabs-indicator-foreground (#0f172a) happens to equal light-mode text/foreground, which is what the pinned icon resolves to. If those two ever diverge, the icon drifts silently and nothing will flag it. It is a stand-in for `currentColor`, not a real binding.
iconInheritanceTrap.apiGotcha: instance.children OMITS hidden children, so `Show icon` must be set to true BEFORE looking for the `icon` child — the first attempt at this test silently pinned nothing. A COMPONENT's children do include hidden ones, which is why the master could be pinned directly.

lessons: MODE IS NOT A VARIANT, and collapsing it needed a new primitive. Light and dark glass differ in GEOMETRY and paint-stack LENGTH (light = top-anchored white sheen over one radial highlight; dark = bottom-anchored ink sheen over a lift plus a bottom-right occlusion, spark 12% -> 8%), so no colour variable can carry it. Solved with whole layer stacks glass-light / glass-dark gated on flag/is-light and flag/is-dark. flag/is-light (VariableID:1197:44) was ADDED for this, the exact inverse of flag/is-dark. Generalises the aiden-dark-gradient overlay pattern from one layer to a pair. Verified against the POC set in both modes before the POC was superseded.
Three mode-dependent layers were FRAME FILLS, not children, so they had to be extracted into rectangles before they could be gated. A paint cannot have its visibility bound; only a node can.

A TRUNCATED STYLE ID FAILS SILENTLY. The first build passed 26-char slices of the text style ids (sliced for display in an earlier read) to setTextStyleIdAsync. Nothing threw, the text rendered in a plausible default, and only the design-check lint caught it — 8 TEXT nodes with no textStyleId. Real ids are 40+ chars WITH a trailing comma.
Blend (hard|soft) on the POC set was never a prop: hard is the six brands' 3-stop ramp, soft is aiden's 4-stop plateau — the data-surface scope expressed as a variant.

AN AMBIENT SCOPE THAT FIGMA CANNOT MODEL AS A COLLECTION BECOMES AN OPAQUE GATED OVERLAY, not a variant. Mode and the aiden surface are the same shape of problem — something the code reads from context rather than from a prop — and they now have the same shape of answer: a layer that covers, gated on a boolean. Variants are for props.

NEVER CONSTRUCT A STYLE ID — fetch it. This page cost two failures to the same root cause: a 26-char slice kept for display was passed to setTextStyleIdAsync (silent, text rendered in a plausible default) and later a full id was GUESSED by extending a truncated one (loud, "Cannot find style", script failed atomically). Real ids are 40+ chars and end in a comma. The loud failure was the cheap one.

A COMPONENT PROPERTY PREFIX CAN BE AMBIGUOUS. _Doc/DoDont exposes "Do#146:7" and "Dont#146:8"; matching with startsWith("Do") hits BOTH, so setting Do and then Dont wrote twice to the same key and the Do side silently kept its default copy. Match on the part before "#". Caught by reading the rendered characters back rather than trusting the write.

resize() RESETS SIZING MODES. The four doc frames were created with primaryAxisSizingMode "AUTO" and then resized to set their width, which silently flipped them back to FIXED — every frame sat at its placeholder 400px height with content overflowing invisibly. Set the mode AFTER the resize.

iconLibrary.source: Generated from node_modules/lucide-react@1.24.0 in this repo — the SAME package the components import at runtime, so the Figma set cannot drift from what the code can render. Regenerate after a lucide upgrade; never hand-add icons.
iconLibrary.naming: Icon/{kebab} exactly as lucide names them (Figma 'circle-alert' = React CircleAlert).
iconLibrary.geometry: 24x24 masters at stroke-width 2 (lucide's native geometry). CRITICAL: lucide's stroke-width is in VIEWBOX units, so in the browser it scales with the icon — 12px renders 1.0px, 14px 1.167px, 16px 1.33px, 20px 1.667px, 24px 2.0px (measured in Storybook, not derived). Figma does NOT scale stroke on resize, so any instance placed below 24px must have its stroke set to 2 x size / 24 or it looks like a blob. Button/Icon-only carries the correct value per size. CloseButton is the carve-out: its CSS pins stroke-width to --icon-border-width (1.33 units) so at 12px it renders 0.665px.
iconLibrary.colour: Stroke bound to color/foreground; a host component (Button, Alert) overrides it, mirroring `color: inherit` in CSS. 25 icons have FILLED shapes (chart-scatter dots etc.) — those fills are bound too.
iconLibrary.aliases: 249 lucide aliases (alert-circle -> circle-alert, home -> house) deliberately EXCLUDED — duplicate geometry under an old name, and two identical entries in a swap list is worse than one findable one.
iconLibrary.licence: Lucide is ISC. The notice lives in node_modules/lucide-react/LICENSE; each component description records its lucide name and licence.
iconLibrary.pipeline: Do NOT paste icon data through the conversation — 353 KB of markup. Generate one SVG with each icon in <g id='{name}'> (the id becomes the Figma layer name), upload via the upload_assets tool + curl, then convert the imported groups to 24x24 components in chunks of ~450 (about 85ms each).
iconLibrary.layerNaming: Every icon's inner layers are uniform — a 'glyph' group over 'path-1', 'path-2', … — and this is load-bearing, not tidiness. Figma matches instance overrides BY LAYER NAME, so uniform names are what let a swapped icon keep the stroke colour and weight its host component set. Per-glyph names ('plus-1') silently reset both on every swap.
iconLibrary.strokeWeightMechanism: Collection 'Icon' (VariableCollectionId:291:32), modes 24/20/16/14/12, variable icon/stroke-weight. lucide's stroke-width is in VIEWBOX units, so the rendered value is 2 x size / 24. At 24/16/12 that lands exactly on the existing Primitives tokens, so those three modes ALIAS them: 24 -> icon-border-width/lg (2), 16 -> icon-border-width/default (1.33), 12 -> icon-border-width/sm (1). Modes 20 (1.667) and 14 (1.167) are intermediates of the same ratio with no token of their own — the code expresses this as a ratio, not a set of constants, so inventing tokens for them would be backwards. All ~6,971 icon vectors bind strokeWeight to the variable; each Button/Icon-only variant sets its size mode; the Icons page grid is pinned to mode 16 so the library displays at 1.33, the system's most common icon weight.
iconLibrary.warning: NEVER type a raw stroke weight on an icon in the Figma UI — it DETACHES the variable binding. That happened on 2026-07-25 (all 6,971 vectors detached to a flat 1.33) and had to be rebound. Change the MODE, not the value.
iconLibrary.swapGuidance: Change a glyph via the component's Icon / Leading glyph / Trailing glyph PROPERTY, not by selecting the nested icon layer and swapping it in the right panel. Both keep the 24x24 sizing, but a direct layer swap DROPS the strokeWeight variable binding (verified 2026-07-25), so the icon silently stops tracking the size mode.
iconLibrary.colourDurability: RESOLVED / was a mis-diagnosis. I previously recorded that an INSTANCE_SWAP discards the icon's stroke colour. Re-tested 2026-07-25 on Default/Default/Default, Error/Ghost/Small and Aiden/Default/Default, for both the icon-only set and the labelled Button's leading slot: swapping via the PROPERTY preserves the bound stroke colour AND the bound stroke weight in every case. The broken instances I originally measured had been damaged by my own swapComponent() rewire step, not by the property mechanism — I diagnosed the mechanism from wreckage I had created. The real, still-true caveat is narrower: swapping the nested icon LAYER directly (right panel, with the layer selected) drops the strokeWeight binding. Use the property.
iconLibrary.colourModel: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-25: icons do NOT auto-tint. They arrive as --foreground and the designer sets the colour after placing. Automatic per-variant tinting was attempted five ways and abandoned: (1) per-layer stroke overrides — only reach layers present on the DEFAULT swap target, so a richer glyph rendered half-tinted; (2) a variable-mode colour collection — Figma caps a collection at 10 modes and 13 icon colours are needed; (3) empty path-2 stubs so an override had somewhere to land — verified not to carry through a swap; (4) manual vectorPaths concatenation to force one path — CORRUPTED all 1,746 icons (see lesson) and forced a full rebuild; (5) figma.flatten + re-sync — geometry survived but the nested instances inside component-set variants became unreadable to the API. Stroke WEIGHT is unaffected and remains variable-driven and correct.
iconLibrary.apiCaveat: The plugin API cannot reliably read or write the subtree of an instance nested inside a COMPONENT-SET VARIANT — findAll() returns 0 vectors for 238 of 240 slots even though they render correctly on canvas. Only the set's DEFAULT variant is reachable. Page-level instances are fully reachable. Any per-variant nested styling must therefore be applied at instance-creation time, before the instance is inserted into the variant.

page102ConsistencyPass2026_09_01.groupingThresholdWrittenDown: Groups with labelled separators appear at roughly SIX or more fields, or when fields fall into three-plus genuinely distinct domains. page102ConsistencyPass2026_09_01.apiGotcha: Array.prototype.indexOf on a node from findAll against parent.children returns -1: the plugin API hands back DISTINCT PROXY OBJECTS for the same node, so identity comparison fails silently and insertChild then throws 'Cannot insert node at a negative index'. page102Confirmation2026_09_01.what: 'Request submitted — confirmation' (2008:1859) at x=10256 — the shared outcome screen for every request type. Cloned from an existing screen so the shell is identical by construction: same width, padding, 672 content cap, heading pattern, Card Size=xl and submit bar.
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.whyAScreenAndNotAToast: Someone has just filled up to eleven fields and the request has entered a review queue they do not control. A toast disappears in four seconds and leaves them staring at a form that may still hold their data. The screen carries the four things a toast cannot: a reference they can quote, what happens next, where updates appear, and where to go now.
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.communicationIsSingleChannel: OWNER CONSTRAINT: all communication about a request lives on the My requests page and nowhere else — no email, no Slack. That drove three decisions: the PRIMARY action is 'View my requests' (solid, trailing arrow) rather than 'Back to Dartboards'; an info Alert states outright 'You won't get an email — this is the only place updates appear'; and no copy anywhere promises a notification. If the only channel is a page, the confirmation has to push people to it and say so, or they will sit waiting for a mail that never comes.
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.composition: FeaturedIcon Color=success + circle-check · title 'Request submitted' · subtitle carries the reference (DR-2026-0417) · Card with a label/value summary (Request type, Dashboard, Submitted, Status) where Status is a Badge Variant=warning-soft reading 'Pending review' · info Alert · bar with 'Reviewed within 2 business days.' plus [View my requests] and [Submit another].
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.nextBuild: This screen is the hand-off point to the My requests page, which is the next build. The reference, the status pill and the review-time promise made here all have to be honoured there.
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.lintCheckBugFound: MY OVERFLOW CHECK HAD A FALSE POSITIVE. It added itemSpacing to every horizontal frame's required width, but Figma DROPS itemSpacing when a frame is SPACE_BETWEEN (already recorded in the playbook for Card's header). The submit bar therefore reported 696 needed against 672 available — a phantom overflow exactly one gap wide. Corrected: gaps count as 0 when primaryAxisAlignItems === 'SPACE_BETWEEN'. It had not fired before only because every other bar's contents were narrow enough to absorb the phantom 24px.
page102Confirmation2026_09_01.realFindingUnderneath: With the check corrected, one genuine finding remained: the status row hugged to its 20px label while the Badge inside it is 24px, so the badge overflowed the row's cross axis. Fixed by letting the row hug vertically. Worth noting the sequence — a broken check masked a real defect by making every run look equally bad.
openForNextTime: No FAILURE state exists for submission. Every screen draws a success path; if submit can fail, that state needs drawing too.
No 'review before submit' step. For an eleven-field form whose own copy warns that custom wording is reviewed more slowly, a confirm step may be worth it — or this screen's summary may be enough.

page102FailureState2026_09_01.what: 'Promote Dashboard — submission failed' (2011:1906) at x=11448 — the recovery state, built on a form that was READY to submit so every entered value is visibly intact.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.theStructuralPointSuccessVsFailure: Success REPLACES the form, because there is nothing left to do. Failure must NOT, because there is everything left to do. A full-page failure screen would throw away up to eleven fields of typing, which is a far worse outcome than the failure itself. So the failure state is the same form, unchanged, with an error Alert as the last item in the card and the submit action still live.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.onlyServerSideFailuresArePossible: A consequence of an earlier decision worth noticing: because submit stays DISABLED until every required field is complete, client-side validation failure cannot occur here. The only reachable failures are server-side — outage, permission, duplicate, expired session — which is why the copy talks about 'our end' rather than asking the user to check their input.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.copy: Title 'We couldn't submit your request'. Description: 'Something went wrong on our end — nothing was sent. Everything you entered is still here, so you can try again. If it keeps failing, quote error SUB-503 to the DART admin team.' Three jobs in three clauses: what happened, that nothing was lost, and how to escalate.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.retryIsTheSameAction: No separate 'Try again' button. Retrying IS submitting, so a second affordance beside 'Submit for Review' would imply two different actions. The alert explains; the existing button recovers. The bar note changes to 'Nothing has been submitted yet.' so it cannot read as a confirmation.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.gapWorthRaising: The error tells people to quote SUB-503 to the DART admin team — but the OWNER'S RULE is that all request communication lives on My requests, and a request that failed to submit never reaches My requests. So the one path this error needs has no channel behind it. Either failures need a fallback contact stated on this screen, or failed attempts need to appear on My requests as a draft the user can retry from.
notBuilt: A conflict/duplicate variant ('there is already an open request for this dashboard') — a different shape, because the recovery is to VIEW the existing request rather than retry.
Session-expired, which is an app-level concern rather than a form one.
page102FailureState2026_09_01.lint: All 20 frames on Page 102: 0 findings on all eight checks, using the corrected SPACE_BETWEEN-aware overflow rule.

page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.chooserAligned: The chooser was the one screen that did not share the form shell: 192px gutters giving 688 of content, and Cancel bottom-LEFT while every form puts it bottom-RIGHT. It now has the same 64px gutters, the same `content column` capped at 672, and a `submit bar` with Cancel right-aligned. Option cards went 336 -> 328. It is the first and last screen in the flow, so it was the worst place to break the pattern.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.submittingState: 'Promote Dashboard — submitting' (2015:2029) at x=12640. Submit takes isLoading with the label 'Submitting…', Cancel is disabled, all four controls are set Disabled, and the note reads 'Sending your request — don't close this page.' This was the highest-risk gap in the flow: without it a slow submit looks like a dead button, people click again, and duplicate requests land in the admin queue. Button already shipped `isLoading`; nothing new was needed.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.readyStatesCompleted: Add (2016:2148), General and Feature now each have a ready-to-submit frame, so every branch shows both ends of its enable rule. Add deliberately fills ONLY its seven required fields and leaves the four optional ones empty — that is what makes the rule legible rather than just showing a full form. Feature likewise leaves Business impact empty.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.dirtyTabSwitchAlreadyCovered: The owner asked for a 'you are about to lose all progress' warning on tab switch. It already exists — the alert dialogs block carries 'Discard your changes? / Switching request type clears the form. The details you've entered won't be saved.' with [Keep editing] [Discard changes]. NOT yet covered by any dialog: switching the standard-vs-custom RADIO on the Banner form after typing a custom message, which destroys the same kind of work for the same reason.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.emptyDataStateDropped: Owner: dashboards will always exist. The empty-picker state raised in the flow review is closed, not deferred.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.apiGotchaFirstFindAllOnAClone: THE FIRST findAll ON A FRESHLY CLONED + APPENDED NODE MISSES. Observed three times in a row: on Add the entire first loop returned nothing while the second loop found everything; on General and Feature the FIRST key of each loop missed and every later key resolved. The node names and property keys were verified correct in between, so this is not a naming bug. Treat the first query after clone()+appendChild as unreliable — re-query, or touch the tree once before relying on it. A script that fills fields in one pass will silently skip its first field.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.lint: All 24 frames on Page 102: 0 findings on all eight checks.
page102FlowReviewFixes2026_09_01.submitIconRemoved: Owner: drop the paper-plane glyph from Submit. Agreed and removed from all 19 Submit buttons across the flow. The reasoning: a paper plane means SEND — a message flying to a person — but this files a request into a review queue; nothing is sent to anyone. The label 'Submit for Review' is already unambiguous, it is the only primary action on the screen so the icon aids neither scanning nor disambiguation, and for most of the flow it sat at 50% opacity on a disabled button, i.e. pure decoration. Contrast with the TAB icons, which were kept: there the icons distinguish four peer options in the screen's primary navigation, which is where an icon earns its place. The submitting state is unaffected — its spinner comes from Button's own isLoading, not from the leading-icon slot, and still renders. The confirmation's 'View my requests' keeps its TRAILING arrow, which is doing a different job: signalling that the action leaves this screen.

page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.problem: The screens were clean and lint-verified, but roughly fifteen behavioural decisions lived only in conversation and this ledger. A developer opening a 24-frame canvas had no entry point, no sequence, and three handoff notes covering about a fifth of what had been decided. The risk was never the pixels.
page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.built: A documentation column at x=-1400, to the LEFT of the flow so it reads first: ① START HERE (2021:2462) · ② BLOCKERS & PREREQUISITES (2022:2462) · ③ BEHAVIOUR SPEC (2023:2500) · ④ FLOW MAP (2024:2500) · ⑤ ALERT DIALOGS (the existing block, renamed and moved in). Screens continue to run left to right from x=120.

Third: `Filled` on Input/Textarea is Figma-only and must not be mirrored as a prop. Fourth: the full 21-component inventory, so nobody builds something custom.

Eleven entries covering activationMode, the dirty-form gates, why only server-side failures are reachable, the note-states-the-blocker rule, Banner type locking, 'All of Dartboards' exclusivity, blank start date, blank Edit field, the single communication channel, the 768 stacking breakpoint, and a Still-open list.

page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.decisionPanelsMissing: The two 'DECISION — Alert action treatment' panels are NO LONGER on the page and there is no record of deliberately deleting them. The decision itself is safe — shipped in Alert.scss and recorded above — but the A/B/C/D comparison and its measurements are gone from the canvas. Flagged to the owner rather than silently rebuilt.
page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.looseTextNode: A loose TEXT node holding the standard-messages brainstorm sits directly on the page canvas, outside any frame. Owner's, left alone.
page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.apiGotcha: textAutoResize='HEIGHT' pins a text node's WIDTH and only lets it grow downward, so a label meant to hug its text wraps mid-word instead. Every step box in the flow map rendered as 'Dashbo/ard' and 'Ad/d' until the labels were switched to WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT. Use HEIGHT for paragraphs, WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT for chips and labels.
page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.lint: All 27 frames on Page 102: 0 findings on all eight checks.
page102HandoffPackage2026_09_01.bannerRadioDialogAdded: The fourth dialog now exists: 'Discard your custom message? / Switching to a standard message replaces what you've written. Your custom title and message won't be saved.' with [Keep editing] [Discard and switch]. It closes the gap the behaviour spec had flagged — the Banner standard-vs-custom radio destroys typed work exactly as a tab switch does. sectionsForNavigation.why: 24 frames in columns communicated the flow only through x/y position. Sections give the canvas a table of contents: they name each stage, appear in the layers panel, and let a developer collapse a branch they are not building.
sectionsForNavigation.sections: 0 · DOCUMENTATION (5) · 1 · CHOOSE (1) · 2 · DASHBOARD REQUEST — four modes behind Tabs (10) · 3 · BANNER / NOTICE (4) · 4 · GENERAL REQUEST (2) · 5 · FEATURE REQUEST (2) · 6 · OUTCOME — shared by every branch (3). 27 frames, none left loose.
sectionsForNavigation.columnsReorderedToMatchTheChooser: Banner had been sitting AFTER General and Feature, contradicting the order the chooser presents (Dashboard, Banner, General, Feature). Columns were moved so the canvas reads in the same order a user meets them, and the three outcome screens were pulled onto one row as submitting → confirmation → failed.
sectionsForNavigation.gotchaSectionPadding: Building each section from its members' bounding box plus 64px of padding made every adjacent pair OVERLAP, because the columns sit 120px apart and 64+64 exceeds that. Figma does not prevent this and overlapping sections are hard to select in. Fix: create the sections from content bounds, then lay them out left to right with an explicit gap (200px), which also lets a section carry its children with it.
sectionsForNavigation.gotchaSectionChildCoords: SECTION children use the section's coordinate space, so appendChild moves a frame unless you re-apply its position: record absoluteBoundingBox first, append, then set x/y to (abs − section origin).
sectionsForNavigation.lint: All 27 frames, now inside sections: 0 findings on all eight checks.
sectionsForNavigation.looseTextNode: A raw list of the 14 standard banner messages was sitting on the canvas as an unparented TEXT node. It is now named 'REFERENCE — standard message library (Banner)' and filed under section 3, below the banner screens. Page children are now 7 sections and nothing else.
sectionsForNavigation.gotchaSectionDoesNotAutoGrow: A SECTION does not resize when you appendChild into it — the node lands outside the visible band with no warning. Recompute the content bounds and resizeWithoutConstraints after any append.

frameNamingPass.why: Eight frames were named by how they were MADE or by a branch they no longer belong to, in the slot every other frame uses to name its STATE. '— built from components' was a note written on the first frame of the session and had propagated to four; it says nothing to a developer, since every frame is built from components.
frameNamingPass.vocabulary: Every frame is now '<branch> — <state>'. States in use: chooser · empty form · no dashboard selected · no type selected · dashboard selected · standard message · custom message + call to action · scope menu open · ready to submit · submitting · confirmation · submission failed.
frameNamingPass.renames: New Request — built from components → chooser · Add/General/Feature — built from components → empty form · Banner / Notice — nothing selected → no type selected · Scope — multi-select menu (open) → Banner / Notice — scope menu open · Promote Dashboard — submitting → Submitting — any branch (Promote shown) · Promote Dashboard — submission failed → Submission failed — any branch (Promote shown).
frameNamingPass.outcomePrefixContradiction: The submitting and failed frames carried a 'Promote Dashboard —' prefix while sitting in a section labelled 'shared by every branch' — the name said the screen belonged to one branch. They now lead with the state and note the worked example in parentheses, matching 'Request submitted — confirmation' beside them.
frameNamingPass.staleReferenceCaught: The ② BLOCKERS frame cited the scope frame BY NAME in prose ('See the “Scope — multi-select menu (open)” frame'). Renaming a frame does not update a text reference to it, and nothing warns. Grep every doc frame's TEXT for the old names after any rename — one of the eight was live.
frameNamingPass.openGap: Edit Dashboard has no 'ready to submit' frame while Promote and Remove do. Its 'dashboard selected' frame already shows prefilled current values with Submit enabled, so the state may be redundant — but the set is asymmetric and that is a decision, not an oversight to leave silent.

failureRetryLabel.finding: The failed frame's submit button was byte-identical to the ready-to-submit frame's — label 'Submit for Review', enabled, isLoading false. The only evidence on the whole screen that a submission had been attempted and failed was the alert. An action bar that looks never-pressed contradicts the alert directly above it.
failureRetryLabel.decision: The button stays ENABLED and relabels to 'Try again'. Enabled is correct: the failure is server-side, nothing was sent, every field is intact, so retry IS the remedy. What was wrong was that the button did not say it was a retry — a user weighing 'did it half-go-through, am I about to file two?' hesitates over a button that reads like a first attempt.
failureRetryLabel.noBackoff: Repeat presses are stopped by the in-flight isLoading treatment the first attempt already uses, not by a cooldown or a disabled window. Adding backoff would punish the user for a server fault.
failureRetryLabel.specUpdated: Rule written into the ③ BEHAVIOUR SPEC beside the existing note that client-side validation failure is unreachable.
failureRetryLabel.stillOpenPruned: 'No dialog guards the Banner standard↔custom radio' was removed — that dialog was built this session. 'Edit Dashboard has no ready-to-submit frame' added in its place.

page102CopyPass2026_09_01.scope: UX copy review of all 21 screen frames plus the four alert dialogs on page 102, fully applied.

defectsFixed.bannerPreviewShowedWrongMessage: The frame headed 'Preview — what users will see' rendered the STANDARD message while the user had typed a custom title and body, and its CTA read 'View Status' while the Button label field beneath it read 'View status page'. The preview is the one element whose whole job is to be truthful. Now mirrors the typed title, body and button label.
defectsFixed.submitHintWasPastTense: Every ready-to-submit frame paired an unpressed 'Submit for review' button with the hint 'Submitted to the DART admin team for approval' — past tense, stated as fact. Directly contradicted the failure screen's careful 'nothing was sent'. Now 'Reviewed by the DART admin team within 2 business days.', which also pulls the SLA forward from the confirmation to before the decision to submit.

placeholderToHelperMove.problem: Short fields put guidance in helper text; the eight long-answer fields put it in the placeholder, where it disappears on the first keystroke — precisely the fields where someone needs the prompt WHILE writing.
placeholderToHelperMove.mechanism: Every Input/Textarea/NativeSelect already carries an exposed nested `label` instance with `Show description` + `Description`. No component change was needed; the helper slot existed and was simply switched off.
placeholderToHelperMove.editFormWasTheSharpCase: Edit's placeholders held DATA, not instruction — `Current: Mortgage Performance Dashboard` on nine fields. The value being edited away from vanished the instant the user typed. Current values are now helper text; text fields read 'Leave blank to keep' and the two selects show '— Select —'.
placeholderToHelperMove.blankMeansNoChangeIsNotSelfEvident: 'Leave blank to keep' repeats on nine fields, which is visually noisy — but blank-means-no-change is a convention, not an intuition, and the ambiguity it removes (does empty mean 'unchanged' or 'clear this value'?) is the one that matters most in an edit form. Kept deliberately; an empty placeholder would be quieter and less safe.

page102CopyPass2026_09_01.consistencyFixes: 'Submit for Review' → sentence case (18 instances) · confirmation timestamp moved from day-first '1 Sep 2026' to the mm/dd/yyyy the input fields teach · two straight apostrophes → curly · prioritises/summarises → US spelling to match the US date format · 'Submit another' → 'Submit another request' · Remove warning's ambiguous 'until they remove it' → 'until they remove it from their space' · 'Reviewers see custom wording more slowly' → 'Custom wording takes longer to approve' · chooser's ungrammatical 'on a dashboard, app, or platform-wide' → 'on a dashboard, an app, or across the whole platform'.
page102CopyPass2026_09_01.subtitleRemoved: 'All requests are reviewed by the DART admin team.' was identical on all 19 form frames and said the same thing as the submit hint below it and the chooser before it — three statements of one fact per screen. Hidden on every form; the chooser and the submit hint carry it now. Hidden rather than deleted, so it is one toggle to restore.
page102CopyPass2026_09_01.gotchaDoubleApplication: Editing a TEXT node inside an instance UPDATES that instance's component property, so a second pass over componentProperties re-applies the same replacement. 'Submit another' → 'Submit another request' → 'Submit another request request'. Any replacement whose search string is a prefix of its replacement will do this. Caught with a repeated-word scan; run one after every bulk text edit.
page102CopyPass2026_09_01.gotchaHintOverflow: The new hint measured 440px against 435px available and broke the submit bar on 8 frames. Setting the text to FILL fixed the overflow but the node is textAlignHorizontal RIGHT, so filling pushed the copy across the bar to sit flush against the button. Correct fix was to measure candidate strings against the real type style (clone the node onto the page canvas — an ABSOLUTE clone throws outside an auto-layout parent) and pick copy that fits at HUG: 'Reviewed by the DART admin team within 2 business days.' at 390px.
page102CopyPass2026_09_01.lint: All 27 frames, eight checks, zero findings. Every fix verified by re-reading the rendered strings, not by assuming the write succeeded.

regressionChooserCardHeights.cause: Lengthening the Banner card's description to fix its grammar took it from two lines to three. The grid rows are HORIZONTAL auto-layout at counterAxisAlignItems MIN with every card hugging its own content, so the taller card grew alone: row 1's two cards ended at different heights and their 'Select' links sat 19px apart.
regressionChooserCardHeights.whyTheLintMissedIt: All eight checks passed. Nothing overflowed and nothing spilled — the row simply hugged the taller child, which is legal layout. Unequal sibling heights inside a grid row is a NEW class of finding: the frame is correct and the design is wrong.
regressionChooserCardHeights.fix: Cards set to layoutSizingVertical FILL so they match the tallest in their row, then ui-card__body → option-content → copy all set to FILL so the slack lands in the copy and Card/Actions pins to the bottom. All four 'Select' links now align (row 1 at y424, row 2 at y662), each 60px above its card's bottom edge.
regressionChooserCardHeights.whyNotJustShortenTheCopy: Shortening the Banner description back to two lines would have made the four cards equal again without touching layout — but it makes alignment a property of the copy, so the next wording change silently breaks it. The layout fix holds at any length.
regressionChooserCardHeights.cssEquivalent: This is what a CSS grid gives for free: align-items stretch is the default, so the cards match per row, and rows size to content, so row 1 (242) and row 2 (222) legitimately differ. The Figma frames now match that behaviour rather than contradicting it.

adminTeamNaming.decision: Owner standardised on 'the DART Central admin team'. 13 occurrences across every frame, doc frames included. Zero stragglers.
adminTeamNaming.copyHadToChangeToFit: Adding ' Central' took the submit hint from 390px to 442px against 435px available — it would have re-broken the submit bar on all 8 ready-to-submit frames. 'within' → 'in' brings it to 414px. The confirmation's 'Reviewed within 2 business days' moved to 'in' as well so the two readings match, though it had room either way.
adminTeamNaming.lesson: A name is not a free substitution when it lives in a fixed-width bar. Measure the longest string against the real available width BEFORE the global replace, not after — the overflow only shows up as a lint finding once every frame is already wrong.

page102CopyPass2026_09_01.staleFillWidths: Setting the card body / content / copy frames to FILL left three text nodes reporting stale widths — Feature Request's title and description at 301px inside 280px instances (spilling 21px) and General Request's title at 259px. They were already layoutSizingHorizontal FILL, so nothing looked wrong in the properties; only the measured width disagreed. Fixed with the FIXED → resize → FILL round-trip. This is the fourth time this file has produced a stale measurement after a sizing change: ALWAYS re-measure after changing layout sizing, never trust the property.

americanEnglishAudit.scope: 598 strings across all 27 frames plus the loose reference note, checked against every common British/American divergence: -ise/-isation, -yse, -our, -re, -ce nouns, doubled L, and the misc set (whilst, amongst, programme, grey, enquiry, learnt, judgement, fulfil, per cent, catalogue, aluminium, maths, towards).
americanEnglishAudit.result: The user-facing screen copy was already clean — every spelling hit was in the DOCUMENTATION panels: 'Behaviour' ×2, 'colour', and 'cancelling'. Frame '③ BEHAVIOUR SPEC' renamed to '③ BEHAVIOR SPEC' and the cross-reference in ① updated with it.
americanEnglishAudit.clockConventionWasMixed: Not a spelling issue but the same class of thing: the flow ran a 24-hour clock ('06:00 ET', '08:00–12:00 ET') alongside a 12-hour one ('2:32 pm'). American English UI uses 12-hour with uppercase meridiem, so these became '6:00 AM ET', '8:00 AM – 12:00 PM ET' and '2:32 PM'. Dates were already mm/dd/yyyy throughout.
americanEnglishAudit.watchTheAllowList: A naive /\w+ise\b/ scan flags rise, advise, promise, otherwise, expertise, comprise, enterprise and two dozen more. The scan needs an allow-list of genuine -ise words or it buries the real findings; after allow-listing, zero -ise words remained and the only -ize words were the two already corrected.
americanEnglishAudit.lint: All 27 frames clean after the longer time strings — the banner message and its preview both absorbed '8:00 AM – 12:00 PM ET' without overflow.

grafanaToTableau.done: Every Grafana reference replaced with Tableau: the name-match helper, the toolbar toggle description, and the Edit frame's current URL. Zero remaining.
grafanaToTableau.liveOwnerEdits: The owner was editing the file during this pass, so two strings changed underneath it: 'Must match Grafana exactly' had already become 'Must match IRM exactly' on the empty form (and is now IRM on both frames), and the Add URL host became 'https://1234/…' mid-scan. Neither was touched by the script. When the owner is in the file, re-read before reporting — a value read at the start of a turn may not be the value at the end.
grafanaToTableau.openUrlShape: The URL path is still Grafana's convention — /d/{slug}. Tableau view URLs are /#/views/{Workbook}/{Sheet}. Swapping the host alone leaves a URL that no Tableau server would issue, so the example teaches the wrong format. Needs the owner's real Tableau server pattern.
grafanaToTableau.openVocabulary: 'Display panel tabs if the dashboard uses tab navigation' survived the swap because it contains no product name, but 'panel' is Grafana's word — Tableau has sheets and dashboard tabs. Same class of leftover as the URL path: renaming the product does not rename its vocabulary.

page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.frame: 'Banner / Notice — scope menu (searchable multi-select)' — two stages side by side: open with nothing typed (8 rows, 3 checked) and after typing 'mort' (filtered to 2 rows, 1 checked).
page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.allOptionRemoved: Owner's call: 'we would never want the user to select all — if they did that would be a site wide banner.' The 'All of Dartboards' row and its separator are gone. Ticking every box to reach a platform-wide banner made the largest-blast-radius outcome the easiest one to reach by accident, and hid it inside a picker instead of stating it.
page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.consequenceRaised: Removing it leaves NO route to a platform-wide banner, which the chooser card explicitly promises ('on a dashboard, an app, or across the whole platform'). Scope is currently a single control. The fix is a scope LEVEL field (specific dashboards / an application / platform-wide) with the searchable multi-select appearing only under the first — which also makes platform-wide an explicit, auditable choice rather than an emergent one. NOT built; needs the owner.
page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.selectionPersistsAcrossFiltering: Both stages show the trigger reading '3 dashboards selected' while the filtered stage lists only two rows — one of them unchecked. That is the behaviour a developer would otherwise have to guess: filtering hides rows, it does not deselect them.

codeChangeRequired.finding: No shipped component is a searchable multi-select. Verified in source, not assumed: Combobox.types.ts declares `value?: string` / `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void` — search, single-select. DropdownMenuCheckboxItem is multi-select with no search. Command has CommandInput + CommandList + CommandEmpty but its items carry no checked state.
codeChangeRequired.recommendation: Add `multiple` to Combobox. It already owns the trigger, the summary, the filter, the empty state and the floating surface; multi-select is a change to what `value` holds (string | string[]) and to the row indicator, not a new component.
codeChangeRequired.figmaDepiction: Drawn as a Combobox/Content instance (which ships the search-row) with DropdownMenu checkbox rows in its Body slot — literally what `Combobox multiple` would render, so the frame and the recommendation agree.

page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.scrollShownInCopyNotGeometry: A half-clipped final row is the better scroll affordance, but it puts the rows in genuine overflow of their slot, which the lint then reports and a later reader cannot distinguish from a real bug. The menu hugs its rows and the note states that the real list is every dashboard and scrolls.
page102ScopeSearchable2026_09_01.lint: Frame clean on all three layout checks. Section 3 resized to hold the wider frame (816 vs the previous 480).

The ② BLOCKERS entry still said the opposite — 'both of which DO ship' — so a developer reading the blocker list, which is the panel that exists precisely to be read before writing code, would have been told this needed no code.

page102MyRequests2026_09_01.carriedFromTheFlow: Reference numbers (#0417 is the confirmation's own reference, so the request a person just filed is the first row) · 'DART Central admin team' · mm/dd/yyyy dates · sentence-case buttons ('New request', not the POC's 'New Request') · the chooser's exact FeaturedIcon color + glyph per type, cloned from the chooser itself so the two cannot drift · the four type names as the chooser words them.
page102MyRequests2026_09_01.filtersAreToggleGroupsNotTabs: Two INDEPENDENT axes — type and status. CLAUDE.md's routing rule: Tabs carries one selection across the whole set and requires a real tabpanel, so it structurally cannot express two axes; filtering in place is ToggleGroup. Both groups use the IDENTICAL variant and size, per the recorded trap that a secondary axis given the louder treatment out-ranks the primary.

newStatusDerivedFromTheOwnersOwnRule.finding: The owner's rule is that My Requests is the ONLY place communication happens. That makes a fourth status necessary: if a person cannot see which requests need THEM, the only way to find an admin question is to open every request one at a time.
newStatusDerivedFromTheOwnersOwnRule.decision: 'Needs your reply' is a real status, in the badge AND in the status filter. Statuses are Pending review · Needs your reply · Approved · Rejected. An admin note that asks a question carries a Reply action and flips the status.
newStatusDerivedFromTheOwnersOwnRule.caughtLate: The first build shipped the status on a card while the filter still had only four options — the one status a person would most want to filter by was the one they could not. Found by screenshot, not by lint.

page102MyRequests2026_09_01.twoEmptyStatesNotOne: 'No requests yet' hides the filters entirely (nothing to filter) and offers New request. 'No results for these filters' keeps the filters visible AND still selected, and offers Clear filters. Showing the first in the second situation tells someone they have never filed a request — false, and unrecoverable without guessing. The POC had neither.
page102MyRequests2026_09_01.contentWidth880NotThe672FormWidth: A list is not a form. The frame stays 1072 to match every other screen, but the content column is 880. The clone inherited maxWidth 672 from the form-width decision, which silently swallowed every resize call — the node reported FIXED and simply did not move. Clear maxWidth before resizing a cloned column.
page102MyRequests2026_09_01.lintBugFoundInMyOwnCheck: The main-axis overflow check clamped itemSpacing with Math.max(0, …), which is wrong for a ToggleGroup: it uses itemSpacing -1 to collapse shared borders, so clamping overstated the need by exactly 4px and reported two false positives. Signed spacing is correct. Second time this check has been wrong about a legitimate layout — the first was SPACE_BETWEEN dropping itemSpacing.
page102MyRequests2026_09_01.layoutOnlyLintsHideRealFindings: Several recent passes ran only the three layout checks, and two unstyled TEXT nodes from the scope-menu build survived because of it. The full eight-check pass found them. Run all eight; the cheap three are not a substitute.
page102MyRequests2026_09_01.instanceInternalsAreALintBlindSpot: The geometry check skips anything inside an INSTANCE, which is right for a master's own internals but wrong for frames I author inside a Card's body SLOT — they escape the check entirely. Bound them by hand (23 values); the only unmapped ones were the ToggleGroups' -1, which is component-internal and correct to leave.
