customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.trigger: Owner asked for a critique of 1.1–1.4 and said it felt broken. It was: the picker and the canvas disagreed about what a widget IS, 1.4 was a dead end that silently changed the page width, and the picker could not say what was already on the page.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.fix1_kpiIsAWidget: Customize mode wrapped the whole KPI row as ONE widget with one remove control, while the picker offered INDIVIDUAL KPIs. Adding one from the picker had no defined destination and you could not remove a single tile. Each KPI is now its own widget with its own grip and ✕, laid out in a row — which is what the picker always described and what the owner asked for ('change the kpis in the top row to different items'). The handle is compact (grip + ✕, no label) because the tile already names itself.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.fix2_oneWidthRuleAndIGOTITWRONGFIRST: 1.4 was 1008 while 1.1–1.3 were 880, so customising silently widened the page. I first set 1.4 to 880 and resized the charts to 416 — which CLIPPED them: measured 13 and 8 children overflowing by up to 44px, with clipsContent true. Chart/Bar and Chart/Line are fixed at 480 and do not reflow. So two charts side by side genuinely need 480+48+480 = 1008, and the overview is now 1008 on ALL FOUR frames. The rule follows the widest widget rather than the narrowest content, and a width that changed per configuration was the actual bug. Tables refit to 1008 with no wraps.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.fix3_pickerKnowsWhatIsAlreadyThere: Five items now read 'Added' on a disabled Button with a muted label rather than offering to add a duplicate, and a line at the top states that new widgets land at the bottom and can be dragged afterwards. The picker's em dashes were also aligned to the middot the canvas uses — same widget, one string.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.fixSurfacedAGapOfItsOwn: Marking added items revealed 'KPI · Promoted Flags' on the page but NOT in the picker — remove it and it could never be recovered. Added under FROM PROMOTIONS, and renamed to 'Live promotions' across 1.1–1.3 because 'Promoted Flags' predates the decision that promotions are not feature flags; 1.4 already said 'Live promotions', so the two halves disagreed. New assertion: every widget on the page must be offerable by the picker — currently 6 on page, 16 offered, 0 unofferable.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.gotchaFillFlipsAxisWhenTheParentDoes: Moving the KPI cards from a HORIZONTAL row into VERTICAL wrappers left them at layoutSizingVertical FILL, which in a hugging vertical parent resolves to ZERO — the cards rendered at height 1 and the tiles vanished while the wrappers looked fine. FILL means 'the parent's primary axis', so re-parenting between a row and a column silently changes what it means. Set HUG after any such move.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.verification: Eight-check lint + deep clip sweep: zero on all four frames. All four columns 1008. Charts back at 480 with zero overflow. Entry points present on 1.1 and 1.4 (Customize) and 1.2/1.3 (Done, Add widget). Picker offerability assertion passes.
stillOpen: No cancel or undo in customize mode — only Done. Removing the wrong widget has no recovery.
No empty state for an overview with every widget removed.
Drag is implied by the grips but there is no drag/drop-target frame.
'+ Add widget' is the weakest control on the screen while being the only route into the picker.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.editModeRebuilt2026_09_03: Owner: 'the edit modes look really weird … dotted outlines that touch the edges. Are those really needed?' Two faults, one mine and one conceptual. MINE: the outlines hugged the content because I had zeroed their horizontal padding earlier to fix an overflow, so they read as a rendering fault. CONCEPTUAL: a dashed border is a WIREFRAME convention — it says placeholder, not editable — and putting one around every widget doubled the borders on screen, since the cards inside already have their own.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.whatReplacedIt: No boxes at all. Each widget keeps a borderless handle row above it (grip · name · remove) and the page carries a BANNER at the top: 'Editing your layout — drag a card to reorder it, or remove what you do not use. Only you see this arrangement.' The page now looks like itself in edit mode, which is the point — you are arranging the real thing, not a wireframe of it. Banner is the component built for a page-level mode announcement, so this is reuse rather than a bespoke bar.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.constraintBannerHasNoActionSlotInFigma: The owner's sketch put Done inside the banner. Banner's Figma component exposes Variant, Title and Show icon only — action, icon and onClose are code-only, and an instance cannot take extra children. So Done stays in the heading row where Customize sits on 1.1, which turns out better anyway: the button does not move when you switch modes, which also closes the 20px heading jump the critique flagged. The mode explanation moved from the subtitle into the banner, so 1.1–1.4 now share one subtitle.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.gotchaGroupNodesHaveNoDashPattern: The assertion sweeping for surviving dashed strokes crashed on a GROUP node, which has no dashPattern property. Guard with an 'in' check before reading a property in a findAll predicate — the callback runs against every node type in the subtree, not only the ones you had in mind.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.editModeTray2026_09_03: Owner: 'the grip and x are just floating and seem random and confusing, how can we connect those to the actual widget? I tried something on 1.2 pending approvals.' They had given that one wrapper a 10% tinted fill at radius 4 — the right instinct: the CONTROLS MUST SHARE A CONTAINER WITH THE THING THEY CONTROL. Borderless handle rows floating above cards read as unattached because nothing said which card they belonged to.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.whatShippedInstead: Every widget now sits in a TRAY: surface/accent, radius/2xl, 8px padding, holding the handle row and the card as one unit. Three corrections to the owner's sketch — a neutral surface rather than a 10% info tint, because in edit mode EVERY widget gets one, so the colour is structural and not a highlight; CONCENTRIC corners (card radius 8 + 8 padding = tray radius 16) instead of 4 outside 8, which reads as a mistake; and the handle's own second tint removed, since the tray is already the background.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.gotchaTrayPaddingBrokeTheTableAgain: The tray's 8px side padding left 992 for a table whose rows were FIXED at 1008 — 16px overflow, clipped. Third time a wrapper's padding has broken fixed-width children. Fixed properly this time rather than by re-deriving widths per mode: the activity table's rows are FILL and the Request column absorbs the slack, so the same table renders correctly at 1008 in 1.1 and 992 inside a tray, with no other column moving. A table that must live in more than one container needs one flexible column; fixed widths everywhere is what makes a wrapper impossible to add later.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.bannerBecameAlert2026_09_03: Owner's call, and the more correct component: Banner is the PAGE-LEVEL full-bleed bar, Alert is the inline one, and the mode notice sits inside the content column rather than spanning the app chrome. Alert also carries a Title AND a Description where Banner has only a Title, so the copy splits properly — 'Editing your layout' over 'Drag a card to reorder it, or remove what you do not use. Only you see this arrangement…' — instead of running as one long line. Variant info / Style default.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.appliedToBothStatesNotJustTheOneAskedFor: The owner said 'on 1.2'. Applied to 1.3 as well, because 1.3 IS 1.2 with the picker drawer open — leaving one as a Banner and the other as an Alert would have made the same screen disagree with itself across two frames. customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.recoveryAndEmptyState2026_09_03: Two frames added: '1.5 Admin Overview — empty (every widget removed)' and '1.6 Admin Overview — widget removed, undo'. LAND is now six frames and the diagram indexes all of them, asserted both directions.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.whyNotACancelButton: Asked for 'cancel/undo'. A Cancel beside Done would claim the whole edit session is BUFFERED, which is not how a layout editor normally behaves — arrangement changes save live. The two things that actually recover you are undoing the removal you just made and putting the shipped layout back, so that is what was built: an UNDO toast per removal, and RESET TO DEFAULT beside Done in edit mode. If a buffered session is genuinely wanted, Cancel is a small addition on top.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.undoUsesTheRealToast: Toast/Card already ships Dismiss and Undo as its two actions, so no relabelling was needed — the component had the pattern built in. Pinned bottom-right with a 24px inset, matching the Toaster. 1.6 actually REMOVES the widget it is about rather than showing the toast over an intact page, so the frame demonstrates the state it claims.
customizeFlowCritiqueFixes2026_09_03.emptyStateOffersBothRoutes: Built from 1.1 rather than from edit mode, because an empty overview is what you LAND on. Empty's own action reads 'Add widgets'; the description also offers to restore the original layout, so a centred ghost 'Reset to default' sits beneath it — a description that promises a route needs a control for it. The Empty's default glyph is an envelope; swapped to Icon/layout-dashboard, since the subject is a layout, not mail. sectionStructureFix2026_09_03.what: 1.4 (Admin Overview — rearranged, 2275:3943) had THREE different section structures on one page. Unified all content blocks to one shape: a section frame holding [section header, content], internal gap 12, sections separated by the column's 32.
sectionStructureFix2026_09_03.theComplaintWasSpacingButTheCauseWasStru: The owner reported 'the charts don't seem to be widgets, no header and spacing between is off'. No spacing VALUE was wrong. The dashboards heading and its table were SIBLINGS in the page column, so the column's 32px inter-section gap fell between a header and its own table, while every real section used 12 internally. charts: a bare HORIZONTAL row sitting directly in the column with NO header at all
section header + ui-table [dashboards — most opened]: two separate siblings of the column

sectionStructureFix2026_09_03.aHeightHeuristicIsNotAWrapTest: A check flagging 'wraps' on height > 20 reported two single-line headings as wrapping — the xs text style's line box exceeds the threshold on its own. This is the fifth false positive from a measurement heuristic on this page (phantom overflow from stale .width, phantom unreachable screen from exact-name match, flow-map regex matching its own new string, stale-'Answered' matching my own explanatory sentence). spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.theOwnerLoweredEightAndKeptTwelveWithWra: Sections went 12 -> 8 so a header sits closer to its content, which would have pulled the three queue cards to 8 as well. spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.aRowGapDoingDoubleDutyIsWhyOneFrameLooke: 1.3's 'page-heading row' was 16 while the other five were 32 — and it could not simply be raised. 1.3 is the only frame with TWO loose action buttons, so its single row gap was serving the heading-to-actions distance AND the button-to-button distance; setting 32 would have shoved the buttons apart. Wrapping the pair in 'actions' at 16 freed the row to be 32. A gap that cannot be changed without breaking something else is the signal that it is doing two jobs.
whatTheHandEditLeftBehind: 1.3's cards wrapper was gap 8, not 12 — the only one of the three that missed the value it was created for
1.4 and 1.6 had NO cards wrapper at all, so their three ui-card instances sat directly in the section at its 8
five widgets were on radius/2xl (16) rather than radius/lg (8): 1.3's queue widget and all four of 1.6's KPI widgets
action buttons sat loose in the row on 1.1, 1.3, 1.4 and 1.5 — only 1.2 and 1.6 had the wrapper
four of the five new frames had an UNBOUND itemSpacing
two 'handle' frames kept a leftover mixed 4/4/0/0 radius on radius/base while their six siblings were 0
1.6's section header carried 0/4/0/4 padding against 0/0/0/0 everywhere else
spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.aHandMadeFrameStartsUnbound: Four of the five frames the owner drew had a literal itemSpacing with no variable behind it. The values were all correct, so nothing looked wrong and the file's own unbound-geometry check is the only thing that catches it. spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.namingFollowsFilePrecedent: Content wrappers -> 'cards' (the Chat page already names a frame of Chat/Source instances 'cards'); button wrappers -> 'actions' (the table donor set already uses it). Chose existing file vocabulary over inventing 'button group' or 'card stack'. spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.sixthFalsePositiveFromAMeasurementHeuris: The overflow check reported three findings — 1.3's scrim, 1.3's add-widget drawer, 1.6's undo toast — all bogus. Every one is layoutPositioning ABSOLUTE, and an absolutely-positioned child ignores its parent's padding, which the check was subtracting. absoluteBoundingBox settled it: the scrim's box is identical to its parent's, the drawer ends exactly on the parent's right edge (2508+420 = 2928), and the toast is inset exactly the documented 24px. An overflow check MUST skip layoutPositioning === 'ABSOLUTE' children. Sixth heuristic false positive on this page; the standing rule holds — a measured finding is a hypothesis until an image or absoluteBoundingBox confirms it.
spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.verification: Playbook design-check lint over all six frames, instance internals skipped: unbound paint 0, unstyled text 0, generic names 0, unbound geometry 0. Structural assertion: 6/6 rows are [page-heading, actions] at 32 bound; 6/6 actions at 16 bound; 10/10 section frames are [section header, single content node] at 8 bound; 5/5 cards wrappers at 12 bound; 17/17 widgets at radius/lg bound. spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.openItem: CLOSED same day, owner's call: the three 'recent activity' frames on 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 are now 'section — recent activity'. A hand traversal of the whole Admin Flow page confirms zero stragglers and 20 section frames, every one named 'section — …' at gap 8. The READ FIRST panel already followed the convention, so those three were the only holdouts. 'stat row' vs 'stat row (4 KPI widgets)' stays split — that one marks view mode against edit mode and is meaningful.
spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.aQuerySelectorValueCannotHoldAnUnquotedS: node.query('FRAME[name=recent activity]') matched ZERO nodes and threw nothing — the rename loop ran over an empty array and returned a clean success. The three frames were sitting right there. Only the structural assertion returned alongside it (no 'section — recent activity' in the list) showed the write had not happened. Same failure class the Tabs icon rebinding hit: a write loop that matches nothing reports success while doing nothing. Two rules from it — address a known node by ID rather than by a name selector, and when a sweep must be by name, hand-traverse and compare with === so a zero match is visible. Always return an assertion the write should have changed, not just the loop's own tally.
spacingModelSweep2026_09_03.aNamedFunctionExpressionIsNotInScopeOuts: '(function walk(){...})(page)' then calling walk() again later throws ReferenceError: 'walk' is not defined — the name binds only inside the function's own body. Worth knowing here because use_figma is ATOMIC: the script had already renamed all three frames before the error, and none of it landed. That is the good outcome, but it means an error late in a script tells you nothing about what the early half did — it did nothing. Declare helpers with 'function name()' at statement level.

trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.what: The owner sent screenshots of 1.1 and 1.2 with no comment. Two faults in customize mode, neither of them spacing: the widget name was rendered TWICE on two widgets, and was missing entirely on the other four. Fixed by making the tray the widget's header in edit mode.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.theNameWasSaidTwiceOnExactlyTheWidgetsTh: widget [Approval queue · top 3] had a tray reading 'Approval queue · top 3' and then, 8px below it, a section header reading 'APPROVAL QUEUE' with a count badge and a View all. Same on widget [Recent activity · 5 rows] over 'RECENT ACTIVITY'. Meanwhile the four KPI trays held grip + spacer + Remove and NO text node at all. So entering customize mode named two widgets twice and left four anonymous — the asymmetry was backwards, because the two with a duplicate already had a title and the four with nothing had no other label than their own card copy.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.theHandleLabelWasNotPurelyRedundant: '· top 3' and '· 5 rows' state the widget's CONFIGURATION, which the section header never says. That is why the fix was not 'delete the duplicate' — deleting the tray label would have lost the only statement of what slice of the queue the widget shows. trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.ownerDecision: The tray becomes the widget's header in edit mode. The inner section header goes, taking its count badge and View all with it; the tray keeps the name plus the config suffix. View mode (1.1, 1.4) is untouched and keeps section header + badge + View all — the tray only exists in edit mode, so there is nothing to duplicate there.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.collapseTheWrapperOrItBecomesTheSameBugA: Removing the header left 'section — approval queue' holding exactly one child, inside a widget that already carries the name. That is the redundant nesting the 1.4 fix was about, so the wrapper was deleted and the content lifted into the widget. A widget is now [handle, content] — [handle, cards] or [handle, ui-table]. trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.theGapFOLLOWSWhatTheStripIS: A tray carrying a title is a HEADER, so its gap to the content is 8 (spacing/2) like every other header-to-content pair in the file. A tray holding only a grip and an × is CHROME, so it stays at 4 (spacing/1). Widget gaps therefore read 4 and 8 on the same frame, which looks like drift and is not — the two strips are doing different jobs. Asserted: 12 unlabelled KPI trays at 4, 5 labelled trays at 8, every one bound.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.theTitleDidNotGetQUIETERThoughItLooksLik: The screenshot reads as though the widget title lost weight on entering edit mode. The only delta is the treatment — the section heading uses the 'xs/leading-normal/Medium Wide' style at 2.5% tracking with the characters typed in caps, the tray uses 'xs/leading-normal/Medium' in sentence case. Recorded because the visual impression was wrong and a redesign was nearly started on it. Left in sentence case: an uppercase wide-tracked 'APPROVAL QUEUE · TOP 3' beside a grip and an × would shout, and the config suffix reads better unshouted.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.aLiveViewAllInsideAWidgetYouAreRearrangi: Both edit-mode section headers kept a link-styled View all and a count badge — navigation out of the layout you are in the middle of editing. Removed with the header rather than as a separate fix, which is the argument for the tray-as-header shape over just adding labels to the four bare trays.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.scrimIsAFalsePositiveOfAnEmptyFrameCheck: An 'empty frame' check flagged 1.3's 'scrim' — a deliberately childless absolutely-positioned overlay fill. The check excluded 'spacer' and not 'scrim'. Seventh heuristic false positive on this page; an empty-frame check must whitelist the frames whose job is to be empty.
trayIsTheHeader2026_09_03.verification: Design-check lint over all six frames, instance internals skipped: unbound paint 0, unstyled text 0, generic names 0, unbound geometry 0. addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.what: Owner: the add-widget drawer on 1.3 'doesn't have a close or done or anything to close the drawer and move on'. It had a close — a 20x20 CloseButton at Size=sm in the header of a 1368px panel — and NO footer. Fixed by turning the footer on and giving it a single Done.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.theCloseWasThereAndStillWasNotAWayOut: A ghost glyph in the corner reads as dismiss, not as finishing. The panel's own copy said 'Drag them where you want once the panel is closed' and then offered nothing to close it with. Rows carry live Add/Added links, so a user adds three widgets and is left looking for the door. The bug was the missing exit affordance, not a missing control.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.theOneDrawerWithItsFooterSwitchedOff: The Drawer master ships 'Show footer' = true. This instance had it set to false — the only one of the four drawers on the page. apply request #0431, apply request #0433 and edit dashboard all carry [ghost Cancel, default Submit/Save] at Size=sm. When one instance of a component disagrees with every sibling on a boolean, check the boolean before redesigning.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.doneNotCancelNotApply: The master's footer defaults read Reset + Apply. Neither word is true here — adds are live (the row flips to Added), so there is nothing buffered to apply and nothing to reset. Same reasoning as the page-level whyNotACancelButton: a Cancel or Reset would claim the session is buffered when it is not. One Done, Style=default, Size=sm to match every other drawer footer in the file; Reset hidden. The header CloseButton stays — X + footer is the Drawer's own anatomy, as with Dialog.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.hidingAnInstanceChildRecreatesTheSubtree: reset.visible = false then reset.parent threw 'The node with id 2332:5405 does not exist'. Toggling visibility on a child inside a slot-bearing instance re-instantiates the subtree, so a node reference held from before the mutation points at a parent id that no longer exists. Script was atomic so nothing half-applied. Fix: re-discover from the stable drawer node by getNodeByIdAsync after EVERY mutation and select children by property (Style=ghost / Style=default), never by a reference taken earlier. Already recorded once for detachInstance; it also applies to plain visibility.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.skipInvisibleInstanceChildrenHidesTheFoo: With 'Show footer' off, drawer.children returned [header, Body] and no footer node at all — the harness runs with invisible instance children skipped. So the footer's buttons could not be inspected before enabling it. Order of work has to be: toggle the boolean, THEN read what the master put there, THEN configure.
addWidgetDrawerDone2026_09_03.verification: Footer visible children after the change: exactly one Button, Style=default, Label 'Done', rendered text 'Done'. Screenshot of 1.3 shows Done bottom-right of the drawer at the same weight as the page's own Done. Instance-only change; the frame lint skips instance internals and nothing outside the drawer moved, so the all-zeros result from the previous pass stands.

Dashboards could plausibly take the product axis that is identical on every other screen; Activity has no obvious second axis (Event? type?). filterBarSeparator2026_09_03.theSearchInputStays: 5.2 has no search field; the queue bars do. The owner's crop showed only the toggle structure and the ask was about the two axes and the divider. A Jira-style queue with no search would be a functional regression, so search was kept as the trailing child on every bar that had one. Not a deviation from 5.2 — an addition beyond it.
filterBarSeparator2026_09_03.aSeparatorInARowNeedsCrossAxisCentre: The divider is 20px in a 36px row. It only reads as a divider if the bar's counterAxisAlignItems is CENTER; MIN would pin it to the top edge. All five bars were already CENTER (asserted, not assumed); set explicitly anyway so a later re-layout cannot drop it.

tableHeaderFill2026_09_03.darkModeMergesWithTheCardByDesign: In dark, surface/secondary and the card surface both resolve to #1e293b, so the filled header is separated from the body by its hairline alone — the recorded, accepted Table decision. tableHeaderFill2026_09_03.anIsolatedRenderOfADarkTableLooksBroken: screenshot() on the table node paints dark-mode --foreground body text on a transparent ground, so the rows read as near-invisible white-on-white. filterRowSpacingModel2026_09_03.spaceBetweenBreaksAFourChildBar: The queue bars were [product, separator, state, search]. SPACE_BETWEEN distributes ALL children, so the divider and the state group would have drifted apart across the width and the two-axis grouping built the same day would have dissolved. filterRowSpacingModel2026_09_03.twoShapesOnePrinciple: Table screens (5.1, 5.6, 4.3, 4.5, 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5): 'filtered table' [filter-bar, ui-table]. filterRowSpacingModel2026_09_03.emptyStateKeepsItsAir: 2.3 (no matching requests) has the same bar treatment (axes, padding, SPACE_BETWEEN) but no wrapper: its next sibling is ui-empty, not a table, and 8px under a search field is not where an empty state wants to sit. 5.1.indexOfIsNotIdentityAcrossLookups: insertChild(parent.children.indexOf(last)) threw 'negative index' twice: findAll() and .children hand back different wrapper objects for the same node in this harness, so === never matches. headingRowRevised.what: The owner built Task 2's heading row, rejected it, and iterated to a settled shape on 5.1: the heading row holds [page-heading, kpi] at gap 64 and the Add moved into the filter row's right-hand 'actions' cluster. Spec §1/§2 and the plan's Tasks 3-6 Step 2 amended to match.
headingRowRevised.whyTheFirstShapeFailed: A KPI is a SURFACE — fill, border, radius, 82px tall — and a button is a CONTROL at 36px. Side by side at the same altitude they read as two unrelated widgets bolted to the title, and no alignment fixes it: top-aligned the button floats beside a tall box, centred it leaves the title's baseline. The heaviest element on the row was also the least actionable one. Separating them by altitude — surface in the header, control in the filter row — is what resolved it.
headingRowRevised.buildTheCardFromItsPropsNotFromAClone: The first KPI cloned 1.1's stat tile and hugged its slot content by hand; it came out 488x108 because the instance was HUG while its ui-card__body SLOT was FILL at a fixed width, so 'hug' resolved to the slot's width. The owner's rebuild uses Card's own header API instead — Show header on, Title=the number, Description=the label, Show header action carrying a ui-badge, everything else off — which is 206x82 and survives a Card update. Reach for a component's props before overriding its slot content.
headingRowRevised.theAddIsLabelledAndSizedToItsRow: A bare ghost + was tried and rejected: no accessible name, and beside a filter control a + reads as 'add a filter' rather than 'create a dashboard' — the same finding already recorded against '+ Add widget' on 1.2. Settled as Style=default, Size=sm with a leading + glyph. sm because the toggle group and the search input are both sm; at xs it was the only xs control on the page and rendered the primary action smaller than the ghost tool beside it.
headingRowRevised.noSortControl: A sort icon-only button was drawn in the cluster and removed — the table header already sorts every column, so it was a second route to the same thing. A hidden leftover bare-plus button was removed with it; a hidden node still clones into every copy of the page.
headingRowRevised.fiveOneHadTheFilterNamesInverted: 5.2/4.4 established the two-level shape: the VERTICAL stack is 'filter-search' and the HORIZONTAL row inside it is 'filter-bar'. 5.1 had them the other way round — its vertical stack was 'filter-bar' and the row inside it was an unnamed 'Frame 1' — so a page-wide filter-bar assertion was matching different things on different pages. Corrected, and the right group named 'actions' after the LAND heading rows.
headingRowRevised.theEightPxIndentWasLostAndRestored: The owner's own earlier decision — 8px each end so the filter row indents from the table — was dropped when the block was restructured. Restored on filter-search (where 5.2 carries it), bound to spacing/2.
headingRowRevised.searchPlacementIsFitNotSymmetry: At 1008 wide with one axis (5.1, 5.6) or two (2.1-2.5) the row has room for search; at 880 with two axes (5.2, 4.4) it does not and search stacks full-width below. Both are the same filter-search shape. Existing screens keep whichever they have — this pass does not move search.
headingRowRevised.openQuestion: 5.3 Promotions and 5.4 URL Redirects have NO filter row — their columns are [page-heading, ui-table, body] — so the amended pattern puts the Add somewhere they lack. patternAppliedAcrossTheSection.theSettledShape: content column (32) > page-heading row [page-heading, kpi] gap 64 (spacing/16) MIN/MIN, then 'filtered table' (8) > filter-bar HORIZONTAL gap 24 (spacing/6) SPACE_BETWEEN/CENTER pad 0/8/0/8 > [<axes>, actions]. patternAppliedAcrossTheSection.fiveTwoHadCloneDrift: 5.2 carried 5.1's KPI verbatim — '201 / Published dashboards / Live' on the Banners page — and an Add labelled 'New dashboard'. Its axes wrapper was an unnamed 'Frame 1' and its heading row was still gap 32 MIN/CENTER. All four corrected: 3 / Active banners / of 6, 'New banner', 'axes', gap 64 MIN/MIN. patternAppliedAcrossTheSection.fiveThreeAndFiveFourGotTheirFilterRow: Both had no filter row at all — columns were [page-heading, ui-table, body] — so the pattern had nowhere to put the Add. patternAppliedAcrossTheSection.aTextNodeKeepsItsOldWidthWhenReparented: 6.1's two 'section heading' TEXT nodes were direct column children at a FIXED 1008 wide. editPaths2026_09_03.destructiveIsATokenNotAVariant: DropdownMenu/Item has NO destructive variant — its only axis is State (default/hover/disabled), which CLAUDE.md already records. editPaths2026_09_03.assertOnTheRESOLVEDVariableNotOnItsPrese: The first destructive assertion tested 'does this label have a bound fill' and reported all four items red on every menu — because a PLAIN item's label is also bound, to text/foreground. editPaths2026_09_03.theValueIsThePlaceholderProp: An Input in these drawers shows its value through Placeholder#192:52 with variant Filled=True — not through a text node — and NativeSelect uses Value#205:26. editPaths2026_09_03.stripTheDiffRowsWhenAnApplyBecomesAnEdit: 4.4's drawer is a request-driven APPLY: every field carries a 'previous value' TEXT reading 'was …'. editPaths2026_09_03.aClonedOverlayKeepsTheOldFrameHeight: 5.1b's drawer and scrim were still 572 tall inside a 546 frame after the owner rebuilt 5.1 — the base got shorter and the absolutely-positioned children did not follow. records2026_09_03.theFlowMapIsNotOneBoxPerFrame: The plan assumed the map lists frames one per line. It does not — it is a laid-out diagram of six auto-layout stage columns whose boxes are one per IDEA, with ranges where states belong together: '1.2–1.4 Customize it', '4.1–4.2 Approved, not applied', '4.3–4.4 Drawer, prefilled'. Adding nine boxes, one per new frame, would have contradicted its own convention. Five went in instead, each covering a page's edit path and inserted directly after that page's box so the column still reads 5.1, 5.1a–5.1b, 5.2, 5.2a … The columns are VERTICAL auto-layout at gap 8, so insertChild reflowed everything; the map has 232px of slack left.

records2026_09_03.theFlowMapsRadiiWereNeverBound: The final lint returned 124 unbound-geometry findings, every one a corner radius on the flow map: 25 boxes at 8 and the panel at 12, none bound — 104 of them pre-existing, 20 inherited by the five boxes cloned from them. Swept all 124 onto radius/lg and radius/xl by matching the literal to the token's value; 0 unmapped, 0 remaining. This is the file-wide rule already recorded for component-set radii — when the same unbound literal shows up across a page, sweep it rather than patch locally. Cloning a node inherits its debt: the clone was correct and still added 20 findings.

critiqueFixes2026_09_04.what: Three fixes from the end-to-end critique: the flow ended twice with no feedback, four destructive actions had no confirm, and the queue — the page an admin lives in — was the flattest screen in the system with its primary route hidden.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.theFlowEndedTwiceWithNoFeedback: Tracing every action to a destination frame found two dead ends: 4.3/4.4 Submit went nowhere, and Save changes in five drawers went nowhere. One toast existed in 40 frames (1.6, widget removed). Closed with 4.6 Applied (2380:7578) and 5.1c Dashboards — saved, undo (2381:7693). An admin who edits a live banner now gets told it went live.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.fourDestructiveActionsHadNoConfirm: ADMIN — ACTION DIALOGS held four dialogs, one of them Delete banner — so the precedent was already set that an irreversible action gets a dialog stating consequences. Decommission, End promotion early, Remove redirect and Revoke admin had none, and two of them are red. Four dialogs added, the row set to WRAP so eight sit in two columns. Confirm styling follows the recorded rule: state changes default (Decommission, End promotion), true removals error (Remove redirect, Revoke access).
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.everyDestructiveDialogNamesTheSofterAlte: Delete banner's copy is the template — it states the consequence AND offers the way to avoid it ('switch it off instead: that keeps the banner and its dates'). Remove redirect follows it exactly, and it matters most there: the page's own doc panel says a redirect with thousands of hits is load-bearing and must not be deleted, while the design let you delete one in two clicks. It now says '213 hits, every one of those links 404s from now on — set it to Inactive instead'.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.theQueuesPrimaryRouteWasHiddenInASeconda: On 2.1 the only affordance on a row was the ⋯ at the far right, with 'Open review' inside it. The Request # was a code chip and the title was plain text — nothing said a row opens. The single most-travelled journey in the product was behind a secondary control. The Request title now binds to text/primary-main-text on all 38 rows across 2.1, 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5, so the row reads as openable and ⋯ keeps the change-status shortcut it was built for.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.visualWeightRanOppositeToImportance: 5.4 URL Redirects — four rows, the least consequential page — had a KPI card and a filled primary button. 2.1 Approval Queue had neither. All five queue frames now carry the same page-heading row and a KPI.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.theQueueKpiIsFourNotFive: 1.1's tile says 5 pending, and the queue's own statuses are Needs review 2, New 2, Awaiting reply 1, plus 8 decided. Waiting on YOU is 4 — the awaiting-reply one is waiting on the requester. Rather than repeat 5 or silently disagree with it, the KPI reads 4 / Waiting on you / '1 awaiting reply', which reconciles to 1.1's 5 and tells the admin which part is theirs. 2.2 is scoped so it reads 1 / Waiting on you / 'Aiden only'.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.aFrameThatClaimsARecordMustShowIt: 4.6's own caption said 'Activity carries the change under your name' while its activity card still showed only Jordan's submission. Two entries added — approved, then applied — and their cloned avatars carried Jordan's JR initials until corrected to the acting admin. A cloned thread entry inherits the wrong person.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.staleIdsAgainAfterCloningInsideAnInstanc: The ids returned when the two activity entries were created did not resolve on the next call — cloning inside a slot-bearing instance re-creates the subtree, the same lesson already recorded for visibility toggles. Re-found them by their text content instead. Do not carry a node id across calls when the write was inside an instance.
critiqueFixes2026_09_04.leftOpen: No loading state and no failed-save state anywhere, though table (loading) and Input Error=True both ship. No no-results state on the MANAGE pages. No bulk action on the queue though Table/SelectionCell exists. Deny is still the only colour on the 3.x decision bar. All recorded in the critique, none built.

loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.what: The last two states the critique flagged as missing: 5.1d Dashboards — loading (2386:8011) and 5.1e Dashboards — no results (2387:8068). Both follow the Table page’s own reference frames rather than inventing a shape.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.theHeaderSurvivesBothStates: table (loading) and table (empty) on the Table page both keep the header-row and swap only the body — skeleton rows in one, an empty-body holding an Empty in the other. Copying that means the columns do not jump between loading, populated and empty, which is the whole reason the header stays. Followed exactly.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.skeletonRowsAreBuiltNotCloned: A table row is a Table/Cell INSTANCE and nothing can be appended inside an instance, so a skeleton row cannot be made by cloning a data row and dropping a Skeleton in. Built as plain FRAMEs instead — one 'cell' per column, each width read off the real header cell (186/104/120/150/152/122/112/62) so the skeletons line up with the columns they stand in for. The actions column is left empty, as on the reference. Skeleton instances cloned from the Table page's own loading frame, which getNodeByIdAsync reaches cross-page without switching.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.theKpiStillShowsANumberWhileTheTableLoad: Deliberate, not an oversight. A count and a paginated table are separate queries and the count routinely lands first; skeletoning the KPI would claim they always resolve together. Recorded so it is not "fixed" later as an inconsistency.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.noResultsNamesTheTermAndOffersTheWayOut: Copied 2.3's approach — it names the actual query ('AST-9999') rather than saying 'no results'. 5.1e reads 'Nothing matches “collateral risk”. Check the spelling, or clear the search to see all 201', the search field carries that term with Filled=True so the state is coherent, and the Empty's action reads Clear search.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.theEmptyGlyphWasTheEnvelopeAgain: Empty's default media is Icon/inbox, and BOTH filter-empty states carried it — 5.1e because it was cloned from 2.3, and 2.3 because nobody had swapped it. The identical bug is already recorded against 1.5 ('the Empty's default glyph is an envelope; swapped to Icon/layout-dashboard, since the subject is a layout, not mail'). Swapped both to Icon/search: the subject is a search that found nothing. Empty exposes its media as a SLOT, not an INSTANCE_SWAP property, so the fix is swapComponent on the nested 'glyph' instance. The stroke binding was checked either side of the swap rather than assumed — text/muted-foreground survived on both, unlike the FeaturedIcon case recorded earlier where a swap kept an inherited binding.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.scope: Shown once on 5.1, the file’s standing convention for a state (1.6 shows undo once, 5.1c shows saved once). The same two states apply to 5.3, 5.4 and 5.6 unchanged. 5.2 Banners is a card list, so its loading is skeleton CARDS rather than skeleton rows — noted, not drawn.
loadingAndNoResults2026_09_04.verification: Assertion: header retained in both; 4 skeleton rows, zero real rows, cell widths byte-identical to the header, 7 skeletons for 8 columns; 5.1e has an empty-body, no rows, an Icon/search glyph and the query in the field; 2.3’s glyph is Icon/search too. 0 violations, lint 0/0/0/0/0 over 5.1d, 5.1e and 2.3.

saveFailed2026_09_04.what: 5.1f Dashboards — save failed (2388:8164): the drawer stays open with an error Alert above the form, a Try again action, and the pending edits intact.
saveFailed2026_09_04.twoFailuresOneNeedsAScreen: A save fails two ways. A REJECTED field (the server refuses a value) is already fully specified by Input's own Error variant plus its error message — a frame would not add anything a component does not already say. A save that NEVER LANDED has no home: nothing else in the file states whether the drawer closes, whether the edits survive, or how to retry. That is the one drawn. The rejected-field case stays undrawn deliberately, not by omission.
saveFailed2026_09_04.theBannerHasToBeVisiblyTrue: First cut showed the fields holding the SAVED values, so the Alert's line 'your edits are still here' had nothing to point at — the drawer and the row behind it read identically. The pending edits now differ from the row: the drawer says Collateral Health Monitor and /views/collateral-health-v2 while the table behind still says Collateral Health Dashboard. A frame that makes a claim in copy has to make the claim visible, or a reader has no reason to believe it.
saveFailed2026_09_04.theCopyStatesWhatWasNotWritten: Alert: 'Could not save — the connection dropped before your changes were written. Nothing has changed yet; the dashboard still shows its old values, and your edits are still here.' The note under the form carries the part people actually need: 'Nothing was written, so there is nothing to undo. Closing this drawer discards the edits above.' A failure message that only says it failed leaves the user guessing whether half of it went through.
saveFailed2026_09_04.setPropertiesResetsTheLayerName: alert.name was set BEFORE setProperties and did not survive it — the instance came back named ui-alert [editing your layout], its source. Caught because the returned formKids still showed the old name. Name an instance AFTER its properties are set, and read the name back rather than trusting the assignment. Same family as the stale-id lesson: a write inside an instance re-creates what you were holding.
saveFailed2026_09_04.reusedNotRebuilt: The Alert is a clone of 1.2's "editing your layout" instance switched to Variant=error with Show action on — the Alert set already carries default/brand/info/success/warning/error, so no new component was needed. Footer keeps ghost Cancel + default Save changes: the retry path is the same button that failed.
saveFailed2026_09_04.verification: Assertion: alert named ui-alert [save failed], Variant=error, action shown and labelled Try again; the drawer's Name differs from the row behind it; footer ghost Cancel sm + default Save changes sm; drawer flush right at full height over a full-frame scrim. 0 violations, lint 0/0/0/0/0.

queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.what: Bulk selection on the queue, a four-tile KPI row replacing the single card, and a relayout of every frame on the page — they had grown into each other.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.kpiRowReplacedTheSingleCard: The queue's single KPI card became a four-tile stat row cloned from 1.1: Waiting on you 4 · Awaiting reply 1 · Oldest waiting 13 days · Decided 7. Every number is derived from that frame's own rows at build time rather than typed — the script reads each table's Status and Submitted columns, so 2.2 (scoped to Aiden) correctly reads 1 / 0 / 5 days / 1 while the rest read the full queue. The single card was removed; a row and a card saying the same thing is the redundancy the critique already flagged.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.theQueuesFirstColumnWasLabelledTwoWays: Deriving the oldest-waiting reference failed on 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5 and returned an empty string. Cause: 2.1's first column header reads 'Request #' and those three still read 'Ref' — the recorded Ref→Request # refinement only ever landed on 2.1. A header-index lookup matched on one frame and silently fell through on three. Renamed all three, and the lookup now finds cells by NAME rather than by header text. A derived value that comes back empty is a finding, not a blank.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.bulkSelection: Table/SelectionCell shipped unused, which the critique flagged as implying a capability that did not exist. A 48px selection column was added to 2.1, 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5, funded by shrinking the Request column by 48 so each table's total width holds exactly (1008 and 2406 unchanged). 2.6 Approval Queue — rows selected (2394:8721) shows three checked with the header indeterminate.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.whileASelectionIsActiveTheToolbarIsAbout: 2.6 hides the filter row and puts a selection bar in its place: '3 requests selected' with Clear selection on the left, Deny and Approve on the right. Filtering and selecting compete for the same strip, and a selection is the more urgent of the two.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.requestMoreInformationIsNotABulkAction: Approve and Deny are the only two bulk verbs. Approve needs no per-item input, and Deny takes one reason that can honestly apply to a batch. 'Request more information' asks a DIFFERENT question of each requester, so a bulk version would send one question to several people about several things — it is excluded deliberately, not forgotten.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.theFramesHadGrownIntoEachOther: Six real overlaps and four sections whose frames ran outside their own bounds. Causes were all the same shape: sections were never resized as frames were appended to the right (MANAGE was 1264 wide holding frames out to x=8496), and frames that GREW pushed into their neighbours — 2.1 gained 148px of stat row and ran into 2.2, the action-dialogs frame doubled in height and ran into the sidebars, and 4.6 was placed at 4.1's y + height without checking what already sat there. Placing a clone relative to ONE neighbour is not a layout.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.theRelayout: Every section relaid out as a wrapped grid: frames sorted in natural order (so 5.1, 5.1a … 5.1f, 5.2 read correctly), 80px between frames, 120px between rows, wrapping at 5000px, 64px section padding, each section resized to its content, then the seven sections spaced left to right in stage order with a 240px gutter. Page is now 34,632 wide. Asserted afterwards: 0 overlaps within any section, 0 frames outside their section, 0 sections overlapping each other.
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.flowMap: Gained boxes for 2.6 Rows selected and 4.6 Applied, and the dashboards edit-path box widened from 5.1a–5.1b to 5.1a–5.1f (menu · drawer · saved · loading · empty · failed).
queueBulkAndPageLayout2026_09_04.verification: Lint over the five queue frames, 2.6 and the flow map: 0/0/0/0/0. Layout assertion: 0 overlaps, 0 out-of-bounds, 0 section collisions across 50 frames in 7 sections.

tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.what: Full tokenisation audit of the Admin Flow page before building components: fills, stroke colour, stroke weight, text styles AND text-style overrides, all four paddings, itemSpacing, counterAxisSpacing, all four radii, and effects — 50 frames, split by whether a node was authored here or belongs to a component instance.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.result: The screens are clean. On nodes authored here: unbound fill 0, unbound stroke colour 0, unstyled text 0, TEXT-STYLE OVERRIDDEN 0, unbound padding 0, unbound gap 0, unbound radius 0, unbound effect 0. Every remaining finding sits inside a component instance and belongs to the master.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.strokeWeightIsStoredPERSIDEAndTheFirstAu: The first pass reported 473 unbound stroke weights and a fabricated conclusion that border-width tokens existed but were used by nothing. Wrong: Figma stores stroke weight as strokeTopWeight / strokeRightWeight / strokeBottomWeight / strokeLeftWeight, and boundVariables.strokeWeight is empty even when all four sides are bound. 665 nodes on this page bind it per side. The 'fix' written on the back of that finding — setBoundVariable('strokeWeight', …) on 35 nodes — silently did NOTHING: no error, no change, and the audit that followed still reported the same 35. A write that reports success and changes nothing is the same failure class already recorded for the Tabs icon rebinding. Check a binding by reading it back, and check the property NAME the API actually uses before concluding a token is unused.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.whatIsActuallyUnbound: Three things, all in component masters, none on the screens: (1) BORDER STROKE WEIGHT on six masters — Dialog 503:45, Button outline 76:80, Card 1811:796, Drawer 514:45 (mixed), Toast/Card 601:45, DropdownMenu/Content 546:52 — all at weight 1, which border-width/100 already matches; 161 instances inherit it on this page alone. (2) ALERT internal gap of 12 on master 416:77, which spacing/3 matches. (3) ICON vector stroke weight is INCONSISTENT across the icon set — Icon/house 312:19434 binds its vector, yet 164 icon vectors on this page do not; the file already has icon-border-width/sm|default|lg and an Icon collection whose icon/stroke-weight aliases them with modes for 24/20/16/14/12, so the mechanism exists and has been applied unevenly.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.notDefects: Skeleton's 28 shimmer sweeps are GRADIENT_LINEAR fills — a gradient cannot bind to a colour variable, the same reasoning already recorded for Mark's artwork. Icon stroke weights of 1.167 / 1.5 / 1.667 have no border-width token and should not: they are 2 × size ÷ 24 per the recorded icon rule, which is what the Icon collection's modes express.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.fixedHere: 5.5 Usage Analytics carried an unnamed 'Frame 1' with an unbound gap of 16 — the last generic name on the page. Named 'row' and bound to spacing/4. 5.5 had never been linted because it was out of scope for the MANAGE pass.
tokenisationAudit2026_09_04.forTheBuild: A developer reading the code tokens will find --border-w-* and the icon stroke rule already documented in CLAUDE.md; the Figma side matches for colour, type, spacing, radius and effects, and diverges only on the six masters above. Binding those six is a small sweep and should happen before Table is built, so the new component inherits a bound hairline rather than adding a seventh.

masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.what: Bound the stroke weights and gaps on the seven component masters the audit named, and moved the Icon collection default from 24 to 16 so an unpinned icon resolves to 1.33 rather than 2.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.theSweep: Dialog 503:150, Button 76:300 (240 variants, 384 side bindings), Card 1812:800, Drawer 514:236, Toast/Card 601:257, DropdownMenu/Content 546:52 and Alert 416:141. 602 per-side stroke-weight bindings and 20 itemSpacing bindings, every literal matched to an existing border-width/* or spacing/* token — 0 unmapped. Zero-weight sides are left alone: a side at 0 means no border there, and binding it would draw one.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.bindEveryNONZEROSideNotAllFour: The first read-back said Dialog still had 4 unbound and Drawer 12. Both were already correct — they are dividers with a stroke on ONE side and 0 on the other three, and the check demanded all four sides be bound. A node is tokenised when every side that actually draws is bound. Same shape as the per-side lesson below: the rule has to match how Figma stores the thing.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.iconDefaultModeWasTwentyFour: The owner reported that changing an icon defaults its stroke to 2 when it should be 1.33. Confirmed: the Icon collection's default mode was 24, and icon/stroke-weight resolves 24 -> icon-border-width/lg = 2. An icon with no pinned mode inherits that. The evidence that the fix was safe: across this page 1,888 nodes pin mode 16, 275 pin 14, 308 pin 12, and NOTHING pins 20 or 24 — so nothing depended on the default being 24, and the 37 vectors rendering at 2 were getting it by accident.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.defaultModeIdHasNoSetterButSetDefaultMod: collection.defaultModeId = id throws 'no setter for property', which reads like the API cannot do it. Enumerating the prototype found setDefaultMode() alongside addMode/removeMode/renameMode. Probe the prototype before concluding an API is missing. Reordering modes was the alternative and would have been catastrophic — 1,888 nodes pin mode ids, and renaming or re-adding modes to change the order would have repointed every one of them.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.iconStrokeWeightWasAllScopes: icon/stroke-weight carried ALL_SCOPES, which the file's own rule calls out as polluting every property picker. Narrowed to STROKE_FLOAT.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.textOverridesInStatTilesWereLost: After the sweeps, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3's first stat tile had reverted from 'Waiting on you' to 'Pending approvals' — the text of the 1.1 tile they were cloned from — while 2.4 and 2.5 kept theirs. Caught by reading the final screenshot, not by any assertion. Restored on all three. The cause is not established: a text node set directly inside an instance is an override, and something between the build and the audit dropped three of five. Set instance text through a component PROPERTY where one exists rather than by writing the TEXT node, and re-read text after any master-level work.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.openItems: FeaturedIcon's border weight is unbound (25 instances) — it was not in the audit's original list and was not swept. 95 icon vectors still carry a hardcoded weight rather than binding icon/stroke-weight; binding them needs a mode pinned per icon size and is a separate pass. Skeleton's 28 gradients cannot bind and are correct. On 1.1 the fourth stat tile is named 'stat — live promotions' but reads 'Dashboards promoted / in Dart Central' — flagged, not changed, since it may be a deliberate owner edit.
masterSweepAndIconDefault2026_09_04.verification: Final audit over 50 frames: nodes authored on the screens are 0 in every category — fill, stroke colour, border weight, icon weight, unstyled text, style overrides, padding, gap, radius, effects. Remaining inside instances: 25 FeaturedIcon borders, 95 hardcoded icon vectors, 28 Skeleton gradients.

queueKpis2026_09_04.what: Section 2's KPI row is now New · Pending · Awaiting · Oldest, on the owner's call that those are the only four an admin acts on. 'Decided' was dropped — a count of things already finished is a scoreboard, not a queue metric.
queueKpis2026_09_04.mapping: New = status New (submitted, not opened yet). Pending = status Needs review (in review, not yet decided). Awaiting = status Awaiting reply (with the requester). Oldest = age of the oldest row in New or Needs review, captioned with its reference and submission date. Counts derive from each frame's own rows: 2.1/2.3/2.4/2.5 read 2 · 2 · 1 · 13 days (#0412, 08/22/2026); the Aiden-scoped 2.2 reads 0 · 1 · 0 · 5 days (#0419, 08/30/2026).
queueKpis2026_09_04.theTileTitleIsTheLayerName: Owner renamed 1.1's fourth tile to 'Dashboards promoted' — 'Live promotions' read like selling something, when the point is that these dashboards carry a Promoted badge. Its layer name still said 'live promotions'. All four LAND frames' stat tiles are now named from their own title text, closing the same mismatch class that produced the wrong write on the banner-count tile earlier.
queueKpis2026_09_04.colourSwap: New and Pending swapped value colours across all five queue frames — New now reads status/info/base (blue), Pending status/error/base (red). Positions unchanged: New, Pending, Awaiting, Oldest. Both were inherited from 1.1's stat row when the tiles were cloned, where red sat on the first tile. Red now marks the count that is actually overdue attention — something already opened and still undecided — while a new arrival is informational. Done by exchanging the bound fill variables on each tile's 'stat value' text, so both stay tokenised.

openItems2026_09_04.1_tableNotInCode: THE BLOCKER. There is no src/components/Table — Table exists in Figma only, as the recorded proposal. openItems2026_09_04.2_tableSelectedPlusHoverToken: Table's own recorded open question, still unanswered: selected + hover has no token. selected is --primary-light, hover is neutral --accent, and stacked they are a color-mix nothing expresses. openItems2026_09_04.4_hardcodedIconVectors: 95 icon vectors still carry a literal stroke weight instead of binding icon/stroke-weight. Binding them needs the right Icon mode pinned per icon size (12/14/16/20/24), so it is a considered pass rather than a sweep. The default is now 16 → 1.33, so an unpinned icon lands correctly.
openItems2026_09_04.5_denyIsTheOnlyColourOnTheDecisionBar: On 3.1–3.5 Deny is an error-outline button isolated bottom-left, and it is the only colour in the bar, so the eye lands on it first on a screen where approve is the common case. The separation is deliberate and right; the suggestion is a neutral outline with the confirm dialog carrying the danger. Owner has not ruled.
openItems2026_09_04.6_noBulkOnRequestMoreInformation: Recorded as a decision, not a gap: bulk actions are Approve and Deny only, because Request more information asks a different question of each requester.
openItems2026_09_04.7_skeletonGradients: Not a defect. Skeleton's 28 shimmer sweeps are gradient fills and cannot bind to a colour variable, the same reasoning already recorded for Mark's artwork.
openItems2026_09_04.8_theShellIsNotInAnyScreen: Every screen frame is drawn as its content column only. The app shell — sidebar nav, two permission variants — lives as two reference frames in READ FIRST and appears in no screen. A developer reading a screen frame will not see the navigation that surrounds it.
openItems2026_09_04.9_cardInteractiveIsCodeOnly: Card has no interactive axis in Figma — its props are Title/Description/Body/slots/Size/Divider. The request cards' titles are now bound to text/primary-main-text on all five LAND frames so the route is visible, but the card-level interactive treatment (border to --border-hover, lift, shadow on hover) exists only in code and has no resting-state representation to draw. Build note, not a Figma gap.
openItems2026_09_04.10_fourFiveDuplicatesFiveOneB: 4.5 and 5.1b draw the same Edit dashboard drawer. 4.5 sits in APPLY and predates 5.1b. One should go; owner's call which.

routesPanel2026_09_04.what: ④ ROUTES — what leads where (2417:9045), a 42-row table of every navigation edge in the admin flow and the control that produces it: From · You click · Goes to · Note. Built by cloning the data-contract panel so it inherits that section’s shape.
routesPanel2026_09_04.whyItEarnsItsPlace: The flow map shows STAGES; it does not show what you click. The end-to-end critique found two dead ends and a hidden primary route precisely because nothing recorded the edges. A row here is a thing a developer has to wire — and the table is assertable in a way prose is not: every frame it names must exist, and every screen must appear at least once in 'Goes to'.
routesPanel2026_09_04.theAssertionFoundRealGaps: First run: 0 dangling references but 17 screens with no stated way in. Most were an artefact of range notation — '3.1 – 3.5' does not literally contain 3.2 — so the checker now expands ranges. The rest were genuine and got rows: 1.5 (a consequence of removing the last widget, not a destination you choose), 5.1d/5.1e/5.1f (states reached by a condition rather than a click), 5.3a, 5.4a and 6.1a. Final: 42 rows, 0 dangling, and only 2.2 and 2.5 with no route in — 2.2 is a permission variant of 2.1 reached through the same sidebar item, and 2.5 is labelled a reference sheet, not a screen. Both correct.
routesPanel2026_09_04.itSurfacedADuplicateScreen: Writing the rows made it obvious that 4.5 'Dashboards — edit drawer (manual, no request)' and 5.1b 'Dashboards — edit drawer' are the SAME screen drawn twice — same drawer, same title, same fields. 4.5 predates 5.1b. Recorded as a row rather than silently deleted; one of them should go, and that is an owner call.
routesPanel2026_09_04.dialogsAndToastsAreNotRoutes: A confirm dialog opens over the screen you are on and returns you to it, so those rows say 'dialog' in Goes to rather than naming a frame. Same for toasts. Listing them as destinations would have made the queue look like it navigates away on every decision, which is the opposite of what 2.4 is for.
routesPanel2026_09_04.theShellIsStatedAtTheTop: The panel’s caption carries the thing a screen frame cannot show: every frame is its content column only, the sidebar exists as two reference frames, and so every route beginning “Sidebar” is real but invisible in the screens.
routesPanel2026_09_04.verification: Panel lint: unbound paint 0, unstyled text 0, generic names 0, unbound geometry 0, unbound stroke weight 0. READ FIRST relaid out to eight frames in a grid with the new panel in place; 0 overlaps, 0 out-of-bounds across the page.

blockersPanelAndToggleFinding2026_09_04.note: Two owner decisions from 4 Sep. The toggle one was chosen, built, measured, disproved and reverted; the scheduling one was recorded rather than built, at the owner's instruction.

togglePressedColour_REVERTED.decision: Owner chose 'colour the active label' to fix not being able to tell which filter toggle is active.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.built: Toggle plain + Pressed=true label moved from text/foreground to text/primary-main-text, on all six variants (sm/default/lg x Disabled false/true), node ids 1736:396, 1736:399, 1736:408, 1736:411, 1736:420, 1736:423. Mirrored in src/components/Toggle/Toggle.scss.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.disproved: Measured worse in every case. Pressed-vs-unpressed contrast went 2.36:1 -> 1.49:1 in light and 1.18:1 -> 1.14:1 in dark. In Figma text/primary-main-text resolves to the SAME hex under all seven Brand modes (#2e3b4f light, #d2dbe5 dark) because it aliases primary-main, which no brand remaps. In code the base theme's --primary-main is slate (#cbd5e1 dark), so --primary-text has no hue to offer; only the six themed subtrees that remap --primary would benefit, and the Admin Flow screen frames pin no Brand mode, so they inherit Slate.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.reverted: All six variants restored to text/foreground and asserted (12 pressed = text/foreground, 12 unpressed = text/muted-foreground, zero primary-main-text left in the set). The SCSS diff is now comment-only; tsc and test:contrast pass.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.whyTheContrastTestMissedIt: test:contrast gates text against SURFACES. Both labels clear AA against the background (12.76:1 for the pressed one). The failure is between two FOREGROUNDS, which nothing in the suite currently gates.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.rootCause: --muted-foreground in dark (#e2e8f0) sits one step from --foreground (#f8fafc). Every muted-versus-normal text pair in the library collapses in dark, not just this control. Same origin as the recorded Tabs indicator finding.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.openOptions: Owner call, neither taken: (a) retheme dark --muted-foreground, which touches the whole library, or (b) use the line toggle variant in filter bars so a --primary bar carries the state instead of colour, which is a zero-code instance swap and is what Tabs already does.
togglePressedColour_REVERTED.recordedIn: Toggle.stories.tsx changelog 2026-09-04 (a no-code-change entry, so the dead end is not retried) and a comment block in Toggle.scss.

schedulingRecordedNotBuilt.decision: Owner: 'for now just list it as a blocker in the documentation.' Not built.
schedulingRecordedNotBuilt.gap: Approve and Apply both act immediately. Nothing in the flow can answer 'when'.
schedulingRecordedNotBuilt.whatExists: 4.2's banner drawer already carries Starts and Ends, and 5.2's stated rule is that a banner displays only when its switch is on and today falls inside its dates - so banners already schedule themselves, but 4.2's copy reads as immediate and never says so. 4.1's dashboard form has no dates at all (Name, Project, Inventory, Lifecycle, Tableau link). 'Approved - not applied' is already a manual hold, but the queue's statuses do not separate applied from waiting, so nothing surfaces it.
schedulingRecordedNotBuilt.whyNotDesigned: A timed apply is a backend capability - a job that fires at a future time - not a screen. The capability has to be decided before a date picker goes onto 4.1 or 4.2.

generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.note: Owner: 3.3 had no reply destination, Reply and Request more information read as the same thing, and there was no way to open a feature request from a General one. All three were real; the file's own data contract confirmed the third.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.finding_replyVsRmi: 3.3's bar was Close - Request more information - Reply, i.e. THREE buttons, two of which compose a message into the same thread. The contract did define them differently: Reply leaves the state unchanged and keeps it in your queue; Request more information sets awaiting_requester and removes it. The difference was a pure side effect that neither label stated, and Reply had no surface at all.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.finding_featureRequest: The DATA CONTRACT already declared a canonical 'feature' type - admin sees 'never enters the queue', approving creates 'A public backlog entry, upvotable' - with NO screen and no route. Meanwhile #0419, the General request drawn on 3.3, is literally a feature ask ('is that possible today, and if not is it on the roadmap?'). It came in as general because that was the only door.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.fix_composer: The ACTIVITY thread gained a composer at its foot - textarea plus an explicit outcome radio ('Keep in my queue' / 'Hand back - they reply next') and a Send reply button. Both message verbs left the bar, which is now Close + Open a feature request. The previously invisible side effect is now chosen where you can see it, at the point of sending.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.fix_composerDefault: 'Keep in my queue' is the checked default, deliberately: it preserves the documented Reply transition, and the other option carries the side effect of leaving your queue. A first pass had them inverted because the option-matching regex /check|select|on/ matched 'Unchecked' - caught by reading back the resolved values rather than trusting the write.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.fix_featureRoute: New frame 3.6 (2452:9336) - the base 3.3 screen under a scrim with a right drawer, 'Open a feature request'. Prefilled and editable Title, Detail and Category, a warning Alert stating it becomes a public upvotable entry, and a note saying #0419 closes with its thread recording where it went. Footer is Cancel / Open request. The drawer IS the confirmation - the text being published is on screen, so a second dialog would be ceremony.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.whyEditableBeforePublishing: The requester wrote that text privately to an admin. Publishing it verbatim to a public backlog is the actual risk in this flow, which is why the drawer is editable rather than a straight confirm.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.dataContractUpdated: general row action bar -> 'Reply in the thread - Open a feature request - Close'. feature row -> 'never enters the queue - opened FROM a General request'. The Reply transition now reads 'unchanged - or awaiting_requester' and explains the composer choice. A new transition row was added: new/in_review -> Open a feature request (General only) -> closed, creating the public backlog entry.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.routesUpdated: The stale '3.3 -> 2.1 via Reply - Close' row now reads Close only and says why. Three rows added: 3.3 -> 3.6, 3.6 -> 2.1, 3.6 -> 3.3. Table is 45 rows.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.prototype: 128 reactions, 39 of 44 frames reachable, zero dangling. Send reply is deliberately NOT wired - replying does not leave the screen - and the reaction it inherited from the old Reply button was cleared. 3.6's base layer has all reactions removed so only the drawer is live, which is what modal means.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.lesson_absolutePositioning: layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE' makes x/y PARENT-RELATIVE. Setting canvas coordinates (frame.x + offset) put the scrim and drawer 3696px outside the frame, where they clipped and rendered as nothing. 5.1b's own values (scrim 0,0 / drawer 716,0) were the reference that made it obvious - copy a working sibling's numbers rather than computing from absolute positions.
generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute202.lesson_staleExportCache: get_screenshot served a STALE raster for node ids 2125:41404 and 2125:41417 across many attempts, showing a narrow inner box in the composer that does not exist. Proof it was the cache and not the file: two requests either side of a real mutation returned byte-identical MD5s, and 3.6 - a clone with identical content on a NEW node id - rendered correctly. Three independent structural reads agreed: 34 nodes in the card, exactly one stroked box, 832 wide, uniform 1px sides. When a render disagrees with repeated measurement, hash two renders across a mutation before believing the picture.

barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.note: Supersedes the radio in generalRequestComposerAndFeatureRoute2026_09_04. The owner asked two questions - does Request more information open the reply box, and why does the composer need radio buttons - and both exposed real faults in what had just been built.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.finding_rmiWasDeadOnEveryScreen: Request more information had ZERO reactions on 3.1, 3.2, 3.4 and 3.5, and no row in the ROUTES table. Its confirm dialog existed on the ACTION DIALOGS board but was never wired to a review screen. barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.finding_radioWasRedundant: The radio encoded the choice the two buttons had encoded - the same number of decisions, relocated. Testing whether 'reply and keep it in my queue' is a real outcome: asking a question hands back, giving a complete answer should close, and replying-and-keeping leaves an item in the queue with nothing pending on either side, which is clutter rather than a state. The third case does not exist, so the outcome belongs on the verb.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.rule: ONE rule, no exceptions: the action bar decides, the thread talks. Every review screen's ACTIVITY card ends in a composer; the bar carries only decisions.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.bars: 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.4 / 3.5 are now Deny + Approve. 3.3 is Close + Open a feature request. Request more information is deleted from all five.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.verbs: Asset screens carry one verb, Send, because they have no Close - approving or denying ends them. 3.3 carries Send and Send & close, because answering a General question and ending it is the common case. Each verb states its own outcome, which is what the labels never did before.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.consequenceText: The copy from the retired RMI dialog moved under the composer as helper text, so nothing was lost: 'Sending hands this back - <name> sees Needs your reply, and it leaves your queue until they answer.' barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.dialogNotSuperseded: CORRECTION made during the pass: the more-info dialog was first relabelled SUPERSEDED, which was wrong - 2.4's row menu and 2.6's bulk bar still offer Request more information, and from the queue there is no thread on screen, so a dialog is the only surface available. It is now labelled 'reached from 2.4 and 2.6 only - the review screens use the thread composer'.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.dataContract: The four asset type rows read 'Approve - Deny - questions go in the thread composer'. The general row reads 'Close - Open a feature request - replies go in the thread composer'. The RMI transition became 'Send (thread composer, every review screen)' -> awaiting_requester and records that the button it replaced was wired to nothing. The old Reply transition became 'Send & close (General only)' -> closed.
barDecidesThreadTalks2026_09_04.routes: Two rows added - '3.1-3.5 -> 2.1 via Send' and '3.3 -> 2.1 via Send & close'. Table is 47 rows.

replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.note: Design critique of the reply flow. The owner's instinct was right on both counts, and checking it surfaced two things I had asserted that were false.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.myError_1: I told the owner Feature Request was 'a declared request type with no screen'. WRONG. The Request Flow page has a complete requester-side section 6 - form, ready-to-submit, and its own outcome screen ('Request submitted - feature request'). What it lacks is an ADMIN review screen, correctly, because feature requests never enter the queue.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.myError_2: The 3.6 drawer claimed opening a feature request lets the requester 'follow the backlog entry rather than losing the thread'. The behaviour spec says the opposite: 'FEATURE REQUESTS ARE THE EXCEPTION AND DO NOT APPEAR ON MY REQUESTS AT ALL' and 'You will not get an email'. So after conversion her General request reads Closed in DONE and the thing it became is invisible to her - indistinguishable from a rejection.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.myError_3: I built the admin composer three commits earlier without ever opening the Request Flow page, which already had one. The spec had documented the model all along: 'Request detail - the thread, and the only place a person can reply.' Landing on the same shape was luck, not method.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.fix_goDark: The closing thread entry now carries the outcome and a link. New frame 'Request detail - closed, became a feature request' shows what Lena sees: status Closed (soft badge, matching the admin queue's own Closed), and an admin entry reading 'This is not something we can do today, but it is a good idea - so I have turned it into a feature request...' with a link-styled button to the backlog entry. The thread is the ONLY surviving channel, so this is required, not decorative.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.fix_composerCollapsed: One behaviour on both sides: the thread ends in a Reply button that expands the composer in place. Collapsed by default, because an always-open textarea out-weighed the decision on the asset screens - on 3.1 it was ~170px of empty box above Deny/Approve, and the critique's own 'what draws the eye first' test failed there.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.newFrames: Following the file's own 5.1a-f convention, every review screen gained its expanded counterpart: 3.1a, 3.2a, 3.3a (renamed from a first pass as 3.7), 3.4a, 3.5a. Section 3 is now 11 frames, relaid out as a wrapped grid, 3664x4192, no overlaps.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.fix_consistencyDrift: Four drifts levelled between the two halves. Verb: both now 'Send reply' (was admin 'Send'). Field label: both show 'Your reply' (admin had none). Separator above the composer: added to the admin side (requester already had one). Consequence text: added to the requester side (admin already had one) - 'Sending puts this back with the DART Central admin team - your request returns to Pending review.'
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.fix_36Fields: 3.6's drawer now matches the REAL feature-request form - Feature title, Describe the feature, Business impact - replacing Title / Detail / Category. Category was never a feature field; I had borrowed it from the General form. Owner's decision: the ADMIN writes Business impact, because a General request never asks for one and the backlog ranks on it. The field ships empty with a prompting placeholder.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.prototype: 150 reactions, 44 of 49 frames reachable, zero dangling. Reply routes to each screen's own expanded frame; the only dead Reply is 3.6's, which sits behind a scrim and is correct.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.bug_renameThenDelete: A rewrite loop renamed 'row - message source' to 'row - message', and the following delete loop - which removed the banner-specific rows by name - then deleted the row that had just been written, leaving the ORIGINAL 'row - message' with the banner's copy. It rendered as a General request whose Message read '8:00 AM - 12:00 PM ET'. Caught in the screenshot, not the assertions, because the assertion only counted rows. Never rename into a namespace a later delete pass will sweep.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.bug_glyphIsNotAVariant: Copying a FeaturedIcon's componentProperties (Color/Shape/Size/Appearance) does NOT move the icon - the glyph is a nested INSTANCE_SWAP, so the frame kept Icon/bell on a General request. Fixed with swapComponent against the source's mainComponent.
replyLoopBothSides2026_09_04.lesson_cloneSubtree: A freshly cloned frame's instance subtree is not queryable in the SAME script - findOne returns null. Clone in one call, mutate in the next. Hit twice now.

separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.note: Owner spotted it in the render: a stray vertical tick above the reply composer where a hairline should be.
separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.bug: All ten composer separators on the Admin Flow page were the VERTICAL variant - a 1x20 tick sitting above the field instead of a full-width rule. Cloning an instance copies its variant, and the source I cloned was 'ui-separator [filter axes]' from 2.1, which separates two toggle groups side by side and is therefore vertical by design.
separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.whyItSurvived: Three checks passed over it. design-check lint has nothing to say - a vertical separator is valid geometry with bound tokens and a real style. layoutSizingHorizontal = 'FILL' silently does nothing useful to a vertical separator. And 3.3a, the ONE admin frame built from a different clone source, happened to pick up a horizontal separator - so the only frame whose separator I had reason to trust was the only correct one.
separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.fix: Every 'ui-separator [composer]' on the page set to Variant=horizontal and FILL: 832x1 on all eleven frames. Section 3 relaid out afterwards because each frame lost ~19px of height; 3664x4116, no overlaps.
separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.emphasisLadderChecked: While in there, verified the button ladder reads correctly rather than trusting the render: Reply = default/outline, Deny = error/outline, Approve = default/default, Send reply = default/default (primary inside the composer, where it is the action), Send & close = default/outline, Close = default/ghost.
separatorOrientationBug2026_09_04.lesson: Cloning an instance to reuse its tokens also inherits its VARIANT, and a variant can be semantically wrong while being structurally perfect. Clone from a source that plays the same role, not merely one that is the same component - and screenshot the first frame after adding a cloned component, which is the step I skipped here.

buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.note: Two new sections on the Admin Flow page, at the owner's request: what a developer actually ships, and the journeys that cross both halves.
buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.section7: '7 · BUILD — every screen a developer ships' (2488:9940). Six columns of boxes in the existing flow-map vocabulary: SHELL 1, REQUESTER 8, ADMIN TRIAGE 3, ADMIN APPLY 1, ADMIN MANAGE 6, ADMIN CONFIGURE 1 = 20 screens.
buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.theDistinctionItMakes: A SCREEN is a route built once; a FRAME is one state of it. buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.countCorrection: An earlier answer in this workstream said TEN screens. That was admin-only and predated 3.6 and the replying states. The admin side is 11 (the earlier 10 plus 4.6 Applied as its own route); with the 8 requester screens and the shell it is 20.

buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.section8: '8 · USER FLOWS — end to end, both sides' (2490:9940). buildListAndUserFlows2026_09_05.whyTheseFive: Each page already had its own flow map, but both stop at the boundary. conventions: Marks are built the playbook's way: figma.createNodeFromSvg with the real lucide path data, rescaled by size/24 so the stroke keeps lucide's 2/24 ratio, and the inner vector named 'glyph' so the design-check lint does not flag it.
