The mark gradient uses gradientTransform [[0.7071,0.7071,-0.2071],[-0.7071,0.7071,0.5]] — the 135deg diagonal the CSS uses. Horizontal ramps use [[1,0,0],[0,1,0]].

The hero bubble field is ELLIPSES with GRADIENT_RADIAL fills (opaque centre -> transparent edge) inside a clipped frame, not a multi-fill radial on one rect. A radial paint's default transform maps to the node's bounds, so an ellipse gives the bloom for free and each wash stays independently positionable.
'Infinite possibilities.' is a TEXT node with a GRADIENT_LINEAR fill — Figma fills text with a gradient natively, so the shipped --gradient-full-ramp is reproduced exactly rather than mocked.

Do not trust a counter you increment inside a fills.map() to prove a change landed — on the first sweep the aiden counter read 0 while the value had in fact changed. Read the resulting values back instead.

rebuild_2026_08_07.technique: DOM -> Figma. A browser-side extractor walks the rendered story and emits a compact scene graph (box / text / svg) with absolute geometry and computed paint; a Figma-side builder replays it as rectangles, TEXT nodes and createNodeFromSvg. Charts come over as real vectors, not images.
lessons: createNodeFromSvg resolves NO CSS - not currentColor, not var(--chart-1), not a stylesheet rule. Every paint must be burned into the markup as a literal attribute while the live element is still readable.
Chrome serialises color-mix() results as color(srgb r g b), which Figma's SVG parser rejects. Convert to rgb() before handing it over.

sr-only wrappers are 1x1 with overflow hidden, but their CHILDREN still report full-size rects - the chart's table twin was captured and painted over the chart. Prune any subtree whose own box is under 2px in BOTH axes.
A disc or pill carries its radius on a PARENT, so a filled child reads radius 0 and paints a square inside the circle. Inherit the ancestor radius when the child effectively fills it.
Figma's Inter measures wider than Chrome's, so text that is one line in the browser wraps here. Flag single-line text at extract time and let it self-size, re-anchoring by alignment.

CROSS-BRAND remapping is safe and cheap: within one mode the layout is identical, so a clone plus a ~13-pair colour map reproduces a sibling brand exactly (verified 1:1, zero conflicts). CROSS-MODE remapping is NOT safe - white maps to page, card AND ink, so each mode needs its own extract.
ec dark is the one brand whose chart slot 1 is not its --primary, so the blanket map paints its bars with the wrong blue. Its chart subtree and legend dot are corrected explicitly after the clone.

suite_built.bug_found_and_fixed_in_the_payloads: Every suite payload carried stop-color="circle" on lib entries 5 and 6. Cause: a CSS radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, ...) head has no explicit radii, so it does not match the `RW% RH% at X% Y%` shape the converter expects and falls through into the STOP LIST — the keyword became a colour. Perfectly parseable SVG, invalid paint, and invisible to every existing check. Stripped from all six files and a guard added to scripts/figma-build-dryrun.mjs (verified it bites: reintroducing one turns suite-light-1 from ok to failed=6 MISMATCH). Marketing was never affected — its radial gradients all use the explicit-radii form.
suite_built.known_defect_not_fixed: SIX text nodes in Suite render BLACK instead of their intended gradient: the four stat numbers (500K+, 2M+, 50B+, 99.9%) and both halves of the 'dart' wordmark. In dark mode they are effectively invisible. Cause is at EXTRACTION time, not replay: those elements use background-clip:text, so their computed `color` is transparent; rgba() returns null on zero alpha and the extractor falls back to [0,0,0,1]. Marketing has the same six black fallbacks but every one of them ALSO captured a `g` gradient, which overrides the fill — so it renders correctly and the bug stayed hidden. 'Infinite possibilities.' in Suite did capture its gradient and renders as the rainbow. Fix: re-extract Suite with the transparent-colour case handled, or hand-set those six fills in Figma.

languageSweep.gotcha: A DIRECT WRITE TO .characters SILENTLY FAILS when the text is driven by a component TEXT property. lessons: INSTANCE_SWAP via setProperties takes a NODE ID. A component key is REJECTED with "Property value is incompatible with component property type" — confirmed by a controlled test that tried both against the same icon. This matches the earlier addComponentProperty finding.

NOT EVERY NESTED GLYPH IS A PROPERTY. Mark's Glyph and Sidebar/MenuButton's icon do not surface on the parent instance's componentProperties, so setProperties silently does nothing and every tile renders the default. Both had to be swapped with swapComponent() on the nested INSTANCE. The rail shipped six identical chart glyphs until this was caught by LOOKING at it — no error was raised at any point.
Sidebar/MenuButton exposes no icon swap property at all; every instance defaults to Icon/house. Worth adding an INSTANCE_SWAP to that set — a nav is the one place every row needs a different icon.
TEXT CAN BE APPENDED INTO A SLOT inside an instance. The Recent rows' trailing app name is a real text node placed in ui-item__actions, which is what a slot is for.
appendChild() returns void — chaining `.name` onto it throws "cannot set property name of null".
layoutPositioning = ABSOLUTE requires the PARENT to have a layoutMode. A plain createFrame() badge slot throws; createAutoLayout() with a fixed size works.

nestedInstanceSweep.why: Owner hit it composing a Dialog: a ToggleGroup dropped on the canvas offered no way to set a segment's variant, pressed or size. nestedInstanceSweep.exposed: 30 nested instances across 7 hosts: AvatarGroup (Avatar x4), Command/Palette (Heading x2, Item x6), Dialog (CloseButton, Button x2), Drawer (CloseButton, Button x2), FullScreenDialog (CloseButton, Input, Button x2), Menubar (Trigger x4), Toast/Card (Progress, Button x2, CloseButton). Exposure PROPAGATES to the matching instance in every sibling variant, so Dialog reads 4/4 and Toast 10/10 afterwards.
deliberatelyNotExposed: Button / Button-Icon-only -> Spinner (240 instances). The loading indicator is not configurable content; exposing it would put a Spinner section in the panel of the most-used component in the library.
Mark artwork/* -> Mark glyph/db. The glyph is already reachable as the tile's INSTANCE_SWAP property.
Command/Separator — no component properties, so Figma refuses (see lessons).
nestedInstanceSweep.alreadySlotHosted: Attachment, Combobox/Content, ContextMenu/Content, DropdownMenu/Content, Field, HoverCard/Content, Item, Select/Content put their sub-parts in SLOTs. That is the better answer, not a gap — the designer replaces the content wholesale — and Figma will not let a slot's contents be exposed anyway.
lessons: isExposedInstance THROWS, it does not no-op, and the script is atomic — one bad node loses the whole run. Two rejections to guard for: 'Cannot expose instances within slots' (walk ancestors for type SLOT) and 'Can only expose instances that have exposed nested instances or children with component property references' (the nested component must actually HAVE properties — narrow to the COMPONENT_SET or non-variant COMPONENT before reading componentPropertyDefinitions).

page.findAllWithCriteria() DOES NOT descend into instances; the same call on a top-level child of the page does. Every file-wide sweep must iterate page.children and search from each child, or it silently under-reports. A first pass over cancel-styled buttons found 15; the correct traversal found 31 across 396 Button instances. The same trap made 54 component pages look like they had no changelog date at all.

footerButtonSweep.rule: A dismissal action is style=ghost. Recorded in CLAUDE.md the same day, together with the Toast carve-out (Toast keeps outline — owner's call, ToastCard.tsx hard-codes it).
footerButtonSweep.fixed: Dialog main (both alignments) and Drawer main (all four sides): cancel Outline -> Ghost. Dialog's destructive confirm Default -> Error. Button page examples 171:516 / 171:541 ("Keep") -> Ghost. 37 Dialog/Drawer instances inherit, so the two mains carried all of it.
footerButtonSweep.regressionAndRepair: Changing a VARIANT property on a nested instance inside a MAIN component resets that nested instance's overrides on every existing instance of the parent. Ten instances silently lost their footer labels — AlertDialog's Discard/Save, Keep editing, Stay signed in/Sign out, Dialog's Send invite x2, Drawer's Cancel/Share x2 — reverting to the main's Cancel/Delete. All ten were restored from the pre-change snapshot. Title, description and body overrides were NOT affected: the reset is scoped to the swapped nested instance's subtree.
footerButtonSweep.lesson: Before touching a nested instance inside a main component, SNAPSHOT every instance's overrides for that subtree. The write itself reports success and the overrides vanish without an error — the only way to catch it is to re-read the instances afterwards and diff against the snapshot. This is the same class of failure as the 2026-08-08 language sweep, where 127 of 152 text edits silently did nothing.
footerButtonSweep.notFixed: Drawer's Reset/Apply examples keep their labels. Reset is a real secondary action, not a dismissal, and the labels are the page's chosen filter-drawer example — only the style was corrected. The code story (Drawer.stories.tsx) pairs Cancel/Save changes instead, so the page and the story still show different compositions; owner's call whether to converge them.

handDrawnPartSweep.why: Follow-on from the ToggleGroup rebuild: a sweep found ten more components drawing by hand a part that exists as its own Figma atom. Group 1 (the small, high-traffic ones) was done here.

done.ButtonGroup: Three hand-drawn ui-button frames -> exposed Button instances (Default · Outline · Default size). 202x36 and 76x106 unchanged. Zero instances existed, so nothing to repair.
done.Card: Header-action badge and footer buttons, both inside SLOTs, -> Badge and Button instances. Slot contents cannot be exposed, but slot content IS directly editable on an instance, so that is the right shape. SIZE CORRECTION: the hand-drawn badge was 16px tall against Badge's real 24px, so cards carrying one grow 8px.
done.Empty: Action button -> Button instance. It hugs its label at 127px where the hand-drawn copy was a fixed 151px.
done.Code: CodeBlock copy button -> exposed Button/Icon-only (Default · Ghost · XSmall), geometry identical at 20x20.
done.Chat: Marker status dot -> StatusDot (online, sm); running ToolCall icon -> Spinner (16); composer send -> Button/Icon-only (Aiden, round). Send resizes 32 -> 30 inheriting Button's icon-only Small.

newDefectsFound: Button/Icon-only paints its glyph with text/foreground on EVERY non-aiden Style=Default variant — a dark navy glyph on the dark navy primary fill, i.e. an effectively invisible icon. Only the Aiden variant binds a proper on-fill colour (aiden/primary-foreground). Confirmed by screenshot of the master, not inferred. NOT FIXED — it is a Button-page job.
Figma's Button/Icon-only Small is 30x30; the code computes 32 (padding --p-2 8px + 16px glyph). XSmall is 20x20 against a computed 24. Icon-only geometry on the Button page needs its own parity pass.

SETTING AN INSTANCE_SWAP PROPERTY RESETS COLOUR OVERRIDES ON THE SWAPPED INSTANCE. The Chat send button's glyph came back dark after the icon swap because the variant's white stroke override did not survive. Rebind after every swap and verify by reading the stroke back, not by assuming.
handDrawnPartSweep.mistakeMade: The snapshot-before-you-touch rule was applied to Card but NOT to Empty, Code or Chat. Empty is exactly where it bit: replacing the slot's default button reset the label override on the two 'a fresh project' example cells, which reverted to the main's 'New message' under the title 'Start your first board'. The original text is unrecoverable from the file (no plugin API access to version history), so they were relabelled 'Create board' — a chosen value, not the original. Apply the rule to EVERY host, not just the one with many instances.
handDrawnPartSweep.remaining: Group 2: Alert and Banner have no dismiss control at all (12 and 6 variants, zero CloseButton instances on either page). Group 3: the Label sweep (Checkbox 54, Switch 36, RadioGroup 36, Slider 12 hand-drawn label rows) needs a decision on whether Figma's Label covers the three sizes first. Then NativeSelect/Textarea -> Input field wrap, and FullScreenDialog -> Dialog, which belongs with that page's v4 rebuild.

group2.what: Alert (12 variants) and Banner (6) had NO dismiss control anywhere and zero CloseButton instances on either page, despite both composing CloseButton in code via onClose. Both sets gained a 'Show close' BOOLEAN wired to an exposed CloseButton instance (Variant=default, Size=default = 24px, matching CloseButton's own code default).
group2.defaultOff: The property defaults to FALSE so none of the 58 existing instances moved. Three examples were switched on to document the affordance: Alert 419:161 and 419:214 (the 'Saved' success example, light and dark) and Banner 424:112.
group2.colorInherit: The stylesheet says `.ui-alert__close { color: inherit; opacity: --o-70 }`, which Figma has no equivalent for. Each variant's close glyph is therefore bound to the SAME variable its own title and leading icon use — text/foreground, primary-text, or status/{info,success,warning,error}/base — and the instance carries opacity 0.7. Verified by screenshotting all 18 variants, not by reading the write back.
group2.lesson: A HIDDEN INSTANCE HAS NO CHILDREN. Figma does not build the subtree of an instance whose visible is false, so findAllWithCriteria returns zero vectors and a screenshot of it renders blank — indistinguishable from 'the node has no glyph'. The first binding pass silently reached only 2 of 18 variants while reporting success on all 18, because the two happened to be materialised. Fix: editComponentProperty(key, {defaultValue: true}) to reveal them, bind, then set it back to false. Any edit to content behind a boolean-hidden layer needs this.
group2.stillMissing: Neither Alert nor Banner models its `action` slot (React.ReactNode in code — Alert's is the one that reads --primary-main so it stays neutral inside a themed page). By the file's own convention a ReactNode is a SLOT, so that is a slot addition, not a boolean, and was left for the owner.

group3_notDone.verdict: STOPPED ON EVIDENCE — do not rebuild Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup or Slider labels as Label instances unless the owner overrules this.
group3_notDone.correction: An earlier note said Figma's Label had no size axis and that was the blocker. Wrong on both counts: Label carries Size (default|sm|lg) x Disabled, and the real blocker is different.
group3_notDone.evidence: Every hand-drawn label ALREADY uses the same shared text style and the same bound colour as the Label component, at every size: sm/leading-normal/Medium at default, xs at sm, base at lg, text/foreground for the label and sm/leading-normal/Normal + text/muted-foreground for the description. Checked across Label, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup and Slider. The duplication is structural only — there is no typographic drift and no drift risk, because the text styles are the single source of truth for type.
group3_notDone.cost: A component property cannot reference text inside a nested instance. Instancing Label would therefore DELETE each host's top-level Label / Description text props and Show label / Show description booleans — the props designers actually use — and the only way back to editing the text would be exposing the nested Label, which also exposes its Size and Disabled and lets them contradict the host's own Size and Disabled variant (a sm checkbox wearing a lg label).
group3_notDone.codeSideNote: Only Slider actually composes <Label> in code. Checkbox, Switch and RadioGroup render .ui-label__* markup themselves, so hand-drawn label rows are arguably the faithful mirror of what the code does.
group3_notDone.ifRevisited: The only version worth building is one where the host keeps its text props and the Label instance is NOT exposed — which Figma cannot express. Revisit only if Figma adds parent-to-nested property mapping.

group2_actionSlots.what: Alert and Banner each gained a 'Show action' BOOLEAN (default false) revealing an exposed outline Button — Alert Small 'Upgrade' vertically centred against a two-line alert, Banner XSmall 'Reload' sitting between the message and the dismiss control.
group2_actionSlots.alertStaysNeutral: Alert's action button is pinned to the Brand collection's Slate mode via setExplicitVariableModeForCollection, which is the Figma equivalent of the --primary-main rule in Alert.scss: inside a themed subtree the alert themes but its action does not. VERIFIED by setting the brand variant to Magenta and screenshotting — title, icon and X went magenta, the button stayed slate. Banner's action is deliberately NOT pinned; it themes, matching Banner.scss.
group2_actionSlots.slotsCannotBeCreated: figma.createSlot does not exist (accessing it THROWS rather than returning undefined — guard every probe of an unknown figma.* property in try/catch). Cloning an existing SLOT reports type SLOT at first but degrades to a plain FRAME once appended into another component, and it carries the source slot's geometry with it — Card's media slot brought a fixed 360x203 box and a solid fill, which rendered as a grey band in Banner and an invisible oversized box in Alert. The action containers are therefore ordinary auto-layout frames holding an EXPOSED Button, which is the better shape here anyway.
group2_actionSlots.hiddenNodeTrap: A second face of the hidden-instance lesson: a hidden node does not RELAYOUT either. Setting layout and sizing on the hidden action container silently did nothing — it stayed 360x203 through two passes. Reveal via editComponentProperty(key, {defaultValue: true}), fix, screenshot, then set it back to false.

devModeAndPublishing.why: A design-system audit found the file's variable layer was invisible to Dev Mode and published its own internals as public API.

codeSyntax.before: 485 of 799 variables had no WEB code syntax. Of the 245 PUBLIC variables, only 129 carried one, so a developer inspecting an Alert in Dev Mode saw 'status/success/base' rather than var(--success).
codeSyntax.after: 209 of 245 public variables carry var(--…) syntax. Written by deterministic name transforms per collection (surface/X and text/X -> --X, status/{s}/base -> --{s}, sidebar/base -> --sidebar, category/{h}/base -> --category-{h}, Brand tint/X -> --X, easing/X -> --ease-X, and so on).
codeSyntax.verifiedNotGuessed: Every written value was exported and diffed against the 498 custom properties actually declared in tokens.scss. 11 name families did NOT exist and were CLEARED rather than left pointing at a token that isn't there: --aiden-base, --aiden-outline-hover-foreground (removed from code 2026-07-28), --band, --chart-line/seq/div-* (deeper-theming Phase B, Figma is ahead of code), and the aiden gradient STOPS (--aiden-primary-1..3 etc, which are components of a gradient, not custom properties). 33 variables cleared.
codeSyntax.remaining: 36 public variables legitimately have no CSS counterpart — the 13 aiden gradient stops, 17 chart-seq/div/line ramps, tint/band + page/band, the two mode flags, and icon/stroke-weight. Do not invent names for these.

publishing.before: 0 of 799 variables and 0 styles were hidden from publishing, so a library consumer saw all 211 raw Primitives (slate/500) and all 343 _brand/{name}/* internals alongside the semantic layer that is supposed to BE the API. CLAUDE.md already states _brand/* is 'the input to the tint derivation, not a second public vocabulary' — Figma was publishing it as one.
publishing.after: 554 internals hidden (211 Primitives + 343 _brand/*). The published surface is now the 245 public variables: the Mode semantics, the Brand public tokens, and the two Tint collections.
publishing.deprecatedStylesDeleted: Aiden/_deprecated/Light/Outline-hover and its Dark twin, for a token the code deleted 2026-07-28. Scanned all 95 pages for fillStyleId/strokeStyleId consumers first — none — then removed. 24 paint styles remain.

foreignLibraries.finding: Three community UI kits are SUBSCRIBED to this file: Material 3 Design Kit, Simple Design System, and iOS 18 and iPadOS 18. Hard rule 1 of the repo is zero third-party UI.

foreignLibraries.cannotBeScripted: The Plugin API has no way to unsubscribe a library — figma.teamLibrary exposes only getAvailableLibraryVariableCollectionsAsync and getVariablesInLibraryCollectionAsync; removeLibrary / unsubscribeLibrary / setLibraries are all undefined. This is an owner action in the Figma UI: Assets panel -> Libraries -> toggle each of the three off.

item4_variantVocabulary.done: All 240 variants across Button and Button/Icon-only renamed to the code vocabulary: Size XSmall|Small|Default|Large -> xs|sm|default|lg, Variant Default|Error|Info|Success|Warning|Aiden -> lowercase, Style Default|Secondary|Outline|Ghost|Link -> lowercase. item4_variantVocabulary.whyItWasSafe: VARIANT property values are not stored on the instance — they are read from the main component's NAME. Renaming the variant components therefore remaps every instance automatically. Verified: 596 Button instances checked afterwards, 0 broken, 0 still carrying a title-case value. A 430-instance snapshot was taken first in case that assumption was wrong.

item5_charts.correctionToTheAudit: The audit said 35 unstyled text nodes. The real number was 170 — the original lint only looked inside main components and skipped the specimen frames.
item5_charts.done: All 170 now carry a text style. item6_buttonMatrix.verdict: NO CHANGE — the finding was a measurement, not a defect. Do not split Button.
item6_buttonMatrix.reasoning: Figma renders one DROPDOWN PER VARIANT PROPERTY, not a flat list, so 120 variants across three orthogonal axes costs the user three dropdowns, exactly what variants are for. Splitting into six sets (one per Variant) would fragment the component in the assets panel, break the identity of 430 instances, and turn a dropdown change into an instance swap. The generic 'cap at 30' guidance targets variant EXPLOSION from non-orthogonal axes; it does not fit this shape.
item6_buttonMatrix.iconOnlySplitIsCorrect: Button/Icon-only exists as a second set rather than a boolean on Button because icon-only changes PADDING (squared, --p-1 at xs and --p-2 elsewhere) and gives aiden --rounded-full. A Figma BOOLEAN can only show and hide layers — it cannot change padding or radius — so the split is forced by the API, not a modelling mistake. The page prose already says so.

newDefectConfirmed_iconOnlyGlyph.what: On Button/Icon-only the glyph renders DARK NAVY on every solid (Style=default) fill — near-invisible on the default variant's dark navy, and low-contrast on error red and success green. Confirmed by screenshotting three masters at 4x, not inferred. The labeled Button is correct: it binds primary-foreground / status/{sem}/foreground / aiden/primary-foreground.
newDefectConfirmed_iconOnlyGlyph.scope: At least 24 variants (6 Variant x 4 Size at Style=default). Whether secondary/outline/ghost/link glyphs are also wrong could not be established by reading — see below.
whyItIsNotTriviallyFixable: Lazy materialisation: an icon instance's subtree is often not built, so findAllWithCriteria returns zero VECTORs for a variant that visibly has a glyph. A read at Size=sm returned bindings for all six variants while the same read at Size=default returned none. Any fix must force materialisation first and verify per variant, never trust a write count.

Swap resets overrides: the glyph is an INSTANCE_SWAP slot, and setting that property discards colour overrides on the swapped instance — proven on the Chat composer send button earlier the same day. So even a perfect binding pass leaves the colour fragile for any consumer who changes the icon. A durable fix needs the icon masters themselves to carry the binding, which Figma has no currentColor equivalent for.
newDefectConfirmed_iconOnlyGlyph.recommendation: Treat as its own task with a materialise-verify-per-variant loop, and decide first whether the durable answer is per-variant binding or a set of pre-coloured icon masters.

rubricCorrection.what: Eight pages were scoring 92 for 'composition' because they hand-draw a sub-part: Checkbox, Switch, Slider, RadioGroup (Label), NativeSelect, Textarea (Input), FullScreenDialog and AidenFullScreen (Dialog chrome).
rubricCorrection.why: The composition dimension exists to catch UNINTENTIONAL duplication. Every one of these is a RECORDED decision with a rationale in this ledger — the Label rows already share Label's text styles and instancing would delete the host's top-level text props, and Dialog's component carries a radius, shadow and max-width that the full-screen surfaces exist to remove. Scoring a documented decision as a defect pushes toward undoing good decisions.

When running this census, separate value-axes (Active, Checked, State=Complete) from interaction-state axes (Disabled, Hover, Focus); a set can have one and still be missing the other.

unboundGeometryFinding.found: Surfaced incidentally while linting after the text renames — NOT introduced by it, and NOT fixed.
unboundGeometryFinding.detail: Unbound padding/radius on Label (8), Chat (83), TabBar (186) and Mark (708 plus 333 unbound paints and 171 unstyled texts). Sampling TabBar showed these are real, not lint false positives: the page frame carries raw 80px padding, the "Composition rows" card raw 32px, and the TabBar/Tab COMPONENT_SET wrapper has cornerRadius 5 with an EMPTY boundVariables — which is precisely the recorded gotcha that "Figma gives every new set a default corner radius of 5 and whatever raw padding you set, both of which the lint flags".
unboundGeometryFinding.implication: Several pages are recorded in this ledger as shipping "lint all-zeros" while carrying these. Either the lint was run before the wrapper bindings mattered, or it was run only over the component set and not the page frames. Worth a file-wide pass, scoped and agreed first.

assetsPanelRule.rule: ONLY COMPONENTS AND COMPONENT SETS APPEAR IN THE ASSETS PANEL. A plain FRAME never does, however it is named or wherever it sits. There is no way to publish a frame to Assets.
assetsPanelRule.implication: The "editable template frame" pattern (Sidebar, Chat, TabBar, Table) buys unlimited extensibility at the cost of ALL Assets-panel discoverability. That trade is right when the list is unbounded and heterogeneous, and wrong when it is a homogeneous list of one atom at a predictable length — there, a locked set with a count variant of EXPOSED instances (the ToggleGroup model) is better, and the two can coexist with the frame as a stated escape hatch.
assetsPanelRule.ask: Before choosing a template frame over a component, ask: is the list unbounded, and is it made of DIFFERENT atoms? Two yeses means a frame. One or none means a component with a count variant.

tier2AssemblySweep.slotApiFinding: figma.createSlot DOES NOT EXIST — reading the property throws rather than returning undefined. The four Body slots were made in the Figma UI. A plugin building a NEW assembly therefore cannot use a slot, and exposed nested instances are the only available mechanism. This is why Pagination and Command/Palette use a count axis + exposure rather than matching the menu families.

foregroundScopeWidening.reportedBy: owner, live: icons default to text/foreground but muted-foreground cannot be selected
foregroundScopeWidening.cause: Lucide glyphs are VECTORs painted by a STROKE, and Figma's colour picker filters variables by scope — a stroke shows only STROKE_COLOR-scoped variables. Every text/* and *-foreground token was scoped TEXT_FILL only, so none appeared. The existing icon bindings were made by the plugin API, WHICH IGNORES SCOPES — scopes gate the human picker only. text/muted-foreground was the most-used icon paint in the file (166 glyph bindings) while being impossible to apply by hand.
foregroundScopeWidening.fix: 50 foreground-family COLOR variables widened to TEXT_FILL + STROKE_COLOR + SHAPE_FILL: text/* (6), primary-foreground/-text, status/*/foreground, tooltip/foreground, sidebar foregrounds, aiden foregrounds, category/*/text + category/foreground, avatar/foreground, and the _brand/* foreground/text ramps. Deliberately NOT FRAME_FILL — a text token as a surface background stays blocked. code/* (11) stays TEXT_FILL-only: syntax colours should never paint an icon.
foregroundScopeWidening.risk: zero rendering change — scopes affect the picker, not resolved paints.

itemSpacingSweep2026_09_07.scope: All 107 pages. Every auto-layout node with a non-zero itemSpacing, including inside COMPONENT and COMPONENT_SET masters, since a master's gaps ARE its spec. Needs an owner call.
itemSpacingSweep2026_09_07.methodLesson: Pages load incrementally, but BOTH reads and writes work on non-current pages when you traverse figma.root.children directly, without setCurrentPageAsync. Proven before relying on it: an unloaded read of the FeaturedIcon page returned 62, byte-identical to its loaded count, and a 3-node write test on App Shell bound and verified. That is what made a 107-page sweep four parallel calls instead of 107 sequential ones. The one-setCurrentPageAsync-per-call rule still governs anything needing a fully resolved subtree, such as the instance census, where instances on unloaded pages read back with no ancestors and no children.

This sweep was itemSpacing only and did not touch them. Note those palette pages contributed almost nothing here, because their swatch grids are absolutely positioned rather than auto-laid-out; the one large non-doc contributor was Chart palettes at 245, all of which bound cleanly.

offScaleResolved.note: Owner asked for the 16 off-scale gaps (12 at 18, 4 at 22) to be moved onto the scale. Done, by measured class convention rather than by rounding, per the rule tier4GeometrySweep set: rounding to the nearest token misstates a spec, matching a measured house convention does not.
offScaleResolved.classesMeasured: Three histograms, taken file-wide before touching anything. (1) SPECIMEN BANDS, frames named 'X - Light' / 'X - Dark': 180 of them, values 24 (62), 20 (16), 48 (16), 14 (16), 32 (10), 56 (10), 16 (8). (2) COMPONENT_SET variant grids: 95 sets, values 16 (37), 24 (18), 32 (10), 20 (9), 28 (6), 40 (5), 48 (5), 12 (4). (3) Nav rows on example pages: Direction 8, Marketing 16, Suite nav 20.
offScaleResolved.decisions: 18 and 22 both sit exactly 2 from a rung in either direction, so distance decides nothing and frequency does. Specimen bands: 18 to 20 (spacing/5) and 22 to 24 (spacing/6), the two commonest band values. The Toggle COMPONENT_SET's own variant grid: 18 to 16 (spacing/4), the plurality across 95 sets. Suite's 'links' row: 18 to 20 (spacing/5), matching the gap of the 'nav' frame it sits inside, so that page becomes internally consistent. apiLessons.modesOrder: A collection's default mode is its FIRST mode and there is no setter, so create the default first (balanced, 1024) and add the others after; the panel order follows.
apiLessons.explicitModes: setExplicitVariableModeForCollection on a frame pins one collection independently of another, which is exactly how data-density and the viewport compose in code; node properties then READ BACK the resolved number, so a specimen grid can be verified without rendering.
apiLessons.scope: GAP is the FLOAT scope that covers both auto-layout gap and padding; the API binds regardless of scope, scope only shapes the picker.
apiLessons.hiddenTab: requestAnimationFrame never fires in a hidden Browser-pane tab, so a verification script that awaits a frame hangs to the 45s timeout; use setTimeout, or keep the pane visible.

slotCorrection2026_09_07.correction: I told the owner twice that the plugin cannot create Figma slots. Wrong. lessons: A failed use_figma script is NOT reliably atomic: after two failed attempts the R1.1 1024 copy had lost its Button and Input instances (the same node types the script had removed from slot placeholders). Build by cloning into the new structure and remove the originals in the final step; recover lost nodes by cloning from a sibling copy.
A slot created from figma.createFrame() with no layoutMode is a plain frame: nothing dropped into it can be FILL. Make every slot an auto-layout container.
A master whose variants HUG cannot pass FILL through to a slot; give the variant a FIXED width axis and set the slot FILL, then instances set to FILL stretch their content.
Hiding a slot via a boolean before looking it up is fine — findAllWithCriteria still returns hidden SLOT nodes — but guard the lookup anyway.
Doc-page root frames have no page padding of their own once PageContainer is inside them; leaving the root's L1 padding doubles the margin (2.1 measured 1008 instead of 1072).
